rcm.1.1.sortha.4.m: Fair as the jasmine and the moon, beloved of Uma, home of compassion, who loves the lowly: may the destroyer of Kama show me grace.
roles: Shows an opening prayer for grace.
rcm.1.1.sortha.4.sa: कुंद इंदु सम देह उमा रमन करुना अयन। जाहि दीन पर नेह करउ कृपा मर्दन मयन ॥

rcm.1.102.chaupai.2.m: 'Can one whose home is beneath the wishing tree suffer the pain of poverty? Thinking this over in your heart, Moon-crowned Lord, take away the heavy confusion of my mind.'
roles: Names her asking plainly of the one who knows.
rcm.1.102.chaupai.2.sa: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥

rcm.1.109.chaupai.5.m: There is no difference between God with form and God without form: so say the sages, the Puranas, the learned and the Vedas. The One without qualities, without form, unseen and unborn, takes on form out of love for his devotees.
roles: Names an honest theological question honoured with an answer.
rcm.1.109.chaupai.5.sa: सगुनहि अगुनहि नहिं कछु भेदा। गावहिं मुनि पुरान बुध बेदा॥ अगुन अरूप अलख अज जोई। भगत प्रेम बस सगुन सो होई ॥

rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.m: Even saying his name helplessly burns away wrongs built up over many lives; and those who remember him with reverence cross the ocean of worldly life as if it were a cow's hoofprint.
rcm.1.112.chaupai.2.sa: बिबसहुँ जासु नाम नर कहहीं। जनम अनेक रचित अघ दहहीं॥ सादर सुमिरन जे नर करहीं। भव बारिधि गोपद इव तरहीं ॥

rcm.1.113.chaupai.1.m: 'Hearing your words, cool as moonbeams, the heavy autumn heat of my delusion is gone. Kind one, you took away all my doubt, and I came to know Ram's true nature.'
roles: Shows she tells her teacher what his words did.
rcm.1.113.chaupai.1.sa: ससि कर सम सुनि गिरा तुम्हारी। मिटा मोह सरदातप भारी॥ तुम्ह कृपाल सबु संसउ हरेऊ। राम स्वरूप जानि मोहि परेऊ ॥

rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.m: Listen, sage: when a sick man in distress begs for food that will harm him, the doctor does not give it. In the same way I have resolved to do what is truly good for you.
roles: Shows a refusal as an act of care.
rcm.1.127.chaupai.1.sa: कुपथ माग रुज ब्याकुल रोगी। बैद न देइ सुनहु मुनि जोगी॥ एहि बिधि हित तुम्हार मैं ठयऊ। कहि अस अंतरहित प्रभु भयऊ ॥

scene.s: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.
scene.t: Narada's pride and the monkey face

rcm.1.135.sortha.1.m: Old age came while he lived at home, yet the pull of pleasures had not faded. His heart grieved deeply that his life had gone by without devotion to Hari.
roles: He grieves over the years already spent.
rcm.1.135.sortha.1.sa: होइ न बिषय बिराग भवन बसत भा चौथपन॥ हृदयँ बहुत दुख लाग जनम गयउ हरिभगति बिनु ॥

rcm.1.141.chaupai.3.m: Like a poor man who finds the wish-fulfilling tree and still hesitates to ask for much, not knowing its power, so doubt rises in my heart.
roles: He feels too small to ask for what he truly wants.
rcm.1.141.chaupai.3.sa: जथा दरिद्र बिबुधतरु पाई। बहु संपति मागत सकुचाई॥ तासु प्रभाउ जान नहिं सोई। तथा हृदयँ मम संसय होई ॥

rcm.1.15.chaupai.2.m: I bow to Mahesh and Bhavani, my teacher, father and mother, friends of the lowly, giving every day; servants, masters and friends of Sita's lord, true well-wishers of Tulsi in every way, without any motive.
roles: He counts those who wish him well for no reason.
rcm.1.15.chaupai.2.sa: गुर पितु मातु महेस भवानी। प्रनवउँ दीनबंधु दिन दानी॥ सेवक स्वामि सखा सिय पी के। हित निरुपधि सब बिधि तुलसी के ॥

rcm.1.153.sortha.1.m: It is not only fools who are taken in by a fine appearance; the clever are too. Look at the beautiful peacock: its voice is like nectar, and it eats snakes.
roles: Shows judging by actions, not looks or sound.
rcm.1.153.sortha.1.sa: तुलसी देखि सुबेषु भूलहिं मूढ़ न चतुर नर। सुंदर केकिहि पेखु बचन सुधा सम असन अहि ॥

rcm.1.180.chhand.4.m: Then the mother spoke, her mind unsettled: 'Child, put away this form. Play as a little child, so dear to the heart; that joy is beyond compare.' Hearing her, the wise Lord began to cry and became a baby. Those who sing this story reach Hari's feet and do not fall into the well of worldly life.
roles: Names the joy of a small child's play.
rcm.1.180.chhand.4.sa: माता पुनि बोली सो मति डोली तजहु तात यह रूपा। कीजै सिसुलीला अति प्रियसीला यह सुख परम अनूपा॥ सुनि बचन सुजाना रोदन ठाना होइ बालक सुरभूपा। यह चरित जे गावहिं हरिपद पावहिं ते न परहिं भवकूपा ॥

rcm.1.186.doha.1.m: The all-pervading, stainless, formless Absolute, beyond all play, the unborn one, lies in Kausalya's lap, won over by love and devotion.
roles: Holds the infinite as a child.
rcm.1.186.doha.1.sa: ब्यापक ब्रह्म निरंजन निर्गुन बिगत बिनोद। सो अज प्रेम भगति बस कौसल्या कें गोद ॥

rcm.1.19.chaupai.3.m: Even a particular form is not recognised without its name, though it sit in the palm of your hand. But remember the name without seeing the form, and a special love rises in the heart.
roles: Cultivates love that rises with the name.
rcm.1.19.chaupai.3.sa: रूप बिसेष नाम बिनु जानें। करतल गत न परहिं पहिचानें॥ सुमिरिअ नाम रूप बिनु देखें। आवत हृदयँ सनेह बिसेषें ॥

rcm.1.19.doha.1.m: Tulsi says: if you want light both inside and outside, place the name of Ram like a jewelled lamp on the threshold of your tongue.
rcm.1.19.doha.1.sa: राम नाम मनिदीप धरु जीह देहरीं द्वार। तुलसी भीतर बाहेरहुँ जौं चाहसि उजिआर ॥

rcm.1.196.chaupai.3.m: All my sons are dear to me as life, and Ram I cannot bring myself to give. Where are those terrible, cruel demons, and where my tender, boyish son?
roles: Depicts him measuring his tender son against terrible demons.
rcm.1.196.chaupai.3.sa: सब सुत प्रिय मोहि प्रान की नाईं। राम देत नहिं बनइ गोसाईं॥ कहँ निसिचर अति घोर कठोरा। कहँ सुंदर सुत परम किसोरा ॥

scene.s: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharath to send the teenage Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest rites from demons. Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, offers land, cows, treasure, even his own life instead. Vasishtha reasons with him, and he finally embraces the boys and hands them over.

rcm.1.247.chaupai.1.m: He saw Vaidehi in deep distress, each moment passing like an age. If a thirsty man dies for want of water, what use is a lake of nectar after he is gone? What use is rain when the crops have dried? What use is regret once the moment has passed? Knowing this, he looked at Janaki, and seeing her deep love, he thrilled.
roles: Shows the closing moment itself becoming the reason to move now.
rcm.1.247.chaupai.1.sa: देखी बिपुल बिकल बैदेही। निमिष बिहात कलप सम तेही। तृषित बारि बिनु जो तनु त्यागा। मुएँ करइ का सुधा तड़ागा ॥ का बरषा सब कृषी सुखानें। समय चुकें पुनि का पछितानें॥ अस जियँ जानि जानकी देखी। प्रभु पुलके लखि प्रीति बिसेषी ॥

rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.m: The name is a wish-fulfilling tree in a terrible time; remembering it stills the whole tangle of the world. In this age the name of Ram gives what the heart rightly wants; it is a well-wisher for this world and the next, a father and a mother.
roles: Taking the name as one's shelter.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.3.sa: नाम कामतरु काल कराला। सुमिरत समन सकल जग जाला॥ राम नाम कलि अभिमत दाता। हित परलोक लोक पितु माता ॥

rcm.1.25.chaupai.4.m: In this age there is no ritual action, no devotion and no discernment left to lean on; the name of Ram is the one support. In the age of Kali, the name is the clever Hanuman against Kalanemi, the master of deceit.
roles: Shows leaning on the name alone.
rcm.1.25.chaupai.4.sa: नहिं कलि करम न भगति बिबेकू। राम नाम अवलंबन एकू॥ कालनेमि कलि कपट निधानू। नाम सुमति समरथ हनुमानू ॥

rcm.1.258.doha.1.m: The truly brave prove themselves by what they do in battle; they do not announce themselves. Cowards, finding an enemy in front of them, talk about their own prowess.
rcm.1.258.doha.1.sa: सूर समर करनी करहिं कहि न जनावहिं आपु। बिद्यमान रन पाइ रिपु कायर कथहिं प्रतापु ॥

scene.s: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
scene.t: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm

rcm.1.26.chaupai.1.m: Said with love or without it, even in irritation or laziness, repeating the name brings good in all ten directions. Remembering that name, I bow my head to Raghunath and begin his story.
roles: Saying the name as one is.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.1.sa: भायँ कुभायँ अनख आलस हूँ। नाम जपत मंगल दिसि दसहूँ॥ सुमिरि सो नाम राम गुन गाथा। करउँ नाइ रघुनाथहि माथा ॥॥

rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.m: He will set right everything about me, he whose kindness never tires of being kind. Ram is a good master and I am a poor servant, yet the ocean of compassion looks at it from his own side and cares for me.
roles: Names trusting the master's nature over one's own record.
rcm.1.26.chaupai.2.sa: मोरि सुधारिहि सो सब भाँती। जासु कृपा नहिं कृपाँ अघाती॥ राम सुस्वामि कुसेवकु मोसो। निज दिसि देखि दयानिधि पोसो ॥

rcm.1.26.doha.1.m: Kind Ram will honour the love and the wish of even a foolish servant, he who made stones into boats and monkeys and bears into wise ministers.
roles: Shows the one who made stones into boats can use me.
rcm.1.26.doha.1.sa: सठ सेवक की प्रीति रुचि रखिहहिं राम कृपालु। उपल किए जलजान जेहिं सचिव सुमति कपि भालु ॥

rcm.1.260.doha.1.m: Seeing Parashurama's fire of anger rise with each of Lakshman's replies, which fell on it like offerings of ghee, Ram, sun of the Raghu line, spoke words like water.
roles: Shows Ram answers rage with water-like words and the fire goes down.
rcm.1.260.doha.1.sa: लखन उतर आहुति सरिस भृगुबर कोपु कृसानु। बढ़त देखि जल सम बचन बोले रघुकुलभानु ॥

rcm.1.261.doha.1.m: Lakshman laughed and said, 'Listen, sage: anger is the root of wrongdoing. In its grip people do what they shouldn't and set themselves against the whole world.'
roles: Heals anger by naming what it makes a person do and whom it turns them against.
rcm.1.261.doha.1.sa: लखन कहेउ हँसि सुनहु मुनि क्रोधु पाप कर मूल। जेहि बस जन अनुचित करहिं चरहिं बिस्व प्रतिकूल ॥

scene.s: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
scene.t: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm

rcm.1.262.chaupai.1.m: Great sage, I am your servant; give up your anger and be kind. A broken bow won't mend because you are angry. You must be tired of standing; do sit down.
roles: Shows anger doing nothing to the loss it is about.
rcm.1.262.chaupai.1.sa: मैं तुम्हार अनुचर मुनिराया। परिहरि कोपु करिअ अब दाया॥ टूट चाप नहिं जुरिहि रिसाने। बैठिअ होइहिं पाय पिराने ॥

scene.s: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
scene.t: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm

rcm.1.27.chaupai.2.m: Hearing, looking and weighing it with care, my Lord praised the devotion in my mind. What is badly said is still good in the heart; Ram is pleased because he knows what his servant means.
roles: Shows being understood by the heart.
rcm.1.27.chaupai.2.sa: सुनि अवलोकि सुचित चख चाही। भगति मोरि मति स्वामि सराही॥ कहत नसाइ होइ हियँ नीकी। रीझत राम जानि जन जी की ॥

rcm.1.27.chaupai.3.m: The Lord does not keep a mistake in his mind; he remembers the heart a hundred times over. The very wrong for which he struck Bali like a hunter, Sugriva later did too.
roles: Shows trust that one is seen by one's intention.
rcm.1.27.chaupai.3.sa: रहति न प्रभु चित चूक किए की। करत सुरति सय बार हिए की॥ जेहिं अघ बधेउ ब्याध जिमि बाली। फिरि सुकंठ सोइ कीन्हि कुचाली ॥

rcm.1.3.chaupai.4.m: Without good company there is no clear judgement, and by Ram's grace alone such company comes easily. Good company is the root of joy and well-being; finding it is the fruit, and every other practice is only the flower.
roles: Shows clear judgement grown among good people, not alone.
rcm.1.3.chaupai.4.sa: बिनु सतसंग बिबेक न होई। राम कृपा बिनु सुलभ न सोई॥ सतसंगत मुद मंगल मूला। सोई फल सिधि सब साधन फूला ॥

rcm.1.3.chaupai.5.m: Even the crooked improve in good company, the way base metal turns to gold at the touch of the philosopher's stone. And if by chance good people fall among bad company, they keep their own nature, like the jewel in a cobra's hood that never takes on its poison.
roles: Keeps one's own quality like the gem on the serpent's hood.
rcm.1.3.chaupai.5.sa: सठ सुधरहिं सतसंगति पाई। पारस परस कुधात सुहाई॥ बिधि बस सुजन कुसंगत परहीं। फनि मनि सम निज गुन अनुसरहीं ॥

rcm.1.318.chaupai.3.m: He was known as supremely detached, yet on seeing Sita his composure fled. The king held Janaki to his heart, and the great banks of his wisdom gave way.
roles: Shows a father famed for calm losing his composure at the parting.
rcm.1.318.chaupai.3.sa: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥

rcm.1.54.chaupai.1.m: Remembering what she had done, her heart was full of a worry beyond telling. 'Shiva, an ocean of compassion, deep beyond measure, did not speak my fault aloud.'
roles: Shows her noticing the mercy of not being shamed aloud.
rcm.1.54.chaupai.1.sa: हृदयँ सोचु समुझत निज करनी। चिंता अमित जाइ नहिं बरनी॥ कृपासिंधु सिव परम अगाधा। प्रगट न कहेउ मोर अपराधा ॥

rcm.1.54.chaupai.2.m: Reading Shiva's manner, Sati knew he had left her in his heart, and she was shaken. Knowing the fault was her own, she could say nothing, but inside her heart burned like a potter's kiln.
roles: Shows the fault is her own and there is nothing she can say.
rcm.1.54.chaupai.2.sa: संकर रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदयँ अकुलानी॥ निज अघ समुझि न कछु कहि जाई। तपइ अवाँ इव उर अधिकाई ॥

rcm.1.54.sortha.1.m: See love's lovely way: water mixed with milk sells at the price of milk. But let the sourness of deceit fall in, and the water separates and the sweetness is gone.
roles: Shows closeness living on nothing being concealed.
rcm.1.54.sortha.1.sa: जलु पय सरिस बिकाइ देखहु प्रीति कि रीति भलि। बिलग होइ रसु जाइ कपट खटाई परत पुनि ॥

rcm.1.58.chaupai.3.m: It is true that one may go uninvited to the home of a friend, a master, a father or a teacher. Yet where someone holds hostility toward you, no good comes of going there.
roles: Names self-respect declining a room that holds contempt.
rcm.1.58.chaupai.3.sa: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥

rcm.1.6.doha.1.m: The Creator made this world, living and lifeless, a mix of virtues and faults. But the wise, like the swan, take the milk of virtue and leave behind the water of faults.
roles: Choose to see what is good in a person.
rcm.1.6.doha.1.sa: जड़ चेतन गुन दोषमय बिस्व कीन्ह करतार। संत हंस गुन गहहिं पय परिहरि बारि बिकार ॥

rcm.1.66.chaupai.2.m: Shambhu is by nature the all-capable Lord; in this marriage there is good of every kind. Mahesh is hard to win by worship, yet he is quickly pleased when one takes on hardship.
roles: Shows hardship taken on for what one wants.
rcm.1.66.chaupai.2.sa: संभु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाहँ सब बिधि कल्याना॥ दुराराध्य पै अहहिं महेसू। आसुतोष पुनि किएँ कलेसू ॥

scene.s: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.

rcm.1.67.doha.1.m: Beloved, put away all this worry and remember the Lord. He who made Parvati will bring about her good.
roles: Shows remembering God in place of fretting.
rcm.1.67.doha.1.sa: प्रिया सोचु परिहरहु सबु सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान। पारबतिहि निरमयउ जेहिं सोइ करिहि कल्यान ॥

scene.s: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.

rcm.1.70.doha.1.m: Daughter of the mountain king, listen: your longing has borne fruit. Now give up all these unbearable hardships; Tripurari will be yours.
rcm.1.70.doha.1.sa: भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव सुनु गिरिराजकुमारि। परिहरु दुसह कलेस सब अब मिलिहहिं त्रिपुरारि ॥

scene.s: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.

rcm.1.72.chaupai.1.m: Somewhere he taught knowledge to sages, somewhere he told of Ram's virtues. Though free of all desire, the wise Lord was pained by separation from his devotee.
roles: Shows him wandering, teaching and singing, carrying her absence.
rcm.1.72.chaupai.1.sa: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥

rcm.1.74.chaupai.3.m: 'My mind has set itself stubbornly and will not hear advice; it wants to build a wall on water. Taking Narada's word as true, I want to fly without wings. Look at my foolishness, sages: I want only Shiva as my husband, always.'
roles: Shows a resolve that hears the advice and stays.
rcm.1.74.chaupai.3.sa: मनु हठ परा न सुनइ सिखावा। चहत बारि पर भीति उठावा॥ नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पंखन्ह हम चहहिं उड़ाना ॥ देखहु मुनि अबिबेकु हमारा। चाहिअ सदा सिवहि भरतारा ॥

rcm.1.76.chaupai.3.m: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
roles: Shows a resolve that does not bargain when tested.
rcm.1.76.chaupai.3.sa: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥

rcm.1.76.doha.1.m: Grant that Mahadev is a house of faults and Vishnu the home of every virtue. Still, the one a heart has settled on is the one it wants.
rcm.1.76.doha.1.sa: महादेव अवगुन भवन बिष्नु सकल गुन धाम। जेहि कर मनु रम जाहि सन तेहि तेही सन काम ॥

rcm.1.8.chaupai.1.m: The eight million four hundred thousand kinds of beings, living in water, on land and in the sky: knowing the whole world to be full of Sita and Ram, I bow to them with folded hands.
rcm.1.8.chaupai.1.sa: आकर चारि लाख चौरासी। जाति जीव जल थल नभ बासी॥ सीय राममय सब जग जानी। करउँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी ॥

rcm.1.8.chaupai.6.m: Who does not like their own poetry, whether it is rich or utterly flat? But people who are delighted by someone else's work are rare in this world.
roles: Shows becoming the rare one who is glad at another's.
rcm.1.8.chaupai.6.sa: निज कबित्त केहि लाग न नीका। सरस होउ अथवा अति फीका॥ जे पर भनिति सुनत हरषाहीं। ते बर पुरुष बहुत जग नाहीं ॥

rcm.1.8.chaupai.7.m: Brother, most people in the world are like ponds and rivers: they swell only when their own waters rise. Rare is the good soul who, like the ocean, surges with joy on seeing another's moon grow full.
roles: The ocean swells at another's full moon.
rcm.1.8.chaupai.7.sa: जग बहु नर सर सरि सम भाई। जे निज बाढ़ि बढ़हि जल पाई॥ सज्जन सकृत सिंधु सम कोई। देखि पूर बिधु बाढ़इ जोई ॥

rcm.2.11.chaupai.3.m: We brothers were born together; we ate, slept and played together as children; ear-piercing, sacred thread and weddings were all celebrated side by side. In this spotless family only this one thing is wrong: that the eldest alone is crowned, leaving his brothers aside. (Tulsidas:) May the Lord's loving regret take the crookedness out of his devotees' hearts.
roles: Gives a joy that wants to be shared.
rcm.2.11.chaupai.3.sa: जनमे एक संग सब भाई। भोजन सयन केलि लरिकाई॥ करनबेध उपबीत बिआहा। संग संग सब भए उछाहा ॥ बिमल बंस यहु अनुचित एकू। बंधु बिहाइ बड़ेहि अभिषेकू॥ प्रभु सप्रेम पछितानि सुहाई। हरउ भगत मन कै कुटिलाई ॥

scene.s: Dasharath, noticing grey hairs, decides to crown Ram heir, and the whole city celebrates. When Vasishtha brings Ram the news, Ram's first thought is not joy but unease: the brothers were born, raised and married together, so why should only the eldest be crowned?
scene.t: Ram's unease on the eve of his crowning

rcm.2.127.doha.1.m: One who never wants anything from you and simply loves you: live in that mind always; it is your own home.
rcm.2.127.doha.1.sa: जाहि न चाहिअ कबहुँ कछु तुम्ह सन सहज सनेहु। बसहु निरंतर तासु मन सो राउर निज गेहु ॥

rcm.2.146.chaupai.3.m: Birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love: these come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad; the steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.
roles: Shows patience taken up through discernment.
rcm.2.146.chaupai.3.sa: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥ सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥

scene.s: Sumantra returns alone to the grieving king Dasharath and steadies him.

rcm.2.159.chaupai.3.m: My child, bless you, hold on to courage even now. Seeing that the times are bad, set aside your grief. Knowing that the course of time and karma cannot be turned, don't take this loss as your shame.
rcm.2.159.chaupai.3.sa: अजहुँ बच्छ बलि धीरज धरहू। कुसमउ समुझि सोक परिहरहू॥ जनि मानहु हियँ हानि गलानी। काल करम गति अघटित जानी ॥

rcm.2.163.doha.1.m: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
roles: Shows courage held in the heart while the hands work.
rcm.2.163.doha.1.sa: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥

rcm.2.165.chaupai.4.m: As he spoke of Ram's goodness, gentleness and nature, the great sage's eyes filled with tears and he trembled. Then, praising the love of Lakshman and Sita, the wise sage was lost in sorrow and affection.
roles: Shows the family's teacher unable to keep his voice steady.
rcm.2.165.chaupai.4.sa: कहत राम गुन सील सुभाऊ। सजल नयन पुलकेउ मुनिराऊ॥ बहुरि लखन सिय प्रीति बखानी। सोक सनेह मगन मुनि ग्यानी ॥

rcm.2.170.chaupai.7.m: You give me simple advice, the kind that would do me good if I followed it. Though I understand it well, my heart is not at peace.
roles: Shows an elder's sound advice pointing one way and his heart the other.
rcm.2.170.chaupai.7.sa: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥

rcm.2.176.chaupai.2.m: Though I am at fault and guilty, and all this trouble came about because of me, still, seeing me come before him for refuge, Ram will forgive everything and show me special kindness.
roles: Shows him trusting the other's heart more than his own record.
rcm.2.176.chaupai.2.sa: जद्यपि मैं अनभल अपराधी। भै मोहि कारन सकल उपाधी॥ तदपि सरन सनमुख मोहि देखी। छमि सब करिहहिं कृपा बिसेषी ॥

scene.s: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.

rcm.2.185.chaupai.4.m: Guha said, 'The old man speaks well. Fools act in haste and repent. To fight without knowing Bharat's character and nature would do great harm to our own good.'
roles: Shows him stopping, listening to an elder, checking first.
rcm.2.185.chaupai.4.sa: सुनि गुह कहइ नीक कह बूढ़ा। सहसा करि पछिताहिं बिमूढ़ा॥ भरत सुभाउ सीलु बिनु बूझें। बड़ि हित हानि जानि बिनु जूझें ॥

rcm.2.196.doha.1.m: I have no taste for wealth, duty or pleasure, nor do I seek liberation. Birth after birth, love for Ram's feet: that is the boon, and no other.
roles: Love for Ram asked as the only boon.
rcm.2.196.doha.1.sa: अरथ न धरम न काम रुचि गति न चहउँ निरबान। जनम-जनम रति राम पद यह बरदानु न आन ॥

rcm.2.197.chaupai.4.m: Child Bharat, you are good in every way; your love for Ram's feet is boundless. You torment yourself with guilt for nothing; no one is dearer to Ram than you.
roles: Shows no one is dearer to the one he fears he hurt.
rcm.2.197.chaupai.4.sa: तात भरत तुम्ह सब बिधि साधू। राम चरन अनुराग अगाधू॥ बादि गलानि करहु मन माहीं। तुम्ह सम रामहि कोउ प्रिय नाहीं ॥

scene.s: Bharat is consumed by shame over the exile; the holy rivers answer him.

rcm.2.198.doha.1.m: Don't eat yourself up with shame remembering your mother's deed. Child, Kaikeyi is not at fault either; the goddess of speech clouded her mind.
rcm.2.198.doha.1.sa: तुम्ह गलानि जियँ जनि करहु समुझि मातु करतूति। तात कैकइहि दोसु नहिं गई गिरा मति धूति ॥

scene.s: At Prayag Bharat meets the sage Bharadwaj, too ashamed to speak. The sage tells him not to eat himself up over his mother's deed and that what Bharat sees as a stain is a lesson for everyone. Bharat answers that he fears neither the world's talk nor the afterlife; only the thought that Ram suffers because of him keeps him awake.

rcm.2.204.chaupai.4.m: Hearing Bharat's words the sage was happy, and everyone praised him in many ways. 'Child, don't worry so much. All your sorrow will lift when you see Ram's feet.'
roles: Names trust in what awaits at the end of the road.
rcm.2.204.chaupai.4.sa: भरत बचन सुनि मुनि सुखु पाई। सबहिं कीन्हि बहु भाँति बड़ाई॥ तात करहु जनि सोचु बिसेषी। सब दुखु मिटिहि राम पग देखी ॥

scene.s: On his way to find Ram, Bharat confides his grief and guilt to the sage Bharadwaj.

rcm.2.211.chaupai.2.m: Though Ram is impartial, without attachment or anger, and does not take on anyone's sin, merit, virtue or fault, he has made action the governing law of the world: whatever one does, one tastes the fruit of it.
rcm.2.211.chaupai.2.sa: जद्यपि सम नहिं राग न रोषू। गहहिं न पाप पूनु गुन दोषू॥ करम प्रधान बिस्व करि राखा। जो जस करइ सो तस फलु चाखा ॥

rcm.2.212.chaupai.1.m: The Lord is true to his word and kind to the gods, and Bharat follows Ram's wishes. You are anxious for nothing, gripped by self-interest. The fault is not Bharat's; it is your own confusion.
rcm.2.212.chaupai.1.sa: सत्यसंध प्रभु सुर हितकारी। भरत राम आयस अनुसारी॥ स्वारथ बिबस बिकल तुम्ह होहू। भरत दोसु नहिं राउर मोहू ॥

scene.s: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.

rcm.2.222.chaupai.2.m: Whatever needs doing, right or wrong, think it through first, then act; everyone calls that good. Those who act in haste and regret afterward, the wise say, are not wise at all.
rcm.2.222.chaupai.2.sa: अनुचित उचित काजु किछु होऊ। समुझि करिअ भल कह सबु कोऊ। सहसा करि पाछे पछिताहीं। कहहिं बेद बुध ते बुध नाहीं ॥

rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.m: Whether he casts me off, knowing my mind to be soiled, or honours me as his servant, my refuge is Ram's sandals. Ram is a good master; the fault is all his servant's.
roles: Names refuge that does not depend on the answer.
rcm.2.225.chaupai.1.sa: जौं परिहरहिं मलिन मनु जानी। जौं सनमानहिं सेवकु मानी॥ मोरें सरन रामहि की पनही। राम सुस्वामि दोसु सब जनही ॥

scene.s: Bharat walks toward Ram at Chitrakoot, afraid of being rejected.

rcm.2.225.chaupai.3.m: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.
roles: Shows devotion carrying him like a patient ox.
rcm.2.225.chaupai.3.sa: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥

rcm.2.23.chaupai.2.m: Her words were soft to hear but harsh in their outcome, as if she were giving poison dissolved in honey. The maid said, 'Mistress, do you remember the story you once told me?'
roles: Shows tasting for the poison under the honey.
rcm.2.23.chaupai.2.sa: सुनत बात मृदु अंत कठोरी। देति मनहुँ मधु माहुर घोरी॥ कहइ चेरि सुधि अहइ कि नाहीं। स्वामिनि कहिहु कथा मोहि पाहीं ॥

rcm.2.235.chaupai.1.m: The all-knowing, compassionate Lord understood all the people in distress. Whatever each one was longing for, in that very way he met them.
roles: Shows meeting people as they need, not all alike.
rcm.2.235.chaupai.1.sa: आरत लोग राम सबु जाना। करुनाकर सुजान भगवाना॥ जो जेहि भायँ रहा अभिलाषी। तेहि तेहि कै तसि तसि रुख राखी ॥

rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.m: Ram met Kaikeyi first of all, and with his simple nature and devotion soothed her mind. Falling at her feet, he laid the blame on time, karma and fate, and comforted her. Then he met all the mothers and comforted each: 'Mother, the world is in God's hands; we should blame no one.'
roles: Shows he sees her shame and eases it.
rcm.2.235.chaupai.4.sa: प्रथम राम भेंटी कैकेई। सरल सुभायँ भगति मति भेई॥ पग परि कीन्ह प्रबोधु बहोरी। काल करम बिधि सिर धरि खोरी ॥ भेटीं रघुबर मातु सब करि प्रबोधु परितोषु। अंब ईस आधीन जगु काहु न देइअ दोषु ॥

scene.s: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.

rcm.2.247.chaupai.1.m: People in distress never speak after weighing things; a gambler sees only his own throw. Hearing the sage, Raghunath said, 'Master, the way forward is in your hands.'
roles: Shows knowing when one's own judgement is not to be trusted.
rcm.2.247.chaupai.1.sa: आरत कहहिं बिचारि न काऊ। सूझ जुआरिहि आपन दाऊ॥ सुनि मुनि बचन कहत रघुराऊ॥ नाथ तुम्हारेहि हाथ उपाऊ ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

rcm.2.249.chaupai.4.m: Since childhood I never left his side, and he never once broke my heart. I have seen the way of his kindness: even when I lost at games, he made me win.
roles: Shows remembering one specific kindness of an elder.
rcm.2.249.chaupai.4.sa: सिसुपन तें परिहरेउँ न संगू। कबहुँ न कीन्ह मोर मन भंगू॥ मैं प्रभु कृपा रीति जियँ जोही। हारेहूँ खेल जितावहिं मोही ॥

rcm.2.252.chaupai.3.m: Brother, you torment your heart with shame for nothing; know that a soul's course is in God's hands. In my view, all the virtuous of past, present and future, in all three worlds, stand below you.
roles: Names him told plainly where he stands in his brother's eyes.
rcm.2.252.chaupai.3.sa: तात जायँ जियँ करहु गलानी। ईस अधीन जीव गति जानी॥ तीनि काल तिभुअन मत मोरें। पुन्यसिलोक तात तर तोरें ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

rcm.2.253.chaupai.1.m: "I tell you truly, with Shiva as witness: the earth stays safe because you hold it. Don't torment yourself with needless doubts, brother. Hostility and love cannot be hidden, however you try."
roles: Shows circling arguments against himself named as kutarka.
rcm.2.253.chaupai.1.sa: कहउँ सुभाउ सत्य सिव साखी। भरत भूमि रह राउरि राखी॥ तात कुतरक करहु जनि जाएँ। बैर पेम नहिं दुरइ दुराएँ ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

rcm.2.256.chaupai.2.m: "I was afraid of imagined fears; my worry had no root at all. If one loses one's direction, the sun is not to blame. It was my misfortune, my mother's crookedness, the hard turn of fate and the difficulty of the times..."
roles: Shows him looking back and seeing he lived in a fear of his own making.
rcm.2.256.chaupai.2.sa: अपडर डरेउँ न सोच समूलें। रबिहि न दोसु देव दिसि भूलें॥ मोर अभागु मातु कुटिलाई। बिधि गति बिषम काल कठिनाई ॥

scene.s: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

rcm.2.271.chaupai.3.m: I have always known Bharat to be the lamp of our family; the king told me so again and again. Gold is known on the touchstone and a gem when a jeweller comes; a person is tested by time and shows his nature.
roles: Treats being tested as assay not punishment.
rcm.2.271.chaupai.3.sa: जानउँ सदा भरत कुलदीपा। बार बार मोहि कहेउ महीपा॥ कसें कनकु मनि पारिखि पाएँ। पुरुष परिखिअहिं समयँ सुभाएँ ॥

rcm.2.280.chaupai.4.m: The Vedas, scriptures and Puranas say, and the world knows, that the duty of service is hard. Duty to one's master and self-interest pull against each other; hatred is blind, and love has no judgement.
rcm.2.280.chaupai.4.sa: आगम निगम प्रसिद्ध पुराना। सेवाधरमु कठिन जगु जाना॥ स्वामि धरम स्वारथहि बिरोधू। बैरु अंध प्रेमहि न प्रबोधू ॥

rcm.2.281.chaupai.1.m: Hearing Bharat's words and seeing his nature, Janaka and his court praised him. His words were easy yet deep, gentle yet firm: few in syllables, boundless in meaning.
roles: Shows being gentle and firm in the same breath.
rcm.2.281.chaupai.1.sa: भरत बचन सुनि देखि सुभाऊ। सहित समाज सराहत राऊ॥ सुगम अगम मृदु मंजु कठोरे। अरथु अमित अति आखर थोरे ॥

scene.s: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.

rcm.2.285.chaupai.1.m: Lord, you are father, mother, friend, teacher and master, worthy of worship, my highest good, knower of my heart; a simple, gentle master, a treasure of good nature, protector of those who bow, all-knowing and wise; mighty, a friend to those who seek refuge, one who values merits and removes faults and sins. There is no master like my master, and, I swear by my master, no one like me.
roles: He lists what he has in Ram.
rcm.2.285.chaupai.1.sa: प्रभु पितु मातु सुहृद गुर स्वामी। पूज्य परम हित अंतरजामी॥ सरल सुसाहिबु सील निधानू। प्रनतपाल सर्बग्य सुजानू ॥ समरथ सरनागत हितकारी। गुनगाहकु अवगुन अघ हारी॥ स्वामि गोसाँइहि सरिस गोसाईं। मोहि समान मैं साइँ दोहाईं ॥

rcm.2.285.doha.1.m: Lord, by your own kindness and goodness you have done me good: my faults became like ornaments, and a good name has spread all around me.
roles: Credits the change to Ram's goodness, not his own.
rcm.2.285.doha.1.sa: कृपाँ भलाईं आपनी नाथ कीन्ह भल मोर। दूषन भे भूषन सरिस सुजसु चारु चहुँ ओर ॥

rcm.2.286.chaupai.2.m: Even such people, hearing of you, came before you for shelter, and with a single bow you made them your own. You saw their faults but never kept them in your heart; you heard their virtues and praised them among the good.
rcm.2.286.chaupai.2.sa: तेउ सुनि सरन सामुहें आए। सकृत प्रनामु किहें अपनाए॥ देखि दोष कबहुँ न उर आने। सुनि गुन साधु समाज बखाने ॥

rcm.2.287.chaupai.1.m: Whether out of grief, love or childishness, I came here against your will. Even then, kind one, you looked at it from your own side and took everything I did as good.
roles: Shows Ram thanking for generous reading.
rcm.2.287.chaupai.1.sa: सोक सनेहँ कि बाल सुभाएँ। आयउँ लाइ रजायसु बाएँ॥ तबहुँ कृपाल हेरि निज ओरा। सबहि भाँति भल मानेउ मोरा ॥

rcm.2.290.doha.1.m: Brother, in deed, word and mind you are spotless; the only one like you is you. But how can I praise a younger brother's goodness in front of our elders, at a hard time like this?
roles: Shows him being told there is no one like him.
rcm.2.290.doha.1.sa: करम बचन मानस बिमल तुम्ह समान तुम्ह तात। गुर समाज लघु बंधु गुन कुसमयँ किमि कहि जात ॥

scene.s: Bharat blames himself for his mother's scheme; Ram answers him in front of the elders.

rcm.2.292.chaupai.4.m: Knowing you are gentle, I still say something hard; in hard times, brother, it isn't wrong of me. In bad times it is good brothers who help; it is the hands that rise to block a thunderbolt.
roles: Shows a gentle person is asked to carry something heavy.
rcm.2.292.chaupai.4.sa: जानि तुम्हहि मृदु कहउँ कठोरा। कुसमयँ तात न अनुचित मोरा॥ होहिं कुठायँ सुबंधु सहाए। ओड़िअहिं हाथ असनिहु के धाए ॥

rcm.2.293.chaupai.4.m: Now, gracious one, whatever you command I will do, holding it on my head with respect. But give me something to lean on, Lord, something I can serve, so that I can get through these years.
roles: He asks for something to hold and serve so that he can last.
rcm.2.293.chaupai.4.sa: अब कृपाल जस आयसु होई। करौं सीस धरि सादर सोई॥ सो अवलंब देव मोहि देई। अवधि पारु पावौं जेहि सेई ॥

rcm.2.301.doha.1.m: A leader should be like the mouth: it alone eats and drinks, yet with good sense it nourishes and sustains every limb of the body.
rcm.2.301.doha.1.sa: मुखिआ मुखु सो चाहिऐ खान पान कहुँ एक। पालइ पोषइ सकल अँग तुलसी सहित बिबेक ॥

rcm.2.310.chaupai.4.m: Bharat lives in that city without attachment, like a bee in a champak garden. Fortunate lovers of Ram turn from the luxuries of wealth as one turns from vomit.
roles: Love of Ram leaves no appetite for luxury.
rcm.2.310.chaupai.4.sa: तेहिं पुर बसत भरत बिनु रागा। चंचरीक जिमि चंपक बागा॥ रमा बिलासु राम अनुरागी। तजत बमन जिमि जन बड़भागी ॥

rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.m: ...and Bharat, dear to me as life, will have the kingdom. Fate is favouring me in every way today. If I would not go to the forest even for such a cause, count me first among fools.
rcm.2.42.chaupai.1.sa: भरतु प्रानप्रिय पावहिं राजू। बिधि सब बिधि मोहि सनमुख आजू॥ जौं न जाउँ बन ऐसेहु काजा। प्रथम गनिअ मोहि मूढ़ समाजा ॥

scene.s: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
scene.t: Ram hears he is to be exiled

rcm.2.42.doha.1.m: Raghuvar's words were simple by nature, but the ill-minded queen took them as crooked, as a leech moves crookedly even through still, even water.
roles: Shows not needing to keep re-examining honest words.
rcm.2.42.doha.1.sa: सहज सकल रघुबर बचन कुमति कुटिल करि जान। चलइ जोंक जल बक्रगति जद्यपि सलिलु समान ॥

rcm.2.50.doha.1.m: Raghuvir's mind was like a newly captured elephant, and the crown like the post it is tethered to. Hearing he must go to the forest, he felt himself set free, and joy rose in his heart.
roles: Joy rises where grief was expected.
rcm.2.50.doha.1.sa: नव गयंदु रघुबीर मनु राजु अलान समान। छूट जानि बन गवनु सुनि उर अनंदु अधिकान ॥

scene.s: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
scene.t: Ram hears he is to be exiled

rcm.2.54.chaupai.2.m: Duty and love together hemmed in her mind; she was like the snake that has seized a muskrat. 'If I insist and keep my son, duty is lost and the brothers fall out...'
roles: Shows a choice costing her something she cannot give up.
rcm.2.54.chaupai.2.sa: धरम सनेह उभयँ मति घेरी। भइ गति साँप छुछुंदरि केरी॥ राखउँ सुतहि करउँ अनुरोधू। धरमु जाइ अरु बंधु बिरोधू ॥

rcm.2.55.doha.1.m: Thinking this over, I will not insist out of false affection. I bless you, son; only keep the bond of a mother, and don't forget me.
rcm.2.55.doha.1.sa: यह बिचारि नहिं करउँ हठ झूठ सनेहु बढ़ाइ। मानि मातु कर नात बलि सुरति बिसरि जनि जाइ ॥

rcm.2.56.chaupai.1.m: May all the gods and ancestors guard you, my lord, the way eyelids guard the eyes. The term of your exile is the water, and your loved ones are the fish in it; you are kind and steadfast in what is right.
roles: Shows love turned into blessing when it cannot protect.
rcm.2.56.chaupai.1.sa: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥

rcm.2.67.chaupai.4.m: O Fate, will my fortune ever turn again? Will I see this lovely pair with my own eyes once more? Son, when will that good day, that blessed hour come, when your mother, still alive, sees your moon-like face again?
roles: Shows she fears she may not be alive at the return.
rcm.2.67.chaupai.4.sa: फिरिहि दसा बिधि बहुरि कि मोरी। देखिहउँ नयन मनोहर जोरी। सुदिन सुघरी तात कब होइहि। जननी जिअत बदन बिधु जोइहि ॥

rcm.2.73.chaupai.2.m: Ayodhya is wherever Ram lives; day is wherever the sun shines. If Sita and Ram really go to the forest, you have nothing to do in Ayodhya.
roles: She sends her son to serve.
rcm.2.73.chaupai.2.sa: अवध तहाँ जहँ राम निवासू। तहँइँ दिवसु जहँ भानु प्रकासू॥ जौं पै सीय रामु बन जाहीं। अवध तुम्हार काजु कछु नाहीं ॥

rcm.2.74.chaupai.3.m: Never, even in a dream, fall under the sway of attachment, anger, envy, pride or delusion. Leaving every such distortion behind, serve Sita and Ram with mind, word and deed.
roles: Gives service with mind, action and speech.
rcm.2.74.chaupai.3.sa: रागु रोषु इरिषा मदु मोहू। जनि सपनेहुँ इन्ह के बस होहू॥ सकल प्रकार बिकार बिहाई। मन क्रम बचन करेहु सेवकाई ॥

rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.m: Then Lakshman spoke in a sweet, gentle voice, steeped in knowledge, detachment and devotion: "No one is the giver of another's joy or sorrow, brother. Everyone lives out the fruit of their own actions."
roles: Shows joy and sorrow traced to one source.
rcm.2.90.chaupai.2.sa: बोले लखन मधुर मृदु बानी। ग्यान बिराग भगति रस सानी॥ काहु न कोउ सुख दुख कर दाता। निज कृत करम भोग सबु भ्राता ॥

scene.s: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
scene.t: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram

rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.m: Thinking this through, do not give way to anger, and do not blame anyone without reason. Everyone is asleep in the night of delusion, and in sleep they see dreams of many kinds.
roles: Shows the world's play seen as dream.
rcm.2.91.chaupai.1.sa: अस बिचारि नहिं कीजिअ रोसू। काहुहि बादि न देइअ दोसू॥ मोह निसाँ सबु सोवनिहारा। देखिअ सपन अनेक प्रकारा ॥

scene.s: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
scene.t: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram

rcm.2.93.chaupai.3.m: "The scriptures all say there is no duty equal to truth. I have found that duty easily within my reach. If I abandon it, disgrace will spread through all three worlds."
roles: Shows he holds to the vow against a loving plea.
rcm.2.93.chaupai.3.sa: धरमु न दूसर सत्य समाना। आगम निगम पुरान बखाना॥ मैं सोइ धरमु सुलभ करि पावा। तजें तिहूँ पुर अपजसु छावा ॥

rcm.2.99.chaupai.3.m: Lord, what have I not received today? The fire of my faults, sorrows and poverty is put out. I have worked for wages a long time; today Providence has paid me fully and well.
rcm.2.99.chaupai.3.sa: नाथ आजु मैं काह न पावा। मिटे दोष दुख दारिद दावा॥ बहुत काल मैं कीन्हि मजूरी। आजु दीन्ह बिधि बनि भलि भूरी ॥

rcm.3.13.chaupai.6.m: Singing of my qualities, the body thrills, the voice chokes, tears flow from the eyes; in whom there is no lust, pride or pretence: in their power, brother, I live always.
roles: Shows tears of love while singing.
rcm.3.13.chaupai.6.sa: मम गुन गावत पुलक सरीरा। गदगद गिरा नयन बह नीरा॥ काम आदि मद दंभ न जाकें। तात निरंतर बस मैं ताकें ॥

rcm.3.13.doha.1.m: Those for whom I am the goal in word, deed and mind, who worship without wanting anything: in the lotus of their heart I rest always.
roles: Shows the heart as his resting place.
rcm.3.13.doha.1.sa: बचन कर्म मन मोरि गति भजनु करहिं निःकाम। तिन्ह के हृदय कमल महुँ करउँ सदा बिश्राम ॥

rcm.3.2.sortha.1.m: Though out of delusion he had done harm, and punishment would have been just, the Lord let him go out of tenderness. Who is as kind as Raghubir?
roles: Shows mercy given where punishment was just.
rcm.3.2.sortha.1.sa: कीन्ह मोह बस द्रोह जद्यपि तेहि कर बध उचित। प्रभु छाड़ेउ करि छोह को कृपाल रघुबीर सम ॥

scene.s: Indra's son, disguised as a crow, pecks Sita's foot to test Ram's power. Ram's straw arrow chases him through every world; no god will shelter him. Narada sends him back to Ram, where he falls at his feet admitting he reaped what he sowed. Ram lets him go with the loss of one eye.
scene.t: Jayant the crow: shelter for the offender

rcm.3.26.doha.1.m: Raghubir, the ocean of kindness, touched his head with his lotus hand. Gazing at Ram's face, the home of beauty, all his pain was gone.
roles: Names the hand laid on the head of the dying.
rcm.3.26.doha.1.sa: कर सरोज सिर परसेउ कृपासिंधु रघुबीर। निरखि राम छबि धाम मुख बिगत भई सब पीर ॥

rcm.3.27.chaupai.5.m: "For those whose minds are ruled by the good of others, nothing in the world is out of reach. Leave this body, friend, and go to my abode; what can I give you, who already have everything?"
roles: Shows the good of others ruling the mind.
rcm.3.27.chaupai.5.sa: परहित बस जिन्ह के मन माहीं। तिन्ह कहुँ जग दुर्लभ कछु नाहीं॥ तनु तिज तात जाहु मम धामा। देउँ काह तुम्ह पूरनकामा ॥

scene.s: Ram returns to an empty hut and searches the forest, asking birds and trees if they have seen Sita. He finds the old vulture Jatayu dying; he had fought Ravana alone to stop the abduction. Ram tells him that for one whose heart is set on others' good, nothing is out of reach, and performs his funeral rites himself, as a son would.
scene.t: Jatayu's last fight and Ram's grief

rcm.3.29.chaupai.1.m: Raghunath is tender-hearted, kind to the lowly, gracious without needing a reason. To a vulture, a lowly bird that ate flesh, he gave the end that yogis beg for.
rcm.3.29.chaupai.1.sa: कोमल चित अति दीनदयाला। कारन बिनु रघुनाथ कृपाला॥ गीध अधम खग आमिष भोगी। गति दीन्ही जो जाचत जोगी ॥

rcm.3.32.chaupai.2.m: The seventh is to see the whole world as filled with me, and to regard good people as greater than me. The eighth is to be content with whatever comes, and never, even in a dream, to look for faults in others.
rcm.3.32.chaupai.2.sa: सातवँ सम मोहि मय जग देखा। मोतें संत अधिक करि लेखा॥ आठवँ जथालाभ संतोषा। सपनेहुँ नहिं देखइ परदोषा ॥

rcm.3.32.chaupai.3.m: The ninth is to be simple and free of guile with everyone, to keep trust in me in your heart, and to be neither elated nor downcast. Whoever has even one of these nine, man or woman or any creature at all...
rcm.3.32.chaupai.3.sa: नवम सरल सब सन छलहीना। मम भरोस हियँ हरष न दीना॥ नव महुँ एकउ जिन्ह कें होई। नारि पुरुष सचराचर कोई ॥

rcm.3.32.chaupai.4.m: ...that one is most dear to me, good lady; and in you every kind of devotion is firm. The state that is hard even for yogis has today become easy for you.
roles: Shows devotion firm in every form.
rcm.3.32.chaupai.4.sa: सोइ अतिसय प्रिय भामिनि मोरें। सकल प्रकार भगति दृढ़ तोरें॥ जोगि बृंद दुरलभ गति जोई। तो कहुँ आजु सुलभ भइ सोई ॥

rcm.3.34.doha.1.m: Brother, three enemies are exceedingly strong: desire, anger and greed. In an instant they unsettle even the minds of sages who are homes of wisdom.
roles: Shows even sages are shaken, so being shaken is no disgrace.
rcm.3.34.doha.1.sa: तात तीनि अति प्रबल खल काम क्रोध अरु लोभ। मुनि बिग्यान धाम मन करहिं निमिष महुँ छोभ ॥

rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.m: Uma, I tell you my own experience: worship of Hari is real, and the whole world is a dream.
roles: Shows devotion named as the one real thing.
rcm.3.35.chaupai.3.sa: उमा कहउँ मैं अनुभव अपना। सत हरि भजनु जगत सब सपना॥ पुनि प्रभु गए सरोबर तीरा। पंपा नाम सुभग गंभीरा ॥

rcm.3.38.chaupai.2.m: 'You know my nature, sage: do I ever hide anything from my own? What thing is so dear to me that you could not ask for it? There is nothing I would withhold from my own; never let go of this trust.' Then Narada, delighted, said: 'I will be bold and ask this boon.'
roles: Shows a trust he asks his devotee never to drop.
rcm.3.38.chaupai.2.sa: जानहु मुनि तुम्ह मोर सुभाऊ। जन सन कबहुँ कि करऊँ दुराऊ॥ कवन बस्तु असि प्रिय मोहि लागी। जो मुनिबर न सकहुँ तुम्ह मागी ॥ जन कहुँ कछु अदेय नहिं मोरें। अस बिस्वास तजहु जनि भोरें॥ तब नारद बोले हरषाई। अस बर मागउँ करउँ ढिठाई ॥

scene.s: Narada hesitates to ask Ram for a boon.

rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.m: 'When I wanted to marry, Lord, why did you not let me?' 'Listen, sage, I tell you gladly: those who worship me, giving up every other reliance, I always guard, as a mother guards her child. When the little child runs to grab fire or a snake, the mother pulls it back.'
rcm.3.39.chaupai.2.sa: तब बिबाह मैं चाहउँ कीन्हा। प्रभु केहि कारन करै न दीन्हा॥ सुनु मुनि तोहि कहउँ सहरोसा। भजहिं जे मोहि तजि सकल भरोसा ॥ करउँ सदा तिन्ह कै रखवारी। जिमि बालक राखइ महतारी॥ गह सिसु बच्छ अनल अहि धाई। तहँ राखइ जननी अरगाई ॥

scene.s: Narada asks why Ram stopped his marriage; Ram explains how he guards those who rely on him.

rcm.3.39.chaupai.4.m: When the son is grown, the mother loves him but no longer as before. The wise are like my grown sons; the humble servant is like my little child. My servant has my strength; the wise one relies on his own. Both face the enemies of desire and anger. Knowing this, the wise worship me, and even after gaining knowledge they do not give up devotion.
roles: Shows leaning on the Lord's strength.
rcm.3.39.chaupai.4.sa: प्रौढ़ भएँ तेहि सुत पर माता। प्रीति करइ नहिं पाछिलि बाता॥ मोरें प्रौढ़ तनय सम ग्यानी। बालक सुत सम दास अमानी ॥ जनहि मोर बल निज बल ताही। दुहु कहँ काम क्रोध रिपु आही॥ यह बिचारि पंडित मोहि भजहीं। पाएहुँ ग्यान भगति नहिं तजहीं ॥

rcm.3.42.chaupai.1.m: They shrink when they hear their own praises and are delighted to hear the praises of others. They are even-tempered and calm, never abandon what is right, are simple by nature and kind to all.
roles: Shows affection toward everyone as one's nature.
rcm.3.42.chaupai.1.sa: निज गुन श्रवन सुनत सकुचाहीं। पर गुन सुनत अधिक हरषाहीं॥ सम सीतल नहिं त्यागहिं नीती। सरल सुभाउ सबहि सन प्रीति ॥

rcm.3.7.chaupai.3.m: 'Will Ram, my master, with his brother, meet me as he would his own servant? There is no firm trust in my heart; no devotion, detachment or wisdom in my mind; no good company, no yoga, chanting or sacrifice, no steady love for his lotus feet. But the ocean of compassion has one habit: the one who has no other refuge is dear to him.'
roles: He runs to meet Ram anyway.
rcm.3.7.chaupai.3.sa: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥

rcm.3.7.chaupai.7.m: The sage had found unbroken loving devotion; the Lord watched him, hidden behind a tree. Seeing his overflowing love, Raghubir, who removes the fears of the world, appeared in his heart.
roles: Shows love so full that he forgets the road.
rcm.3.7.chaupai.7.sa: अबिरल प्रेम भगति मुनि पाई। प्रभु देखैं तरु ओट लुकाई॥ अतिसय प्रीति देखि रघुबीरा। प्रगटे हृदयँ हरन भव भीरा ॥

rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.m: Seeing Tara distraught, Raghunath gave her wisdom and took away her delusion: 'This body is made of five elements, earth, water, fire, sky and air, and it is a lowly thing. That body lies here before you, asleep; the self is eternal. For whom are you weeping?' When understanding dawned, she bowed at his feet and asked for the gift of devotion.
rcm.4.12.chaupai.2.sa: तारा बिकल देखि रघुराया। दीन्ह ग्यान हरि लीन्ही माया॥ छिति जल पावक गगन समीरा। पंच रचित अति अधम सरीरा ॥ प्रगट सो तनु तव आगे सोवा। जीव नित्य केहि लगि तुम्ह रोवा॥ उपजा ग्यान चरन तब लागी। लीन्हेसि परम भगति बर मागी ॥

scene.s: After Bali's death his wife Tara weeps over his body. Ram speaks to her gently: the body is made of five elements and lies here before her, but the self is not only this body; for whom is she weeping? Comforted, she asks for devotion, and Bali's son Angad is made heir.

rcm.4.15.chaupai.2.m: The clouds hang low as they rain, the way the wise bow when they gain learning. The mountains bear the beating of the raindrops the way the good bear the harsh words of the wicked.
roles: The mountain does not answer each drop.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.2.sa: बरषहिं जलद भूमि निअराएँ। जथा नवहिं बुध बिद्या पाएँ। बूँद अघात सहहिं गिरि कैसे। खल के बचन संत सह जैसें ॥

rcm.4.15.chaupai.3.m: Little streams swell and rush along, bursting their banks, the way a petty person swaggers on a little money. Rainwater falling on the ground turns muddy, as the soul is clouded once it is wrapped in illusion.
roles: Shows swelling over a small gain as a shallow stream.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.3.sa: छुद्र नदीं भरि चलीं तोराई। जस थोरेहुँ धन खल इतराई॥ भूमि परत भा ढाबर पानी। जनु जीवहि माया लपटानी ॥

rcm.4.15.chaupai.4.m: Water gathers bit by bit and fills the ponds, as good qualities come one by one to a good person. River water, reaching the ocean, becomes still, as a soul becomes steady on finding Hari.
roles: Gives growth as slow gathering, not a leap.
rcm.4.15.chaupai.4.sa: समिटि समिटि जल भरहिं तलावा। जिमि सदगुन सज्जन पहिं आवा॥ सरिता जल जलनिधि महुँ जोई। होइ अचल जिमि जिव हरि पाई ॥

rcm.4.17.chaupai.2.m: Agastya's star rises and dries the water on the roads, as contentment dries up greed. Rivers and lakes shine with clear water, like the heart of a good person freed from pride and confusion.
roles: Shows a clear heart once pride and confusion have settled.
rcm.4.17.chaupai.2.sa: उदित अगस्ति पंथ जल सोषा। जिमि लोभहिं सोषइ संतोषा॥ सरिता सर निर्मल जल सोहा। संत हृदय जस गत मद मोहा ॥

rcm.4.17.chaupai.4.m: With neither mud nor dust, the earth looks like the work of a wise king. As the water shrinks, the fish grow restless, like a thoughtless householder when the money runs out.
roles: Shows providing for the dry season while the water is high.
rcm.4.17.chaupai.4.sa: पंक न रेनु सोह असि धरनी। नीति निपुन नृप कै जसि करनी॥ जल संकोच बिकल भइँ मीना। अबुध कुटुंबी जिमि धनहीना ॥

rcm.4.21.chaupai.4.m: Lord, there is no intoxicant like the pleasures of the senses; they cloud even a sage's mind in an instant. Hearing his humble words, Lakshman was pleased and reassured him in many ways.
roles: Shows comfort making him forget what he owed.
rcm.4.21.chaupai.4.sa: नाथ विषय सम मद कछु नाहीं। मुनि मन मोह करइ छन माहीं। सुनत बिनीत बचन सुख पावा। लछिमन तेहि बहु बिधि समुझावा ॥

rcm.4.29.chaupai.2.m: He (Jatayu) could not bear the sun's heat and turned back; I, being proud, flew on towards the sun. My wings burned in its boundless blaze, and I fell to the earth with a terrible cry.
roles: Shows he names his own pride as the cause.
rcm.4.29.chaupai.2.sa: तेज न सहि सक सो फिरि आवा। मैं अभिमानी रबि निअरावा॥ जरे पंख अति तेज अपारा। परेउँ भूमि करि घोर चिकारा ॥

rcm.4.30.chaupai.1.m: Whoever can leap the hundred-league ocean, wise and capable, will do Ram's work. Look at me and take heart: see what Ram's grace has done to my body.
roles: Shows grace has visibly acted once already.
rcm.4.30.chaupai.1.sa: जो नाघइ सत जोजन सागर। करइ सो राम काज मति आगर॥ मोहि बिलोकि धरहु मन धीरा। राम कृपाँ कस भयउ सरीरा ॥

rcm.4.30.chaupai.2.m: Even sinners who remember his name cross the boundless ocean of the world. You are his messengers: give up your timidity, keep Ram in your heart and find a way.
roles: Acts with Ram held in the heart.
rcm.4.30.chaupai.2.sa: पापिउ जाकर नाम सुमिरहीं। अति अपार भवसागर तरहीं॥ तासु दूत तुम्ह तजि कदराई राम हृदयँ धरि करहु उपाई ॥

rcm.4.31.chaupai.3.m: "What task in the world is too hard for you, my son? You were born for Ram's work." Hearing this, Hanuman grew to the size of a mountain.
rcm.4.31.chaupai.3.sa: कवन सो काज कठिन जग माहीं। जो नहिं होइ तात तुम्ह पाहीं॥ राम काज लगि तव अवतारा। सुनतहिं भयउ पर्बताकारा ॥

rcm.4.4.chaupai.1.m: Though I have many faults, Lord, let the servant not slip from the master's memory. Lord, every soul is bewildered by your illusion; it is freed only by your tenderness.
roles: Shows release asked from grace, not earned.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.1.sa: जदपि नाथ बहु अवगुन मोरें। सेवक प्रभुहि परै जनि भोरें॥ नाथ जीव तव मायाँ मोहा। सो निस्तरइ तुम्हारेहिं छोहा ॥

rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.m: And on top of that, I swear by Raghubir, I know no method of worship. A servant relies on his master, a child on its mother, and lives free of worry; the master has to look after him.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.2.sa: ता पर मैं रघुबीर दोहाई। जानउँ नहिं कछु भजन उपाई॥ सेवक सुत पति मातु भरोसें। रहइ असोच बनइ प्रभु पोसें ॥

rcm.4.4.chaupai.3.m: Saying this he fell at his feet in distress, showing his own form, his heart full of love. Then Raghupati lifted him up, held him to his heart, and cooled him with the tears of his own eyes.
roles: Shows him falling at the feet and being embraced.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.3.sa: अस कहि परेउ चरन अकुलाई। निज तनु प्रगटि प्रीति उर छाई॥ तब रघुपति उठाई उर लावा। निज लोचन जल सींचि जुड़ावा ॥

rcm.4.4.chaupai.4.m: Listen, Hanuman: don't let your heart feel small. You are twice as dear to me as Lakshman. Everyone calls me impartial, yet the one who serves me is dear to me, because he has no other refuge.
roles: Names having no other refuge as what makes him dear.
rcm.4.4.chaupai.4.sa: सुनु कपि जियँ मानसि जनि ऊना। तैं मम प्रिय लछिमन ते दूना॥ समदरसी मोहि कह सब कोऊ। सेवक प्रिय अनन्य गति सोऊ ॥

rcm.4.6.chaupai.4.m: Sugriva said: Listen, Raghuvir. Put aside your worry and steady your heart. I will serve you in every way, whatever it takes for Janaki to come back to you.
roles: Comfort given as a concrete promise of help.
rcm.4.6.chaupai.4.sa: कह सुग्रीव सुनहु रघुबीरा। तजहु सोच मन आनहु धीरा॥ सब प्रकार करिहउँ सेवकाई। जेहि बिधि मिलिहि जानकी आई ॥

rcm.4.8.chaupai.1.m: Those who are not pained by a friend's pain commit a grave wrong just by being seen. A true friend treats his own mountain of sorrow as a speck of dust, and his friend's speck of sorrow as a mountain.
roles: Shows being pained by a friend's pain.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.1.sa: जे न मित्र दुख होहिं दुखारी। तिन्हहि बिलोकत पातक भारी॥ निज दुख गिरि सम रज करि जाना। मित्रक दुख रज मेरु समाना ॥

rcm.4.8.chaupai.10.m: Bali is in fact my greatest benefactor: through him I met you, who end all sorrow. Now if I fought him even in a dream, I'd feel ashamed on waking.
roles: Shows the quarrel losing its grip in Ram's presence.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.10.sa: बालि परम हित जासु प्रसादा। मिलेहु राम तुम्ह समन बिषादा॥ सपनें जेहि सन होइ लराई। जागें समुझत मन सकुचाई ॥

scene.s: Bali chased a demon into a cave and told Sugriva to wait a fortnight. Sugriva waited a month; blood flowed out, he assumed Bali dead, sealed the cave and was made king. Bali fought his way out, decided his brother had betrayed him, and drove him out. Later, safe with Ram, Sugriva says that if he fought his brother even in a dream he'd be ashamed on waking.
scene.t: Sugriva and Bali: brothers split by a misunderstanding

rcm.4.8.chaupai.2.m: Why do those who lack this natural feeling force themselves into friendships? A friend turns you back from the wrong path and sets you on the right one, makes your good qualities known and keeps your faults to himself.
roles: Shows friendship defined by what it does for the other's good.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.2.sa: जिन्ह कें असि मति सहज न आई। ते सठ कत हठि करत मिताई॥ कुपथ निवारि सुपंथ चलावा। गुन प्रगटै अवगुनन्हि दुरावा ॥

rcm.4.8.chaupai.3.m: He gives and takes without suspicion, always does you good as far as he is able, and in hard times loves you a hundred times more. These, say the scriptures, are the qualities of a good friend.
roles: Shows love that multiplies in the friend's bad time.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.3.sa: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥

rcm.4.8.chaupai.4.m: One who says sweet, made-up words to your face but wishes you ill behind your back, with a crooked mind; whose heart moves like a snake, brother: it is best to leave such a false friend.
roles: Shows letting go of one who harms you.
rcm.4.8.chaupai.4.sa: आगें कह मृदु बचन बनाई। पाछें अनहित मन कुटिलाई॥ जाकर िचत अहि गति सम भाई। अस कुमित्र परिहरेहिं भलाई ॥

rcm.5.1.doha.1.m: Hanuman touched it with his hand, bowed to it, and said: how can I rest until I have done Ram's work?
rcm.5.1.doha.1.sa: हनूमान तेहि परसा कर पुनि कीन्ह प्रनाम। राम काजु कीन्हें बिनु मोहि कहाँ बिश्राम ॥

rcm.5.1.shloka.2.m: Raghupati, I tell you truly, and you are the inner self of all: there is no other longing in my heart. Give me full devotion, best of the Raghus, and make my mind free of desire and the other faults.
roles: Shows a daily prayer for devotion alone.
rcm.5.1.shloka.2.sa: नान्या स्पृहा रघुपते हृदयेऽस्मदीये सत्यं वदामि च भवानखिलान्तरात्मा। भक्तिं प्रयच्छ रघुपुंगव निर्भरां मे कामादिदोषरहितं कुरु मानसं च ॥

rcm.5.12.chaupai.1.m: Knowing him to be the Lord's own, her love deepened; her eyes filled and she thrilled. 'Hanuman, I was drowning in a sea of separation, and you became my ship.'
roles: Names the one who reached her.
rcm.5.12.chaupai.1.sa: हरिजन जानि प्रीति अति गाढ़ी। सजल नयन पुलकावलि बाढ़ी॥ बूड़त बिरह जलधि हनुमाना। भयहु तात मो कहुँ जलजाना ॥

rcm.5.12.chaupai.5.m: Mother, the Lord and his brother are well, but your sorrow makes him sorrowful. Don't let your heart feel small, mother: Ram's love for you is twice yours.
roles: She is told not to count herself less.
rcm.5.12.chaupai.5.sa: मातु कुसल प्रभु अनुज समेता। तव दुख दुखी सुकृपा निकेता॥ जनि जननी मानह जियँ ऊना। तुम्ह ते प्रेमु राम कें दूना ॥

rcm.5.13.chaupai.3.m: Telling one's grief lightens it a little. But whom can I tell? No one knows this pain. The truth of the love between you and me, my beloved, only my own heart knows.
roles: The ache is his alone to carry.
rcm.5.13.chaupai.3.sa: कहेहू तें कछु दुख घटि होई। काहि कहौं यह जान न कोई॥ तत्व प्रेम कर मम अरु तोरा। जानत प्रिया एकु मनु मोरा ॥

rcm.5.13.chaupai.4.m: And that heart of mine stays with you always. Know that this is the whole of my love. Hearing her Lord's message, Sita was so lost in love she forgot herself.
roles: Shows his love measured in one sentence.
rcm.5.13.chaupai.4.sa: सो मनु सदा रहत तोहि पाहीं। जानु प्रीति रसु एतनेहि माहीं॥ प्रभु संदेसु सुनत बैदेही। मगन प्रेम तन सुधि नहिं तेही ॥

rcm.5.13.chaupai.5.m: Hanuman said: 'Hold steady in your heart, mother. Remember Ram, who gives joy to his servants. Bring to mind Raghupati's strength; hearing my words, put away your fear.'
roles: Shows steadiness asked of the heart.
rcm.5.13.chaupai.5.sa: कह कपि हृदयँ धीर धरु माता। सुमिरु राम सेवक सुखदाता॥ उर आनहु रघुपति प्रभुताई। सुनि मम बचन तजहु कदराई ॥

rcm.5.14.doha.1.m: Listen, mother: monkeys have no great strength or wisdom. But by the Lord's power even a tiny snake can swallow Garuda.
roles: Shows strength borrowed from the Lord.
rcm.5.14.doha.1.sa: सुनु माता साखामृग नहिं बल बुद्धि बिसाल। प्रभु प्रताप तें गरुड़हि खाइ परम लघु ब्याल ॥

rcm.5.2.chaupai.5.m: As Surasa widened her mouth, Hanuman showed a form twice as large. She made her mouth a hundred leagues wide; then Hanuman took a very tiny form.
roles: Shows him meeting a test with play and not dread.
rcm.5.2.chaupai.5.sa: जस जस सुरसा बदनु बढ़ावा। तासु दून कपि रूप देखावा॥ सत जोजन तेहिं आनन कीन्हा। अति लघु रूप पवनसुत लीन्हा ॥

rcm.5.20.doha.1.m: Raghunayak protects those who bow to him; he is an ocean of compassion. If you go to him for refuge, the Lord will protect you and forget your offence.
roles: Going for refuge while there is time.
rcm.5.20.doha.1.sa: प्रनतपाल रघुनायक करुना सिंधु खरारि। गएँ सरन प्रभु राखिहैं तव अपराध बिसारि ॥

scene.s: Hanuman, a prisoner, tells Ravana himself that the door is still open.

rcm.5.21.chaupai.3.m: For one turned away from Ram, wealth and power slip away even while held, and having them is like not having them. Rivers with no spring at their source dry up as soon as the rains have passed.
rcm.5.21.chaupai.3.sa: राम बिमुख संपति प्रभुताई। जाइ रही पाई बिनु पाई॥ सजल मूल जिन्ह सरितन्ह नाहीं। बरषि गएँ पुनि तबहिं सुखाहीं ॥

scene.s: Bound and dragged before Ravana, Hanuman feels no shame and tells the most powerful man in the world, calmly, to return Sita: wealth with no deep source dries up like a rain-fed river. Ravana orders his tail set on fire; Hanuman burns Lanka and returns. Back before Ram, he insists none of it was his own greatness.

rcm.5.25.chaupai.2.m: Give him my greeting, friend, and say: Lord, you lack nothing, but kindness to the helpless is your promise. Remember it, and take away my heavy trouble.
roles: Shows her appealing to his promise.
rcm.5.25.chaupai.2.sa: कहेहु तात अस मोर प्रनामा। सब प्रकार प्रभु पूरनकामा॥ दीन दयाल बिरिदु संभारी। हरहु नाथ सम संकट भारी ॥

rcm.5.3.doha.1.m: Friend, put all the joys of heaven and liberation on one side of the scale: together they cannot match the joy of a single moment of good company.
roles: Shows the joy of being with the good.
rcm.5.3.doha.1.sa: तात स्वर्ग अपबर्ग सुख धरिअ तुला एक अंग। तूल न ताहि सकल मिलि जो सुख लव सतसंग ॥

rcm.5.30.chaupai.1.m: Hearing of Sita's sorrow, the Lord, home of joy, filled his lotus eyes with tears. 'Can one whose only refuge is me, in word, body and mind, ever meet calamity, even in a dream?'
rcm.5.30.chaupai.1.sa: सुनि सीता दुख प्रभु सुख अयना। भरि आए जल राजिव नयना॥ बचन कायँ मन मम गति जाही। सपनेहुँ बूझिअ बिपति कि ताही ॥

scene.s: Hearing of Sita's suffering, Ram's eyes fill with tears.

rcm.5.30.chaupai.2.m: Hanuman said: 'Lord, calamity is only this: when remembering and worshipping you does not happen. What is a demon to the Lord? We will defeat the enemy and bring Janaki back.'
roles: Shows remembrance as the one thing to guard.
rcm.5.30.chaupai.2.sa: कह हनुमंत बिपति प्रभु सोई। जब तव सुमिरन भजन न होई॥ केतिक बात प्रभु जातुधान की। रिपुहि जीति आनिबी जानकी ॥

scene.s: Ram has asked whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers.

rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.m: "All of it was your glory, Lord. None of it was my own greatness."
roles: The strength was lent, so the glory is returned.
rcm.5.31.chaupai.5.sa: सो सब तव प्रताप रघुराई। नाथ न कछू मोरि प्रभुताई ॥

rcm.5.32.chaupai.1.m: 'Lord, give me by your kindness the devotion that brings great joy and never leaves.' Hearing the monkey's utterly simple words, the Lord said 'so be it', Bhavani.
rcm.5.32.chaupai.1.sa: नाथ भगति अति सुखदायनी। देहु कृपा करि अनपायनी॥ सुनि प्रभु परम सरल कपि बानी। एवमस्तु तब कहेउ भवानी ॥

rcm.5.35.doha.1.m: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
roles: Names the duty to say the unwelcome thing.
rcm.5.35.doha.1.sa: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥

rcm.5.36.chaupai.4.m: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
roles: Shows small greed undoing every other merit.
rcm.5.36.chaupai.4.sa: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥

rcm.5.38.chaupai.3.m: Good sense and bad sense live in every heart; so say the scriptures. Where good sense is, many kinds of prosperity follow; where bad sense is, calamity is sure to come.
rcm.5.38.chaupai.3.sa: सुमति कुमति सब कें उर रहहीं। नाथ पुरान निगम अस कहहीं॥ जहाँ सुमति तहँ संपति नाना। जहाँ कुमति तहँ बिपति निदाना ॥

rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.m: (Shiva:) Uma, this is the greatness of the good: they do good even to those who harm them. (Vibhishan:) You are like a father to me; strike me if you will. But your good, brother, lies in turning to Ram.
roles: Names goodwill toward the one who struck him.
rcm.5.39.chaupai.4.sa: उमा संत कइ इहइ बड़ाई। मंद करत जो करइ भलाई॥ तुम्ह पितु सरिस भलेहिं मोहि मारा। रामु भजें हित नाथ तुम्हारा ॥

scene.s: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
scene.t: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked

rcm.5.39.doha.1.m: Ram is the Lord whose resolve is true, and your court is in the grip of doom. I go now to Raghuvir for refuge; don't blame me.
roles: Shows he leaves openly, having said the true thing.
rcm.5.39.doha.1.sa: रामु सत्यसंकल्प प्रभु सभा कालबस तोरि। मैं रघुबीर सरन अब जाउँ देहु जनि खोरि ॥

scene.s: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
scene.t: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked

rcm.5.4.chaupai.1.m: Enter the city and do all your work, holding the king of Kosala in your heart. For such a one, poison turns to nectar, enemies become friends, the ocean shrinks to a hoofprint, and fire turns cool.
roles: Shows ocean becomes a hoofprint and fire turns cool.
rcm.5.4.chaupai.1.sa: प्रबिसि नगर कीजे सब काजा। हृदयँ राखि कोसलपुर राजा॥ गरल सुधा रिपु करहिं मिताई। गोपद सिंधु अनल सितलाई ॥

rcm.5.41.chaupai.4.m: 'The wretch has come to learn our secrets; I think we should bind him.' 'Friend, you have weighed policy well. But my vow is to take away the fear of whoever comes for refuge.'
roles: Shows shelter given against cautious advice.
rcm.5.41.chaupai.4.sa: भेद हमार लेन सठ आवा। राखिअ बाँधि मोहि अस भावा॥ सखा नीति तुम्ह नीकि बिचारी। मम पन सरनागत भयहारी ॥

scene.s: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
scene.t: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech

rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.m: Even someone who carries the sin of killing countless brahmins, if he comes to me for shelter, I will not turn away. The moment a soul turns to face me, the wrongs of countless lives are wiped away.
roles: Shows coming for shelter as one is.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.1.sa: कोटि बिप्र बध लागहिं जाहू। आएँ सरन तजउँ नहिं ताहू॥ सनमुख होइ जीव मोहि जबहीं। जन्म कोटि अघ नासहिं तबहीं ॥

rcm.5.42.chaupai.2.m: It is the natural way of a sinner never to like worshipping me. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me at all?
roles: Shows trust in what the turning shows.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.2.sa: पापवंत कर सहज सुभाऊ। भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥ जौं पै दुष्ट हृदय सोइ होई। मोरें सनमुख आव कि सोई ॥

scene.s: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
scene.t: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech

rcm.5.42.chaupai.3.m: "A person with a clean mind reaches me; I have no liking for deceit, tricks or fault-finding. Even if Ravana sent him to learn our secrets, there is no fear or loss in it for us, Sugriva."
roles: Nothing to fear and nothing to lose from giving shelter.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.3.sa: निर्मल मन जन सो मोहि पावा। मोहि कपट छल छिद्र न भावा॥ भेद लेन पठवा दससीसा। तबहुँ न कछु भय हानि कपीसा ॥

scene.s: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.

rcm.5.42.chaupai.4.m: Friend, Lakshman could destroy every demon in the world in a moment. And if he has come to me in fear, seeking shelter, I will keep him as dear as my own life.
roles: Gives shelter that does not ask where one came from.
rcm.5.42.chaupai.4.sa: जग महुँ सखा निसाचर जेते। लछिमनु हनइ निमिष महुँ तेते॥ जौं सभीत आवा सरनाईं। रखिहउँ ताहि प्रान की नाईं ॥

rcm.5.43.doha.1.m: Hearing your good name with my own ears I have come, Lord, breaker of the fear of the world. Save me, save me, remover of distress, Raghubir, whose refuge brings joy.
rcm.5.43.doha.1.sa: श्रवन सुजसु सुनि आयउँ प्रभु भंजन भव भीर। त्राहि त्राहि आरति हरन सरन सुखद रघुबीर ॥

rcm.5.44.chaupai.3.m: 'You lived day and night among the wicked; how did you keep your goodness, friend? I know all your ways: very wise in conduct, with no taste for wrong.'
roles: His goodness among the cruel is honoured.
rcm.5.44.chaupai.3.sa: खल मंडली बसहु दिनु राती। सखा धरम निबहइ केहि भाँती॥ मैं जानउँ तुम्हारि सब रीती। अति नय निपुन न भाव अनीती ॥

rcm.5.44.chaupai.4.m: "Better to live in hell, friend, than to be given the company of the wicked. Now that I have seen your feet, Lord, I am well, since you have shown me kindness, knowing me as your own."
roles: Shows him well now, having been taken in.
rcm.5.44.chaupai.4.sa: बरु भल बास नरक कर ताता। दुष्ट संग जनि देइ बिधाता॥ अब पद देखि कुसल रघुराया। जौं तुम्ह कीन्हि जानि जन दाया ॥

rcm.5.45.chaupai.4.m: I am a demon, low by nature; I have never done a single good deed. And yet the Lord whose form sages cannot reach even in meditation has gladly held me to his heart.
roles: Shows being astonished at being received.
rcm.5.45.chaupai.4.sa: मैं निसिचर अति अधम सुभाऊ। सुभ आचरनु कीन्ह नहिं काऊ॥ जासु रूप मुनि ध्यान न आवा। तेहिं प्रभु हरषि हृदयँ मोहि लावा ॥

rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.m: Listen, friend, I tell you my own nature, as Bhushundi, Shambhu and Girija know it. If a person who has harmed every living thing comes to me afraid, looking for shelter, and gives up pride, delusion, deceit and trickery, I make him like a saint at once. Mother, father, brother, son, wife, body, wealth, home, friends and family:
roles: Refuge taken with pride and guile laid down.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.1.sa: सुनहु सखा निज कहउँ सुभाऊ। जान भुसुंडि संभु गिरिजाऊ॥ जौं नर होइ चराचर द्रोही। आवै सभय सरन तकि मोही ॥ तजि मद मोह कपट छल नाना। करउँ सद्य तेहि साधु समाना॥ जननी जनक बंधु सुत दारा। तनु धनु भवन सुहृद परिवारा ॥

rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.m: Gathering the threads of attachment to all of these, he twists them into one cord and ties his mind to my feet. Even-minded, wanting nothing, with no elation, grief or fear in his mind: such a good person lives in my heart as wealth lives in a miser's heart. Saints like you are dear to me; I take a body for no other reason.
roles: Shows seeing alike and wanting nothing.
rcm.5.46.chaupai.3.sa: सब कै ममता ताग बटोरी। मम पद मनहि बाँध बरि डोरी॥ समदरसी इच्छा कछु नाहीं। हरष सोक भय नहिं मन माहीं ॥ अस सज्जन मम उर बस कैसें। लोभी हृदयँ बसइ धनु जैसें॥ तुम्ह सारिखे संत प्रिय मोरें। धरउँ देह नहिं आन निहोरें ॥

rcm.5.47.chaupai.3.m: Listen, Lord of all that moves and does not move, protector of those who bow, knower of hearts: there was some desire in my heart at first; it has been carried away in the river of love for your feet.
roles: Shows love for the Lord's feet as the river.
rcm.5.47.chaupai.3.sa: सुनहु देव सचराचर स्वामी। प्रनतपाल उर अंतरजामी॥ उर कछु प्रथम बासना रही। प्रभु पद प्रीति सरित सो बही ॥

rcm.5.48.chaupai.4.m: Raghunath, though a single arrow of yours could dry up countless oceans, good policy says: first go and ask the ocean politely.
roles: Shows restraint chosen by the one who could compel.
rcm.5.48.chaupai.4.sa: कह लंकेस सुनहु रघुनायक। कोटि सिंधु सोषक तव सायक॥ जद्यपि तदपि नीति असि गाई। बिनय करिअ सागर सन जाई ॥

scene.s: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.
scene.t: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after

rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.m: "Lakshman, bring my bow and arrows; I will dry up the ocean with fiery shafts. Pleading with the stubborn, friendship with the crooked, fine principles to a born miser, talk of wisdom to someone lost in possessiveness, praise of renunciation to the very greedy, calm to the angry, and holy stories to the lustful: all are like sowing seed in barren soil."
roles: Shows after real humility, firmness is right.
rcm.5.56.chaupai.1.sa: लछिमन बान सरासन आनू। सोषौं बारिधि बिसिख कृसानु॥ सठ सन बिनय कुटिल सन प्रीति। सहज कृपन सन सुंदर नीति ॥ ममता रत सन ग्यान कहानी। अति लोभी सन बिरति बखानी॥ क्रोधिहि सम कामिहि हरिकथा। ऊसर बीज बएँ फल जथा ॥

scene.s: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.
scene.t: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after

rcm.5.6.chaupai.1.m: Son of the wind, hear how I live: like the poor tongue among the teeth. Friend, knowing me to be without support, will the Lord of the Sun dynasty ever show me grace?
roles: The tongue must move with care or be bitten.
rcm.5.6.chaupai.1.sa: सुनहु पवनसुत रहनि हमारी। जिमि दसनन्हि महुँ जीभ बिचारी॥ तात कबहुँ मोहि जानि अनाथा। करिहहिं कृपा भानुकुल नाथा ॥

rcm.5.6.chaupai.2.m: 'I have a demon's body and no spiritual practice, no love for his lotus feet in my mind. But now I have hope, Hanuman: without Hari's grace one does not meet the good.'
roles: Shows hope born from one good meeting.
rcm.5.6.chaupai.2.sa: तामस तनु कछु साधन नाहीं। प्रीत न पद सरोज मन माहीं॥ अब मोहि भा भरोस हनुमंता। बिनु हरिकृपा मिलहिं नहिं संता ॥

rcm.5.6.doha.1.m: Listen, friend: I am that lowly, and yet on me Raghubir showed kindness. Remembering his goodness, his eyes filled with tears.
roles: Shows tears at the memory of kindness received.
rcm.5.6.doha.1.sa: अस मैं अधम सखा सुनु मोहू पर रघुबीर। कीन्हीं कृपा सुमिरि गुन भरे बिलोचन नीर ॥

rcm.6.110.doha.1.m: Listen, brother: your treasury and home are truly mine. But remembering Bharat's state, each moment feels like an age to me.
roles: Comfort is offered and his mind is already at home with the one waiting.
rcm.6.110.doha.1.sa: तोर कोस गृह मोर सब सत्य बचन सुनु भ्रात। भरत दसा सुमिरत मोहि निमिष कल्प सम जात ॥

rcm.6.111.doha.1.m: The one whom sages cannot reach in meditation, whom the Vedas call 'not this, not this': that ocean of kindness is joking and playing with monkeys.
roles: Names the unreachable one at play with simple creatures.
rcm.6.111.doha.1.sa: मुनि जेहि ध्यान न पावहिं नेति नेति कह बेद। कृपासिंधु सोइ कपिन्ह सन करत अनेक बिनोद ॥

rcm.6.111.doha.2.m: Uma, yoga, chanting, charity, austerity, sacrifices, vows and rules: none of these win Ram's kindness the way pure love alone does.
roles: Names love alone as the means.
rcm.6.111.doha.2.sa: उमा जोग जप दान तप नाना मख ब्रत नेम। राम कृपा नहिं करहिं तसि जसि निष्केवल प्रेम ॥

rcm.6.112.chaupai.3.m: Now go home, each of you. Remember me, and don't be afraid of anyone. Hearing this, the monkeys, overcome with love, joined their hands and spoke respectfully.
