rcm.6.112.chaupai.3.sa: निज निज गृह अब तुम्ह सब जाहू। सुमिरेहु मोहि डरपहु जनि काहू॥ सुनत बचन प्रेमाकुल बानर। जोरि पानि बोले सब सादर ॥

rcm.6.12.chaupai.3.m: How is it that sound advice doesn't take with you? Like medicine on one in death's grip. Seeing it was evening, Ravana went to his palace, admiring his twenty arms.
roles: Shows knowing when advice can no longer land.
rcm.6.12.chaupai.3.sa: हित मत तोहि न लागत कैसें। काल बिबस कहुँ भेषज जैसें॥ संध्या समय जानि दससीसा। भवन चलेउ निरखत भुज बीसा ॥

scene.s: Mandodari, hearing the bridge is built, again begs Ravana to pick fights only where he can win, and to step back. Ravana boasts. His son Prahasta tells the court that flatterers are many and honest advisers few, and suggests first sending an envoy. Ravana insults him, and Prahasta leaves saying good advice cannot reach one set on ruin.
scene.t: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again

rcm.6.19.chaupai.4.m: Why explain much to you? I know you are very capable. Talk with the enemy in a way that gets our work done and is good for him too.
roles: Shows goodwill held even toward the enemy.
rcm.6.19.chaupai.4.sa: बहुत बुझाइ तुम्हहि का कहऊँ। परम चतुर मैं जानत अहऊँ॥ काजु हमार तासु हित होई। रिपु सन करेहु बतकही सोई ॥

rcm.6.19.doha.1.m: Then he went into the court, remembering Ram's lotus feet, looking this way and that with a lion's gait, steady, brave, a mass of strength.
rcm.6.19.doha.1.sa: गयउ सभा दरबार तब सुमिरि राम पद कंज। सिंह ठवनि इत उत चितव धीर बीर बल पुंज ॥

rcm.6.19.sortha.3.m: 'Every task is already accomplished by itself; the Lord has only given me the honour.' Thinking this, the prince's body thrilled and his heart was glad.
rcm.6.19.sortha.3.sa: स्वयंसिद्ध सब काज नाथ मोहि आदरु दियउ। अस बिचारि जुबराज तन पुलकित हरषित हियउ ॥

rcm.6.34.doha.2.m: The monkey's foot would not leave the ground, and seeing it, the enemy's pride drained away; just as a good person's mind does not abandon what is right, though a million obstacles come.
roles: Shows a foot that will not lift from the ground.
rcm.6.34.doha.2.sa: भूमि न छाँड़त कपि चरन देखत रिपु मद भाग। कोटि बिघ्न ते संत कर मन जिमि नीति न त्याग ॥

rcm.6.60.chaupai.2.m: Brother, you could never bear to see me sad; your nature was always gentle. For my sake you left mother and father and bore the forest's cold, heat and wind.
roles: Shows the night is passing and help has not come.
rcm.6.60.chaupai.2.sa: सकहु न दुखित देखि मोहि काउ। बंधु सदा तव मृदुल सुभाऊ॥ मम हित लागि तजेहु पितु माता। सहेहु बिपिन हिम आतप बाता ॥

rcm.6.62.chaupai.4.m: Listen, son: Ravana is in the grip of doom; would he heed good counsel now? Blessed, blessed, blessed are you, Vibhishan; you have become the ornament of our clan.
roles: Shows his choice being called the clan's pride.
rcm.6.62.chaupai.4.sa: सुनु भयउ कालबस रावन। सो कि मान अब परम सिखावन॥ धन्य धन्य तैं धन्य विभीषन। भयहु तात निसिचर कुल भूषन ॥

scene.s: Woken to fight, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana plainly he was wrong to take Sita and should have consulted him first. Still he goes out to fight for his brother. On the field he meets Vibhishan, who chose Ram, and instead of cursing him, he blesses him as the pride of their family.
scene.t: Kumbhakarna fights for a brother he knows is wrong

rcm.6.76.chaupai.1.m: Ravana gave them sermons on knowledge: he himself was wicked, but his talk was pure and fine. Many are skilled at advising others; those who practise it themselves are not many.
roles: Measuring teaching by the teacher's conduct, starting with oneself.
rcm.6.76.chaupai.1.sa: तिन्हहि ग्यान उपदेसा रावन। आपुन मंद कथा सुभ पावन॥ पर उपदेस कुसल बहुतेरे। जे आचरहिं ते नर न घनेरे ॥

rcm.6.79.chaupai.3.m: Valour and patience are the wheels of that chariot; truth and good conduct are its firm flag and banner. Strength, discernment, self-control and kindness to others are its horses, yoked with the reins of forgiveness, compassion and evenness of mind.
roles: Patience named as a wheel of victory.
rcm.6.79.chaupai.3.sa: सौरज धीरज तेहि रथ चाका। सत्य सील दृढ़ ध्वजा पताका॥ बल बिबेक दम परहित घोरे। छमा कृपा समता रजु जोरे ॥

rcm.6.8.chaupai.3.m: "My lord, pick a quarrel only with someone you can defeat with your wits and strength. Between you and Ram there is the difference between a firefly and the sun."
roles: Shows measuring the opponent before choosing a fight.
rcm.6.8.chaupai.3.sa: नाथ बयरु कीजे ताही सों। बुधि बल सकिअ जीति जाही सों॥ तुम्हहि रघुपतिहि अंतर कैसा। खलु खद्योत दिनकरहि जैसा ॥

scene.s: Mandodari, hearing the bridge is built, again begs Ravana to pick fights only where he can win, and to step back. Ravana boasts. His son Prahasta tells the court that flatterers are many and honest advisers few, and suggests first sending an envoy. Ravana insults him, and Prahasta leaves saying good advice cannot reach one set on ruin.
scene.t: Mandodari and Prahasta warn Ravana again

rcm.7.10.chaupai.4.m: Listen, sage: these are all my friends. They were my boats across the ocean of battle. For my sake they staked their lives; they are dearer to me than even Bharat.
roles: Shows thanks given publicly and specifically.
rcm.7.10.chaupai.4.sa: ए सब सखा सुनहु मुनि मेरे। भए समर सागर कहँ बेरे॥ मम हित लागि जन्म इन्ह हारे। भरतहु ते मोहि अधिक पिआरे ॥

rcm.7.104.doha.3.m: This ignorant soul, in the grip of your maya, wanders constantly astray. Ocean of mercy, Lord, do not be angry with him.
roles: Shows the one insulted is the one who pleads for the offender.
rcm.7.104.doha.3.sa: तव माया बस जीव जड़ संतत फिरइ भुलान। तेहि पर क्रोध न करिअ प्रभु कृपासिंधु भगवान ॥

scene.s: In an earlier life Kakbhushundi was a proud, wealthy, sharp-tongued young man whose gentle teacher kept trying to guide him. One day in the temple he refused even to rise when the teacher entered. The teacher said nothing, but a curse fell on the student; the teacher at once prayed for him, asking that he not be punished in anger. Lives later, the one thorn Kakbhushundi still carries is the memory of that teacher's gentleness.
scene.t: The student who would not stand for his teacher

rcm.7.106.chaupai.1.m: Whatever body I took, animal, god or human, I kept up my devotion to Ram. Yet one thorn never left me: I never forgot my teacher's gentle, kindly nature.
roles: Names remorse that outlasts lifetimes and the other's kindness that hurts most.
rcm.7.106.chaupai.1.sa: त्रिजग देव नर जोइ तनु धरउँ। तहँ तहँ राम भजन अनुसरऊँ॥ एक सूल मोहि बिसर न काऊ। गुर कर कोमल सील सुभाऊ ॥

rcm.7.107.chaupai.8.m: Lord, listen: even a wise man's heart grows angry when he is slighted again and again. If someone rubs sandalwood too hard, even it will burst into flame.
roles: Shows the wise losing their temper after long provocation.
rcm.7.107.chaupai.8.sa: सुनु प्रभु बहुत अवग्या किएँ। उपज क्रोध ग्यानिन्ह के हिएँ॥ अति संघरषन जौं कर कोई। अनल प्रगट चंदन ते होई ॥

rcm.7.108.doha.2.m: Uma, those devoted to Ram's feet, free of desire, pride and anger, see the whole world filled with their Lord; with whom would they quarrel?
roles: Shows seeing one's Lord in every being.
rcm.7.108.doha.2.sa: उमा जे राम चरन रत बिगत काम मद क्रोध। निज प्रभुमय देखहिं जगत केहि सन करहिं बिरोध ॥

rcm.7.116.chaupai.1.m: I have explained the principle of knowledge; now hear the power of the jewel of devotion. Devotion to Ram is a beautiful wish-granting gem, Garuda: in whose heart it lives, it is supreme light day and night, needing no lamp, ghee or wick. The poverty of delusion does not come near, and the wind of greed cannot blow it out.
roles: Shows a light that needs no tending.
rcm.7.116.chaupai.1.sa: कहेउँ ग्यान सिद्धांत बुझाई। सुनहु भगति मनि कै प्रभुताई॥ राम भगति चिंतामनि सुंदर। बसइ गरुड़ जाके उर अंतर ॥ परम प्रकास रूप दिन राती। नहिं कछु चहिअ दिआ घृत बाती॥ मोह दरिद्र निकट नहिं आवा। लोभ बात नहिं ताहि बुझावा ॥

rcm.7.116.chaupai.9.m: Ram is the ocean, and the steady good are the clouds; Hari is the sandal tree, and the saints are the breeze. The fruit of everything is beautiful devotion to Hari, and no one has found it without the good.
roles: Shows devotion as the fruit of everything.
rcm.7.116.chaupai.9.sa: राम सिंधु घन सज्जन धीरा। चंदन तरु हरि संत समीरा॥ सब कर फल हरि भगति सुहाई। सो बिनु संत न काहूँ पाई ॥

rcm.7.117.chaupai.11.m: The rise of the good always brings joy, as moon and sun bring joy to the whole world. The Vedas hold non-harm as the highest duty, and there is no wrong as heavy as slandering others.
roles: Shows the saint's rising gladdens everyone like sun and moon.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.11.sa: संत उदय संतत सुखकारी। बिस्व सुखद जिमि इंदु तमारी॥ परम धर्म श्रुति बिदित अहिंसा। पर निंदा सम अघ न गरीसा ॥

rcm.7.117.chaupai.15.m: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
roles: Names anger as bile that burns one's own chest.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.15.sa: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥

rcm.7.117.chaupai.17.m: Possessiveness is ringworm and envy is the itch; the swings of elation and dejection are throat ailments. The burning you feel at another's happiness is consumption, and malice and a crooked mind are leprosy.
roles: Names burning at another's joy as an illness one suffers, which can be treated.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.17.sa: ममता दादु कंडु इरषाई। हरष बिषाद गरह बहुताई॥ पर सुख देखि जरनि सोइ छई। कुष्ट दुष्टता मन कुटिलई ॥

rcm.7.117.chaupai.6.m: Those who gain this body and still do not worship Hari, sunk in the lowest of pleasures, throw away the philosopher's stone from their hand and take shards of glass in exchange.
roles: Gives human birth for worship of Hari.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.6.sa: सो तनु धरि हरि भजहिं न जे नर। होहिं बिषय रत मंद मंद तर॥ काँच किरिच बदलें ते लेहीं। कर ते डारि परस मनि देहीं ॥

rcm.7.117.chaupai.7.m: There is no sorrow in the world like poverty, and no joy like meeting good people. To do good to others in word, thought and deed is the natural way of the good.
roles: Shows the company of good people as the greatest joy.
rcm.7.117.chaupai.7.sa: नहिं दरिद्र सम दुख जग माहीं। संत मिलन सम सुख जग नाहीं॥ पर उपकार बचन मन काया। संत सहज सुभाउ खगराया ॥

rcm.7.12.chaupai.1.m: The Lord saw that Kaikeyi was ashamed, so he went first to her house, Bhavani, comforted her and gave her great ease. Then he went to his own palace.
roles: Shows forgiveness given to one already sunk in remorse.
rcm.7.12.chaupai.1.sa: प्रभु जानी कैकई लजानी। प्रथम तासु गृह गए भवानी॥ ताहि प्रबोधि बहुत सुख दीन्हा। पुनि निज भवन गवन हरि कीन्हा ॥

scene.s: From the air Ram points out his birthplace, dearer to him than heaven. Bharat falls at his feet; Ram lifts him up and the mothers run to him like cows to their calves at dusk. Ram introduces his friends as those who carried him through the war, and seeing Kaikeyi ashamed, goes to her house first.

rcm.7.121.doha.2.m: Girija, there is no gain like the company of saints; and it does not happen without Hari's grace, sing the Vedas and Puranas.
roles: Names a good meeting as grace.
rcm.7.121.doha.2.sa: गिरिजा संत समागम सम न लाभ कछु आन। बिनु हरि कृपा न होइ सो गावहिं बेद पुरान ॥

rcm.7.126.chaupai.3.m: In this age of Kali there is no other means, no yoga, sacrifice, chanting, austerity, vow or ritual worship: remember Ram, sing Ram, and always listen to the qualities of Ram.
rcm.7.126.chaupai.3.sa: एहिं कलिकाल न साधन दूजा। जोग जग्य जप तप ब्रत पूजा॥ रामहि सुमिरिअ गाइअ रामहि। संतत सुनिअ राम गुन ग्रामहि ॥

rcm.7.126.doha.1.m: There is no one as poor as I am, and no friend of the poor like you, Raghubir. Thinking this over, jewel of the Raghus, take away the heavy fear of the world.
roles: Shows his poverty and the Lord's kindness set side by side as the whole prayer.
rcm.7.126.doha.1.sa: मो सम दीन न दीन हित तुम्ह समान रघुबीर। अस बिचारि रघुबंस मनि हरहु बिषम भव भीर ॥

rcm.7.20.chaupai.2.m: Remember your vow to shelter the shelterless and don't abandon me, friend of devotees. You are my lord, teacher, father and mother; leaving your feet, where would I go?
roles: Shows he asks to stay at Ram's feet.
rcm.7.20.chaupai.2.sa: असरन सरन बिरदु संभारी। मोहि जनि तजहु भगत हितकारी॥ मोरें तुम्ह प्रभु गुर पितु माता। जाउँ कहाँ तजि पद जलजाता ॥

rcm.7.22.chaupai.2.m: You are my friend and a brother like Bharat. Keep coming and going to Ayodhya always. Hearing this, he felt great joy and fell at Ram's feet, eyes full of tears.
roles: Shows friendship kept across rank and distance.
rcm.7.22.chaupai.2.sa: तुम्ह मम सखा भरत सम भ्राता। सदा रहेहु पुर आवत जाता॥ बचन सुनत उपजा सुख भारी। परेउ चरन भरि लोचन बारी ॥

rcm.7.3.chaupai.1.m: Only one day of the appointed time, the support of his life, was left. Thinking of it, Bharat's grief was boundless. 'Why hasn't my Lord come? Has he forgotten me, knowing me to be crooked?'
roles: Shows the mind supplying the worst reason for the silence.
rcm.7.3.chaupai.1.sa: रहेउ एक दिन अवधि अधारा। समुझत मन दुख भयउ अपारा॥ कारन कवन नाथ नहिं आयउ। जानि कुटिल किधौं मोहि बिसरायउ ॥

rcm.7.3.doha.1.m: Bharat's mind was sinking in the ocean of separation from Ram when the son of the wind arrived in a Brahmin's guise, as if a boat had come.
roles: Shows the long faithfulness being answered.
rcm.7.3.doha.1.sa: राम बिरह सागर महँ भरत मगन मन होत। बिप्र रूप धरि पवनसुत आइ गयउ जनु पोत॥1क॥

rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.m: The way good and bad people treat each other is like sandalwood and the axe: listen, brother, the axe cuts the sandalwood tree, yet the sandalwood, by its own nature, leaves its fragrance on the axe.
roles: Shows giving fragrance to the blade.
rcm.7.39.chaupai.4.sa: संत असंतन्हि कै असि करनी। जिमि कुठार चंदन आचरनी॥ काटइ परसु मलय सुनु भाई। निज गुन देइ सुगंध बसाई ॥

scene.s: Bharat asks Ram to explain the difference between good and malicious people. Ram says the good are like sandalwood that perfumes the axe that cuts it; they feel others' sorrow and joy as their own and never speak harshly. The malicious burn at others' success and feast on gossip. No duty equals doing good to others.
scene.t: Ram on good people and difficult people

rcm.7.4.chaupai.6.m: Seeing you, all my sorrows are over; today I have met my beloved Ram himself. He asked again and again after everyone's welfare. 'Brother, what can I give you? Nothing in the world equals this news; I have thought it over. I can never repay you. Now tell me about my Lord.'
roles: Shows every sorrow ending at the sight of the messenger.
rcm.7.4.chaupai.6.sa: कपि तव दरस सकल दुख बीते। मिले आजुमोहि राम पिरीते॥ बार बार बूझी कुसलाता। तो कहुँ देउँ काह सुन भ्राता ॥ एहि संदेस सरिस जग माहीं। करि बिचार देखेउँ कछु नाहीं॥ नाहिन तात उरिन मैं तोही। अब प्रभु चरित सुनावहु मोही ॥

rcm.7.4.chaupai.8.m: Then Hanuman bowed at his feet and told all of Raghupati's virtues. 'Tell me, Hanuman: does the kind master ever remember me, as one remembers a servant?'
roles: Depicts him hoping to be remembered only as a servant.
rcm.7.4.chaupai.8.sa: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥

rcm.7.40.chaupai.1.m: They are not greedy for pleasures; they are mines of good conduct and virtue; others' sorrow makes them sad and others' joy makes them glad. They are even-minded, see no one as an enemy, are free of pride and detached, and have let go of greed, rage, elation and fear.
roles: Shows being pained by another's pain.
rcm.7.40.chaupai.1.sa: बिषय अलंपट सील गुनाकर। पर दुख दुख सुख सुख देखे पर॥ सम अभूतरिपु बिमद बिरागी। लोभामरष हरष भय त्यागी ॥

rcm.7.40.chaupai.4.m: Know that whoever carries all these qualities in their heart is truly good. They never waver from self-control, discipline and right conduct, and never speak a harsh word. Praise and blame are the same to them, and their love is for my feet: such good people, homes of virtue and joy, are dear to me as life.
roles: Shows praise and blame received alike.
rcm.7.40.chaupai.4.sa: ए सब लच्छन बसहिं जासु उर। जानेहु तात संत संतत फुर॥ सम दम नियम नीति नहिं डोलहिं। परुष बचन कबहूँ नहिं बोलहिं ॥ निंदा अस्तुति उभय सम ममता मम पद कंज। ते सज्जन मम प्रानप्रिय गुन मंदिर सुख पुंज ॥

rcm.7.41.chaupai.2.m: The hearts of the wicked burn with a special heat: they are always on fire at the sight of someone else's prosperity. Wherever they hear someone being run down, they are delighted, as if they had stumbled on treasure.
roles: Shows the one who gloated at your fall is described exactly.
rcm.7.41.chaupai.2.sa: खलन्ह हृदयँ अति ताप बिसेषी। जरहिं सदा पर संपति देखी॥ जहँ कहुँ निंदा सुनहिं पराई। हरषहिं मनहुँ परी निधि पाई ॥

rcm.7.43.chaupai.1.m: There is no duty equal to doing good to others, brother, and no baseness equal to causing others pain. This is the verdict of all the scriptures; the wise know it.
roles: Shows others' pain as the thing never to cause.
rcm.7.43.chaupai.1.sa: पर हित सरिस धर्म नहिं भाई। पर पीड़ा सम नहिं अधमाई॥ निर्नय सकल पुरान बेद कर। कहेउँ तात जानहिं कोबिद नर ॥

rcm.7.45.chaupai.3.m: "The one who follows my teaching is truly my dear servant. But if I say anything unjust, brothers, put aside your fear and stop me."
rcm.7.45.chaupai.3.sa: सोइ सेवक प्रियतम मम सोई। मम अनुसासन मानै जोई॥ जौं अनीति कछु भाषौं भाई। तौ मोहि बरजहु भय बिसराई ॥

rcm.7.46.chaupai.3.m: Driven always by illusion, surrounded by time, karma, nature and the qualities, the soul wanders; then sometimes, out of compassion, God, a friend without a reason, gives it a human body. The human body is a boat for the ocean of becoming, my grace is the favourable wind, a true teacher is the steady helmsman: you have been given, easily, what is hard to get.
roles: Gives a human birth as a gift given without cause.
rcm.7.46.chaupai.3.sa: फिरत सदा माया कर प्रेरा। काल कर्म सुभाव गुन घेरा॥ कबहुँक करि करुना नर देही। देत ईस बिनु हेतु सनेही ॥ नर तनु भव बारिधि कहुँ बेरो। सन्मुख मरुत अनुग्रह मेरो॥ करनधार सदगुर दृढ़ नावा। दुर्लभ साज सुलभ करि पावा ॥

rcm.7.48.chaupai.1.m: "Tell me, what effort does this path take? No yoga, no sacrifices, no chanting, austerities or fasts. Only a simple nature, a mind without crookedness, and contentment with whatever comes."
rcm.7.48.chaupai.1.sa: कहहु भगति पथ कवन प्रयासा। जोग न मख जप तप उपवासा। सरल सुभाव न मन कुटिलाई। जथा लाभ संतोष सदाई ॥

rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.m: If someone calls himself my servant and still hangs his hopes on others, tell me, what sort of trust is that? Why say more and lengthen the story: it is by this conduct that I am won, brothers.
roles: Shows final reliance placed in the Lord alone.
rcm.7.48.chaupai.2.sa: मोर दास कहाइ नर आसा। करइ तौ कहहु कहा बिस्वासा॥ बहुत कहउँ का कथा बढ़ाई। एहि आचरन बस्य मैं भाई ॥

rcm.7.48.chaupai.3.m: "Holding no grudge and picking no quarrel, with neither craving nor fear, every direction is joyful to him. He starts nothing out of craving for results, clings to no house, wants no honour, is free of wrongdoing and anger, skilled and wise."
roles: Names neither wanting nor fearing anything.
rcm.7.48.chaupai.3.sa: बैर न बिग्रह आस न त्रासा। सुखमय ताहि सदा सब आसा॥ अनारंभ अनिकेत अमानी। अनघ अरोष दच्छ बिग्यानी ॥

rcm.7.6.chaupai.2.m: Though everyone praises Vaikuntha, as the Vedas and Puranas say and the world knows, even that is not as dear to me as Avadhpuri; few know this secret. This lovely city is my birthplace; to its north flows the holy Sarayu, by bathing in which people come to dwell near me without effort.
roles: Shows love for the soil and river one comes from.
rcm.7.6.chaupai.2.sa: जद्यपि सब बैकुंठ बखाना। बेद पुरान बिदित जगु जाना॥ अवधपुरी सम प्रिय नहिं सोऊ। यह प्रसंग जानइ कोउ कोऊ ॥ जन्मभूमि मम पुरी सुहावनि। उत्तर दिसि बह सरजू पावनि॥ जा मज्जन ते बिनहिं प्रयासा। मम समीप नर पावहिं बासा ॥

rcm.7.61.chaupai.2.m: You met me on the road; how can I explain it to you in passing? All doubts end only when one spends a long time in good company.
roles: Trust grows by staying near those who have it.
rcm.7.61.chaupai.2.sa: मिलेहु गरुड़ मारग महँ मोही। कवन भाँति समुझावौं तोही॥ तबहिं होइ सब संसय भंगा। जब बहु काल करिअ सतसंगा ॥

rcm.7.68.chaupai.6.m: Only one scorched by the sun knows the comfort of a tree's shade. Friend, had I not been so deeply confused, how would I ever have met you?
rcm.7.68.chaupai.6.sa: जो अति आतप ब्याकुल होई। तरु छाया सुख जानइ सोई॥ जौं नहिं होत मोह अति मोही। मिलतेउँ तात कवन बिधि तोही ॥

rcm.7.69.chaupai.4.m: Whom has delusion not blinded? Who in the world has desire not made to dance? Whom has craving not maddened? Whose heart has anger not burned?
roles: Shows falling to these forces is the common lot.
rcm.7.69.chaupai.4.sa: मोह न अंध कीन्ह केहि केही। को जग काम नचाव नजेही॥ तृस्नाँ केहि न कीन्ह बौराहा। केहि कर हृदय क्रोध नहिं दाहा ॥

rcm.7.7.chaupai.4.m: Bharat lay on the ground and would not get up when they tried to lift him. The ocean of kindness lifted him by force and held him to his heart. Ram's dark body thrilled, and tears flooded his lotus eyes.
roles: Shows a person unable to raise himself from the ground after fourteen years.
rcm.7.7.chaupai.4.sa: परे भूमि नहिं उठत उठाए। बर करि कृपासिंधु उर लाए॥ स्यामल गात रोम भए ठाढ़े। नव राजीव नयन जल बाढ़े ॥

rcm.7.7.chhand.2.m: When the Lord asked Bharat how he was, no words would come. Shiva says: Parvati, that joy is beyond words and thought; only one who has felt it knows. Bharat said: Now I am well, Lord of Kosala. You saw how I suffered and showed yourself to me. I was drowning in the sea of separation, and you took me by the hand.
roles: Shows joy beyond word and thought.
rcm.7.7.chhand.2.sa: बूझत कृपानिधि कुसल भरतहि बचन बेगि न आवई॥ सुनु सिवा सो सुख बचन मन ते भिन्न जान जो पावई॥ अब कुसल कौसलनाथ आरत जानि जन दरसन दियो। बूड़त बिरह बारीस कृपानिधान मोहि कर गहि लियो ॥

rcm.7.70.chaupai.2.m: Whom has envy not stained? Whom has the wind of grief not shaken? Whom has the snake of worry not bitten? Who in the world has not been caught by illusion?
roles: The snake of worry has bitten everyone.
rcm.7.70.chaupai.2.sa: मच्छर काहि कलंक न लावा। काहि न सोक समीर डोलावा॥ चिंता साँपिनि को नहिं खाया। को जग जाहि न ब्यापी माया ॥

rcm.7.72.chaupai.2.m: When someone's eyes are diseased, he calls the moon yellow; when someone loses his bearings, he says the sun rose in the west. A man on a moving boat sees the world moving and, deluded, thinks himself still. Children spin round, not the houses, yet they call each other liars.
roles: Checking one's own position before judging.
rcm.7.72.chaupai.2.sa: नयन दोष जा कहँ जब होई। पीत बरन ससि कहुँ कह सोई॥ जब जेहि दिसि भ्रम होई खगेसा। सो कह पच्छिम उयउ दिनेसा ॥ नौकारूढ़ चलत जग देखा। अचल मोह बस आपुहि लेखा॥ बालक भ्रमहिं न भ्रमहिं गृहादी। कहहिं परस्पर मिथ्याबादी ॥

scene.s: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.

rcm.7.73.chaupai.3.m: Hear Ram's natural way: he never lets pride stay in his devotee, for pride is the root of the cycle of birth and death, the giver of many pains and of every sorrow.
roles: Shows the removal of pride is the Lord's care.
rcm.7.73.chaupai.3.sa: नहु राम कर सहज सुभाऊ। जन अभिमान न राखहिं काऊ॥ संसृत मूल सूलप्रद नाना। सकल सोक दायक अभिमाना ॥

rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.m: So the merciful one removes it, for he loves his servant deeply. When a boil forms on a child's body, the mother has it lanced as if she were hard-hearted. Though the child suffers at first and cries out, the mother, to cure the illness, pays no heed to that pain.
roles: The hand that hurt was a mother's.
rcm.7.73.chaupai.4.sa: ताते करहिं कृपानिधि दूरी। सेवक पर ममता अति भूरी॥ जिमि सिसु तन ब्रन होई गोसाईं। मातु चिराव कठिन की नाईं ॥ जदपि प्रथम दुख पावइ रोवइ बाल अधीर। ब्याधि नास हित जननी गनति न सो सिसु पीर॥ 74 क॥

scene.s: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.

rcm.7.8.chhand.1.m: Like cows that had to leave their young calves at home to graze in the forest, and at day's end run lowing toward the village, milk flowing, so the mothers ran. With great love the Lord met each of them and spoke many gentle words. The hard pain of separation left them, and they found countless joys.
roles: Shows the hard pain of separation gone and joy countless.
rcm.7.8.chhand.1.sa: जनु धेनु बालक बच्छ तजि गृहँ चरन बन परबस गईं। दिन अंत पुर रुख स्रवत थन हुंकार करि धावत भईं॥ अति प्रेम प्रभु सब मातु भेटीं बचन मृदु बहुबिधि कहे। गइ बिषम बिपति बियोगभव तिन्ह हरष सुख अगनित लहे॥

rcm.7.83.chaupai.3.m: Without devotion, all virtues and pleasures are like many dishes without salt. What use is happiness without devotion? Thinking so, I spoke.
roles: Shows him asking for devotion over every power offered.
rcm.7.83.chaupai.3.sa: भगति हीन गुन सब सुख ऐसे। लवन बिना बहु बिंजन जैसे॥ भजन हीन सुख कवने काजा। अस बिचारि बोलेउँ खगराजा ॥

rcm.7.85.chaupai.5.m: Even Brahma, without devotion, is dear to me only as any being is. A devoted creature, however lowly, is dear to me as life: this is my word.
roles: Shows devotion as the only measure.
rcm.7.85.chaupai.5.sa: भगति हीन बिरंचि किन होई। सब जीवहु सम प्रिय मोहि सोई॥ भगतिवंत अति नीचउ प्रानी। मोहि प्रानप्रिय असि मम बानी ॥

rcm.7.86.chaupai.1.m: One father has many sons, each different in gifts, nature and conduct: one a scholar, one an ascetic, one wise, one rich, one brave, one generous; one all-knowing, one devoted to duty. The father's love is the same for all; but if one is devoted to the father in mind, word and deed, knowing no other duty even in dreams...
roles: Devotion is what draws the Lord closest.
rcm.7.86.chaupai.1.sa: एक पिता के बिपुल कुमारा। होहिं पृथक गुन सील अचारा॥ कोउ पंडित कोउ तापस ग्याता। कोउ धनवंत सूर कोउ दाता ॥ कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥

scene.s: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.

rcm.7.86.chaupai.2.m: One is all-knowing, one devoted to duty; the father loves them all equally. But one son is devoted to his father in word, mind and deed, and in his dreams knows no other duty: that son is dear to his father as life, though he is unskilled in every way. In this same way are all beings, moving and unmoving, gods, humans and demons.
roles: Names single-minded devotion as what the father treasures.
rcm.7.86.chaupai.2.sa: कोउ सर्बग्य धर्मरत कोई। सब पर पितहि प्रीति सम होई॥ कोउ पितु भगत बचन मन कर्मा। सपनेहुँ जान न दूसर धर्मा ॥ सो सुत प्रिय पितु प्रान समाना। जद्यपि सो सब भाँति अयाना॥ एहि बिधि जीव चराचर जेते। त्रिजग देव नर असुर समेते ॥

rcm.7.86.doha.1.m: Man, woman or of any gender, any being that moves or does not move: whoever worships me with all their heart, giving up deceit, is supremely dear to me.
rcm.7.86.doha.1.sa: पुरुष नपुंसक नारि वा जीव चराचर कोइ। सर्ब भाव भज कपट तजि मोहि परम प्रिय सोइ ॥

rcm.7.87.chaupai.4.m: Seeing him, the mother rose anxiously and ran, spoke softly to him and held him to her heart. She kept him in her lap and fed him, singing of Raghupati's lovely deeds.
roles: The ordinary tenderness of holding a crying child.
rcm.7.87.chaupai.4.sa: देखि मातु आतुर उठि धाई। कहि मृदु बचन लिए उर लाई॥ गोद राखि कराव पय पाना। रघुपति चरित ललित कर गाना ॥

rcm.7.87.chaupai.8.m: Without knowing his greatness, no trust forms; without trust, no love; and without love, devotion is not firm, just as, king of birds, oil does not stay on water.
roles: Names knowing as the first step so asking is right.
rcm.7.87.chaupai.8.sa: जानें बिनु न होइ परतीती। बिनु परतीति होइ नहिं प्रीती॥ प्रीति बिना नहिं भगति दिढ़ाई। जिमि खगपति जल कै चिकनाई ॥

rcm.7.87.sortha.5.m: Can anyone find rest without natural contentment, friend? Can a boat move without water, though you strain and wear yourself out with a million efforts?
roles: Names contentment as the water the boat needs.
rcm.7.87.sortha.5.sa: कोउ बिश्राम कि पाव तात सहज संतोष बिनु। चलै कि जल बिनु नाव कोटि जतन पचि पचि मरिअ ॥

rcm.7.95.chaupai.4.m: The teacher who takes his disciple's money but not his sorrow falls into a terrible hell. Parents call their children and teach them only the dharma that fills the belly.
roles: Names asking what one is really passing on to a child.
rcm.7.95.chaupai.4.sa: हरइ सिष्य धन सोक न हरई। सो गुर घोर नरक महुँ परई॥ मातु पिता बालकन्हि बोलावहिं। उदर भरै सोइ धर्म सिखावहिं ॥

scene.s: Kakbhushundi, describing a degraded age, on what teachers and parents pass on.

st.rcm.angad_asks_to_stay.l: Friendships made in hard times deserve to be kept; say so out loud.
st.rcm.angad_asks_to_stay.s: After six happy months, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends home with gifts. Angad, whose father is dead, begs to stay: Ram is his father and mother now. Ram embraces him and sends him on. To the boatman Guha he says: you are a brother to me; keep visiting.
st.rcm.angad_asks_to_stay.t: Ram says goodbye to his friends

st.rcm.angad_the_envoy.l: Under insult, keep your purpose; a steady mind does not leave what is right.
st.rcm.angad_the_envoy.s: Ram sends Angad as envoy, asking him to speak so the work gets done and it does Ravana good too. In court Ravana insults Angad, his dead father and his lord. Angad bears it, remembering that a lion gains no glory by killing a jackal. At last he plants his foot and dares anyone to move it; no warrior can.

st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.l: You can live amid plenty without being owned by it.
st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.s: Bharat places Ram's sandals on the throne and lives outside the city in a hut, sleeping on grass, fasting, governing only as a caretaker. The palace's riches are all around him and do not touch him, like a bee in a champak garden.
st.rcm.bharat_and_the_sandals.t: Bharat rules from a hut for fourteen years

st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.l: You are not your family's mistakes; carry only what is yours.
st.rcm.bharat_at_prayag.s: At Prayag Bharat meets the sage Bharadwaj, too ashamed to speak. The sage tells him not to eat himself up over his mother's deed and that what Bharat sees as a stain is a lesson for everyone. Bharat answers that he fears neither the world's talk nor the afterlife; only the thought that Ram suffers because of him keeps him awake.

st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.l: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.
st.rcm.bharat_comes_home_to_blame.s: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.

st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.l: Forgiveness can mean going first to the person who hurt you and putting them at ease.
st.rcm.bharat_dread_on_the_road.s: Bharat walks barefoot to Chitrakoot and falls at Ram's feet; Ram lifts him into his arms. Ram learns his father has died and grieves. When the queens arrive, Ram goes first to Kaikeyi, who caused it all, falls at her feet and comforts her, blaming no one.

st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.l: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.
st.rcm.bharat_refuses_the_throne.s: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.

st.rcm.chitrakoot_sabha.l: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.
st.rcm.chitrakoot_sabha.s: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.

st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.l: Parents protect children best by letting them go when the time comes.
st.rcm.dasharath_lets_his_sons_go.s: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharath to send the teenage Ram and Lakshman to protect his forest rites from demons. Dasharath, who had his sons late in life, offers land, cows, treasure, even his own life instead. Vasishtha reasons with him, and he finally embraces the boys and hands them over.

st.rcm.dharma_rath.l: Inner qualities are the real equipment for a hard fight.
st.rcm.dharma_rath.s: Ravana rides out in a chariot; Ram stands on foot, and Vibhishan worries. Ram describes the chariot that really wins: courage and patience as its wheels, truth and character as its flag, strength, judgement, self-control and kindness as its horses.

st.rcm.garuda_doubts_after_rescue.l: Doubt is human; stay long enough in good company and it can lead somewhere better.
st.rcm.garuda_doubts_after_rescue.s: Garuda, Vishnu's own mount, frees Ram from a serpent-noose in battle and starts to doubt: how can God be bound? He goes to Narada, Brahma and Shiva, who sends him to an old crow, Kakbhushundi, saying doubts clear only with long time in good company. Kakbhushundi tells him no one has escaped delusion, desire, craving or anger; Garuda ends up grateful for the doubt that led him there.

st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.l: Find out someone's intent before you prepare for war with them.
st.rcm.guha_assumes_the_worst.s: Seeing Bharat's army approach the Ganga, Guha assumes he is coming to kill Ram and prepares his men to die fighting. An old man reads the omens and says Bharat comes to bring Ram back. Guha agrees that fools act in haste and repent, goes to meet Bharat with gifts, and the two embrace.

st.rcm.hanuman_bound_before_ravana.l: Speak truth to power calmly, and afterwards don't take the credit.
st.rcm.hanuman_bound_before_ravana.s: Bound and dragged before Ravana, Hanuman feels no shame and tells the most powerful man in the world, calmly, to return Sita: wealth with no deep source dries up like a rain-fed river. Ravana orders his tail set on fire; Hanuman burns Lanka and returns. Back before Ram, he insists none of it was his own greatness.

st.rcm.hanuman_forgot_his_master.l: You don't need the right method; being his is enough, and he weeps to have you back.
st.rcm.hanuman_forgot_his_master.s: Sent by a frightened Sugriva, Hanuman goes disguised as a brahmin to question two strangers. When Ram names himself, Hanuman recognises his Lord, falls at his feet speechless, then gently complains that Ram forgot him. He says he knows no method of worship and relies on Ram as a child relies on its mother. Ram lifts him up, holds him, cools him with his own tears, and tells him he is twice as dear as Lakshman.

st.rcm.hanuman_gives_the_credit_away.l: Do the work, give away the credit, and ask only to keep loving.
st.rcm.hanuman_gives_the_credit_away.s: Back from Lanka, Hanuman tells Ram how Sita survives: his name guards her day and night. Ram, in tears, asks whether one who relies on him can meet calamity; Hanuman answers that the only calamity is forgetting him. Ram says he can never repay Hanuman and cannot even look him in the face; Hanuman falls at his feet and will not get up. Offered anything, he asks only for unwavering devotion, and credits every deed to Ram.

st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.l: Meet obstacles with flexibility: sometimes bigger, sometimes smaller, never stuck.
st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.s: Leaping the ocean, Hanuman refuses to rest on a friendly mountain until the work is done. Surasa blocks him and opens her jaws; he doubles his size each time she widens them, then shrinks tiny and slips in and out. A demon that catches flyers by grabbing their shadows tries the same trick, and he sees through it at once.
st.rcm.hanuman_no_rest_and_surasa.t: Hanuman meets Surasa on the way

st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.l: Your fear of someone else's goodness usually says more about your interests than theirs.
st.rcm.indra_afraid_of_bharat.s: Indra, king of the gods, fears that Bharat's devotion will bring Ram back and spoil the gods' plans, and wants to trick him. His teacher Brihaspati tells him that the world runs on action, that harming a good person backfires, and that his anxiety comes from his own self-interest, not from Bharat.

st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.l: Sometimes we need someone else to remind us what we can do; and the old can be that someone.
st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.s: Nobody can leap the ocean. Old Jambavant admits honestly that he is no longer young. Then he turns to the silent Hanuman and asks why he sits quiet: what task in the world is too hard for him? Hanuman grows to the size of a mountain.
st.rcm.jambavan_why_so_silent.t: Jambavant reminds Hanuman of his strength

st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.l: Some moments do not wait; when it is time, act.
st.rcm.janak_despair_lakshman_stung.s: Ten thousand kings fail to lift Shiva's bow, and Janaka cries out that the earth has no heroes left. Lakshman bristles; Vishwamitra sends Ram forward. Ram sees Sita's anguish, knows that rain after the crops have dried is useless, lifts the bow and breaks it in a moment.

st.rcm.janak_vidai.l: Even the wisest parent breaks a little when a child leaves home; that is love.
st.rcm.janak_vidai.s: After the wedding the time comes for Sita to leave Mithila. The palace, even the pet parrots, are in tears. Janaka, known everywhere for his detachment, holds his daughter and loses all composure; his ministers have to remind him it is time.
st.rcm.janak_vidai.t: Janaka says goodbye to his daughter

st.rcm.jatayu_old_and_outmatched.l: Nothing you do for love is small; it is honoured like family.
st.rcm.jatayu_old_and_outmatched.s: Searching for Sita, Ram finds the old vulture who fought Ravana to save her, dying. Ram touches his head and the bird's pain leaves. Jatayu refuses Ram's offer to heal him: the one whose name people pray to say at death is in front of his eyes. He asks only for devotion, and Ram, in tears, performs his last rites with his own hands.

st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.l: Consequences may remain, but the one who turns back is still taken in.
st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.s: Indra's son, disguised as a crow, pecks Sita's foot to test Ram's power. Ram's straw arrow chases him through every world; no god will shelter him. Narada sends him back to Ram, where he falls at his feet admitting he reaped what he sowed. Ram lets him go with the loss of one eye.
st.rcm.jayant_no_shelter.t: Jayant the crow: shelter for the offender

st.rcm.kakbhushundi_cursed_and_glad.l: Even calm people burn when pushed too far; take correction without bitterness.
st.rcm.kakbhushundi_cursed_and_glad.s: As a young seeker Kakbhushundi went to the sage Lomash, who taught the formless God; Kakbhushundi kept arguing for his own view until the sage, provoked again and again, lost his temper and cursed him to become a crow. Kakbhushundi took it without fear or self-pity, and the sage, regretting his anger, called him back and taught him the Ramcharitmanas.

st.rcm.kakbhushundi_doubts_the_toddler.l: Pride is taken from us painfully, for our good; what remains is what matters.
st.rcm.kakbhushundi_doubts_the_toddler.s: Kakbhushundi used to visit Ayodhya to watch Ram as a child. Once he doubted that a toddler chasing a crow could be God; Ram reached for him across every world, and he saw universes inside the child's mouth. Humbled, he was offered every power and chose devotion, since comforts without it are a feast without salt. Ram explains that pride is lanced from those he loves, as a mother lances a child's boil.

st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.l: Even the one who hurt you can be approached; compassion answers grief.
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.s: Kama, sent by the gods to break Shiva's meditation, is burned by his third eye. His wife Rati, fainting and weeping, goes straight to Shiva and pleads. Shiva, quick to be pleased and compassionate, promises her that Kama will live on without a body and that she will meet him again when Krishna is born.
st.rcm.kamadeva_goes_knowing.t: Rati comes weeping to the god who burned her husband

st.rcm.kaushalya_and_sunayana.l: When you are too close to a decision, say so, and speak briefly and honestly.
st.rcm.kaushalya_and_sunayana.s: Sita's parents arrive and the two families grieve together. Kausalya tells Sunayana that people, like gold, are proved by time. Janaka asks Bharat to decide, and Bharat declines: duty and self-interest pull apart, hatred is blind and love cannot reason, so he will follow Ram's wish. His few words leave the whole court in awe.

st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.l: Letting a child go with your blessing is love at its hardest.
st.rcm.kaushalya_cannot_say_go_or_stay.s: Ram comes to his mother as she is preparing for his coronation. Torn between duty and love, she decides not to hold him back with 'false affection', blesses him and asks only that he not forget her. As he leaves she wonders aloud whether she will live to see his face again.

st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.l: When someone is drowning in guilt for what others did, an embrace helps more than blame.
st.rcm.kaushalya_embraces_bharat.s: Bharat returns from his uncle's home to a silent city. His mother tells him proudly what she arranged; he learns his father is dead and his brother exiled because of him. Overwhelmed with shame he goes to Kausalya, expecting blame, and she embraces him as if Ram had come back, telling him not to carry the loss as his shame.

st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.l: The grandest thing about a child may be the ordinary hours of childhood itself.
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.s: At his birth Ram shows Kausalya his cosmic form, and she asks him instead to be simply a baby. Later scenes are pure childhood: the boy runs off mid-meal, curd on his face, dusty from play, while his father laughs and his mother chases him. When she once glimpses the whole universe in him again, she asks only to be spared that and keep her child.
st.rcm.kaushalya_two_children.t: Kausalya and the child who ran from dinner

st.rcm.kevat_bargains.l: Some exchanges can't be priced; gratitude can be payment enough.
st.rcm.kevat_bargains.s: At the Ganga, a boatman refuses to take Ram across until he can wash his feet, joking that if the dust of those feet turned a stone into a woman, it might turn his boat, his family's livelihood, into one too. Ram laughs and agrees. On the far bank Sita offers her ring as fare, and Kevat refuses: after a lifetime of wages, today he has been paid in full.

st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.l: Siblings can choose differently and still bless each other.
st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.s: Woken to fight, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana plainly he was wrong to take Sita and should have consulted him first. Still he goes out to fight for his brother. On the field he meets Vibhishan, who chose Ram, and instead of cursing him, he blesses him as the pride of their family.
st.rcm.kumbhakarna_tells_his_brother.t: Kumbhakarna fights for a brother he knows is wrong

st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.l: Think before you act on an assumption; haste turns misunderstandings into wars.
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.s: Forest dwellers report that Bharat is coming with an army. Lakshman, sure it is an attack, climbs a tree and swears to destroy him. A voice from the sky warns against acting in haste, and Ram explains that Bharat could never turn against him; power could not corrupt him.
st.rcm.lakshman_assumes_bharat_attacks.t: Lakshman assumes the worst about Bharat

st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.l: Before blaming someone for your pain, look at the whole chain of causes, including yourself.
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.s: On the first night of exile, Guha the boatmen's chief sees Ram and Sita sleeping on grass and weeps with anger at Kaikeyi. Lakshman, keeping watch, tells him no one gives us joy or sorrow; we live out our own actions, so don't blame anyone needlessly.
st.rcm.lakshman_tells_guha_not_to_blame.t: Lakshman and Guha by the sleeping Ram

st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.l: Carry what you love into the hard place, and the hard place changes.
st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.s: Entering Lanka at night as small as a mosquito, Hanuman is caught by Lankini, the city's guardian. One blow of his fist floors her; she remembers a prophecy that this means the city's end, and blesses him: a moment of good company outweighs heaven, and if he carries Ram in his heart, poison will turn to nectar.
st.rcm.lankini_struck_awake.t: Lankini at the gate of Lanka

st.rcm.manas_rog.l: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.
st.rcm.manas_rog.s: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.

st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.l: It is not too late to turn towards what matters, but it takes courage to ask for it.
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.s: King Manu and Queen Shatarupa realise in old age that a whole life has passed without what mattered most to them. They hand over the kingdom, go to the forest and practise austerity for years. When Vishnu offers a boon, Manu hesitates like a poor man before the wishing tree, then asks for a son like God himself.
st.rcm.manu_shatarupa_late_turn.t: Manu and Shatarupa ask late in life

st.rcm.maricha_two_deaths.l: A boss who threatens you into wrongdoing leaves no good option; see it early.
st.rcm.maricha_two_deaths.s: Ravana orders his uncle Maricha to become a golden deer to lure Ram away. Maricha warns him that Ram cannot be defeated, but Ravana threatens him. Seeing death either way, Maricha reasons that it never pays to cross a powerful master, and chooses death at Ram's hands over death at Ravana's.

st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.l: The moment you boast of beating a weakness, it has found another way in.
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.s: Narada conquers desire in meditation and cannot stop telling people about it. Vishnu creates a city and a princess's swayamvara; Narada falls for her and asks Vishnu for a beautiful face. Vishnu, like a doctor refusing harmful food, gives him a monkey's face instead, and Narada is laughed out of the hall until he sees what his pride has done.
st.rcm.narad_pride_after_victory.t: Narada's pride and the monkey face

st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.l: Clever replies feed anger; calm, humble words put it out.
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.s: Parashurama storms into the wedding hall furious that Shiva's bow is broken. Lakshman answers every threat with a joke, and each reply feeds the fire. Ram steps in with soft words, takes the blame on himself, and calmly points out that an old bow broke at a touch; the sage's anger finally turns to recognition.
st.rcm.parashuram_rage_met_two_ways.t: Parashurama's rage, Lakshman's taunts, Ram's calm

st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.l: Honest doubt, asked with love, is met with patience, not blame.
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.s: On Kailash, Parvati sits beside Shiva and, still carrying her old doubt from her life as Sati, asks how a grieving prince can be God. Shiva is moved to tears, reassures her that there is no doubt left in her heart, and explains that the formless becomes form out of love for devotees. Her confusion lifts 'like autumn heat under moonlight'.
st.rcm.parvati_asks_openly.t: Parvati asks, and Shiva answers with reassurance

st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.l: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
st.rcm.parvati_holds_her_choice.s: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.

st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.l: Always ask humbly first. But don't let humility be taken for weakness.
st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.s: On Vibhishan's advice, Ram first asks the ocean politely to let his army cross, and waits three days. When nothing changes, he takes up his bow, observing that counsel to the unwilling is like seed on barren soil. The ocean appears, apologises, and shows him how to build a bridge.
st.rcm.ram_and_the_ocean.t: Three days at the ocean: humble first, firm after

st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.l: Standing up for someone matters, even when you cannot win.
st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.s: Ram returns to an empty hut and searches the forest, asking birds and trees if they have seen Sita. He finds the old vulture Jatayu dying; he had fought Ravana alone to stop the abduction. Ram tells him that for one whose heart is set on others' good, nothing is out of reach, and performs his funeral rites himself, as a son would.
st.rcm.ram_asks_the_trees.t: Jatayu's last fight and Ram's grief

st.rcm.ram_asks_to_be_corrected.l: A good leader invites correction; a good life is simple, honest and free of grudges.
st.rcm.ram_asks_to_be_corrected.s: Ram calls his people together and says he speaks without pride of rank: if he says anything wrong, stop him without fear. The way he recommends needs no grand effort, only a simple nature, an honest mind, contentment, and no grudges, no quarrels, no craving and no fear.

st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.l: A lost role can be met with grace; sometimes it even feels like freedom.
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.s: Ram is called to his father's room and finds him collapsed. Kaikeyi tells him the terms. Ram smiles: his brother gets the throne, he gets to meet sages in the forest, and he can keep his father's word. Kaikeyi reads his plain words as cunning, and Ram walks out feeling, the poet says, like an elephant freed from its post.
st.rcm.ram_hears_of_exile.t: Ram hears he is to be exiled

st.rcm.ram_hurries_home.l: When someone at home is waiting, no comfort elsewhere can hold you.
st.rcm.ram_hurries_home.s: After the war, Vibhishan begs Ram to stay a while, bathe and rest in Lanka's palaces. Ram says all of it is his as much as Vibhishan's, but thinking of Bharat waiting at home, each moment feels like an age; if he is late, he may not find his brother alive.

st.rcm.ram_message_no_one_to_tell.l: When someone is near despair, a message that they are remembered can carry them.
st.rcm.ram_message_no_one_to_tell.s: Sita, captive and threatened by Ravana, has nearly lost hope; only the guard Trijata has been kind. Hanuman drops Ram's ring from a tree, then tells her Ram's whole story. Sita says he has been her ship in a sea of separation; he gives her Ram's message that speaking of pain helps, but there is no one to tell, and asks her to wait a few days more.

st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.l: Real affection for siblings feels uneasy when one is favoured over the rest.
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.s: Dasharath, noticing grey hairs, decides to crown Ram heir, and the whole city celebrates. When Vasishtha brings Ram the news, Ram's first thought is not joy but unease: the brothers were born, raised and married together, so why should only the eldest be crowned?
st.rcm.ram_uneasy_at_being_singled_out.t: Ram's unease on the eve of his crowning

st.rcm.ram_waits_out_the_rains.l: Nature keeps teaching: steadiness, humility, patience, and saving for the dry season.
st.rcm.ram_waits_out_the_rains.s: Waiting out the rains on a mountain, Ram points out lessons to Lakshman in each sight: clouds bow low when full, mountains take the rain as the steady take harsh words, small streams swagger, ponds fill drop by drop, autumn sun dries the puddles as contentment dries greed, and fish panic as the water shrinks.

st.rcm.sampati_wings_regrow.l: Even after the fall your pride caused, you can still be useful, and hope can return.
st.rcm.sampati_wings_regrow.s: The search party, past its deadline with no news, sits down by the sea to die. A huge old vulture, Sampati, overhears them talking of his brother Jatayu. He tells them how pride once made him fly too close to the sun and burn his wings; a sage told him they would grow back when he helped Ram's messengers. He tells them where Sita is, and his wings grow back as he speaks.

st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.l: Grief and devotion can walk together; steady love in loss is seen.
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.s: After Sati is gone, Shiva wanders, teaching and singing of Ram, repeating his name. Though beyond desire, he still grieves the loss of his devotee. Seeing his steady love, Ram appears, grateful and kind, praises Shiva's vow and asks him to marry Parvati.
st.rcm.shiva_grief_turns_to_name.t: Shiva's grief turns to Ram's name

st.rcm.student_who_would_not_rise.l: Respect those who teach you; and forgive like the teacher who prayed for his rude student.
st.rcm.student_who_would_not_rise.s: In an earlier life Kakbhushundi was a proud, wealthy, sharp-tongued young man whose gentle teacher kept trying to guide him. One day in the temple he refused even to rise when the teacher entered. The teacher said nothing, but a curse fell on the student; the teacher at once prayed for him, asking that he not be punished in anger. Lives later, the one thorn Kakbhushundi still carries is the memory of that teacher's gentleness.
st.rcm.student_who_would_not_rise.t: The student who would not stand for his teacher

st.rcm.sugriva_forgets_his_friend.l: Success and comfort make us forget who helped us; admit it quickly and make it right.
st.rcm.sugriva_forgets_his_friend.s: The rains end and Sugriva, now king, has forgotten his promise to search for Sita. Ram is hurt; Lakshman storms into the city in anger. Hanuman had already nudged Sugriva, who comes out, admits that comfort intoxicated him, and sends search parties in every direction.

st.rcm.sugriva_what_a_friend_is.l: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.
st.rcm.sugriva_what_a_friend_is.s: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.

st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.l: Home is where your people are; a good send-off gives values, not just tears.
st.rcm.sumitra_sends_lakshman.s: Ram asks Lakshman to stay and care for their old father and grieving mothers; Lakshman cannot imagine life apart from him. He goes to his mother Sumitra, afraid she will stop him. Instead she tells him that home is wherever Ram is, as day is wherever the sun shines, and gives him one piece of advice for the road.

st.rcm.sutikshna_too_unworthy_to_hope.l: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.
st.rcm.sutikshna_too_unworthy_to_hope.s: A young sage hears Ram is near and runs out, sure he has no devotion, wisdom or discipline worth anything, trusting only that Ram loves those with nowhere else to go. Lost in love he wanders, dances, forgets the way; Ram watches from behind a tree, then lifts him up and holds him. Asked for a boon, the sage says only: may this one pride never leave me, that I am his.

st.rcm.tara_consoled.l: Grief needs time; later, perspective on what is lost and what endures can comfort.
st.rcm.tara_consoled.s: After Bali's death his wife Tara weeps over his body. Ram speaks to her gently: the body is made of five elements and lies here before her, but the self is not only this body; for whom is she weeping? Comforted, she asks for devotion, and Bali's son Angad is made heir.

st.rcm.trijata_the_one_kind_guard.l: When someone is near despair, a message that they are remembered can carry them.
st.rcm.trijata_the_one_kind_guard.s: Sita, captive and threatened by Ravana, has nearly lost hope; only the guard Trijata has been kind. Hanuman drops Ram's ring from a tree, then tells her Ram's whole story. Sita says he has been her ship in a sea of separation; he gives her Ram's message that speaking of pain helps, but there is no one to tell, and asks her to wait a few days more.

st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.l: Notice whether you can be glad at someone else's good work, not only your own.
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.s: Tulsidas calls his own poetry plain and asks readers to forgive it. Along the way he notes that everyone loves their own work, that few are glad at another's success, and that most people swell only with their own rising waters.
st.rcm.tulsi_begins_feeling_unequal.t: Tulsidas on loving our own work

st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.l: The people around you shape your judgement; choose them, and take the good from everyone.
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.s: Before the story begins, Tulsidas bows to good people and, with gentle irony, to troublesome ones too. He describes how each acts, why company shapes us, and how the wise take the good and leave the rest, like the swan taking milk from water.
st.rcm.tulsi_bows_to_detractors.t: Tulsidas on good company and difficult people

st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.l: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.
st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.s: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
st.rcm.vibhishan_kicked_for_counsel.t: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked

st.rcm.vibhishan_refuge_debate.l: Leaving a bad place takes courage; a good leader receives people without suspicion first.
st.rcm.vibhishan_refuge_debate.s: Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram. Sugriva suspects a spy; Ram says he never turns away anyone who comes for refuge, and that only a clean heart, without deceit, reaches him. He embraces Vibhishan, asks how he kept his goodness among the wicked, and crowns him king of Lanka before the war has even begun.

st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.l: Even in a hostile place there may be one ally; find them.
st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.s: Searching Lanka, Hanuman is surprised to find a house with Ram's name on it. Its owner, Vibhishan, Ravana's brother, says he lives in Lanka like a tongue among teeth. Hanuman tells him even a restless monkey like himself was given Ram's love.
st.rcm.vibhishan_tongue_among_teeth.t: Hanuman finds a friend in Lanka

st.vr.bhagiratha_finishes_what_three_gen.l: Some goals take longer than one effort or one lifetime; keep going and others' work is not wasted.
st.vr.bhagiratha_finishes_what_three_gen.s: King Sagara's sixty thousand sons are burnt to ash; only the Ganga's water can free them. Sagara, his grandson Anshuman and Anshuman's son Dilipa each try and die without success. Bhagiratha finally persists until the river descends, and Brahma honours him for finishing what three generations began.

st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.l: Grief and rage come together; one calm person can stop a moment we'd regret forever.
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.s: The brothers perform their father's rites and collapse in grief; the family priest lifts them up. When Shatrughna drags Manthara before him in rage, Bharata stops him: Ram would never forgive cruelty done in his name.
st.vr.bharata_collapses_at_the_pyre.t: At the pyre, and the hand that stopped

st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.l: Missing a parent's death far from home is its own grief; let yourself feel it.
st.vr.bharata_comes_home_too_late.s: Bharata, living at his uncle's court, has a nightmare and is summoned home. He finds the city silent and learns from his mother that his father has died while he was away, and then that Ram is in exile because of her.

st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.l: Not every gain is worth taking; integrity sometimes means refusing what you are handed.
st.vr.bharata_refuses_the_throne.s: The court offers Bharata the kingdom his mother won for him. He refuses before the whole assembly, says it belongs to his brother, and sets out with the army and the city to bring Ram back.

st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.l: Faithful waiting is rewarded; return what was entrusted to you, and more.
st.vr.bharata_returns_what_he_held_in_tr.s: Hanuman finds Bharata thin, in bark clothes, still waiting. Hearing Ram is near, Bharata faints with joy: a person who stays alive will find joy, even after a hundred years. He places the sandals back on Ram's feet and hands back the kingdom he kept in trust, now ten times richer.

st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.l: Waiting can be active: keep faith by taking care of what was entrusted to you.
st.vr.bharata_rules_from_nandigram.s: Bharata refuses to live in the palace. From a village hut he governs in the name of Ram's sandals, dressed as an ascetic, holding everything in trust and waiting fourteen years for his brother.

st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.l: Prepare if you must, but find out someone's intent before you judge them.
st.vr.bharata_sees_rams_grass_bed.s: Ram's friend Guha sees Bharata's army and assumes he has come to kill Ram. He prepares to block the river but goes to meet him first. Learning Bharata's intent, he becomes his guide and shows him the grass bed where Ram slept, where Bharata vows to live as an ascetic until Ram returns.

st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.l: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.
st.vr.bharata_suspected_by_everyone.s: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.

st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.l: Carelessness can wound for decades; owning it honestly is the only way to carry it.
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.s: Dying of grief, Dasharatha confesses to Kausalya that as a young prince he shot at a sound in the dark and killed a boy filling water for his blind, aged parents. He took the water to them and told them the truth himself. The father cursed him to lose a son as they had, and now, longing for Ram, the king dies at midnight.
st.vr.dasharatha_and_the_boy_at_the_rive.t: The boy at the river: Dasharatha's old guilt

st.vr.dasharatha_lets_ram_go_with_vishva.l: Letting a child go out into the world can be the most loving thing a parent does.
st.vr.dasharatha_lets_ram_go_with_vishva.s: The sage Vishvamitra asks the king for his teenage son Ram to protect a ritual. Dasharatha, who waited years for a child, refuses and offers himself and his army instead. His guru reminds him of his word and that the sage asks for Ram's own growth, and the king lets him go.

st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.l: Goodbyes to ageing parents are hard; leave with love and a promise to return.
st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.s: The broken king begs Ram to stay one more night so his parents can see him. Ram gently refuses, saying a promise made must be kept and he will return in fourteen years. Dasharatha embraces him and collapses.
st.vr.dasharatha_one_more_night.t: One more night: Ram leaves his father

st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.l: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
st.vr.hanuman_and_surasa.s: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.

st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.l: Gratitude and focus can go together; know when to be big and when to be small.
st.vr.hanuman_declines_the_resting_mount.s: Hanuman leaps across the ocean. A mountain rises to repay an old kindness by offering rest; he thanks it but keeps his promise not to stop. He outwits Surasa by shrinking small and defeats Simhika, and the watching beings praise his steadiness, sight, judgement and skill.

st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.l: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.
st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.s: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
st.vr.hanuman_first_words_to_ram.t: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words

st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.l: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.s: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.
st.vr.hanuman_lets_himself_be_caught.t: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka

st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.l: Before a hard conversation, think about how the other person will hear you.
st.vr.hanuman_plans_how_to_approach_her.s: Hanuman has found Sita but she is terrified. He thinks carefully: speak in ordinary language, not court Sanskrit; don't gamble on a fight; start by gently praising Ram so she can trust him. He sings Ram's story softly from the tree, and she hears hope for the first time: joy comes to the one who stays alive.

st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.l: Comfort makes us forget our promises; a true friend reminds us in time.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_his_king_the_truth.s: Restored to his throne, Sugriva sinks into pleasure and forgets his promise to search for Sita. Hanuman warns him that help given late counts for little. Autumn comes; angry, Ram sends Lakshman, and Hanuman counsels the frightened Sugriva to bear harsh words and keep faith.

st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.l: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.s: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.
st.vr.hanuman_tells_ravana_the_truth.t: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka

st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.l: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.
st.vr.hanuman_weeps_when_he_finds_her.s: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.

st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.l: Doubt deserves a hearing; answer it with how you choose to live.
st.vr.jabali_tells_ram_to_be_practical.s: The priest Jabali argues that nobody belongs to anyone, rituals are empty and only the present matters, so Ram should take the throne. Ram answers that conduct, not claims, shows who we are, and that people follow the example of those who lead.

st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.l: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.
st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.s: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
st.vr.jambavan_admits_he_is_old.t: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is

st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.l: Sometimes you need someone to remind you what you are capable of.
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.s: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
st.vr.jambavan_wakes_hanuman.t: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is

st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.l: Age is no reason to stop standing up for what's right; honour those who stood up for you.
st.vr.jatayu_fights_knowing_he_will_lose.s: The aged vulture Jatayu wakes to see Ravana carrying Sita off. He warns him, then fights him alone and is mortally wounded. Later Ram finds him dying, hears his news, and cremates him with the honour due a father.

st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.l: When you are lost, look for someone who has been through the same thing.
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.s: Freed from a curse, the creature Kabandha tells the grieving brothers to seek out Sugriva, an exile who has also lost his wife and home. Only a friend in the same trouble, he says, can help them now.
st.vr.kabandha_find_one_who_has_lost_the.t: Kabandha: find a friend who understands

st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.l: Love sometimes means staying behind to care for someone else.
st.vr.kausalya_blesses_the_road.s: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.

st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.l: Grief makes us wound those we love; apologising quickly heals more than being right.
st.vr.kausalya_lashes_out_then_apologise.s: In her grief Kausalya lashes out at her husband for exiling their son. When he folds his hands and asks her forgiveness, she is horrified, apologises, and explains that grief made her speak.

st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.l: You can tell family the hard truth and still stand by them; humility does, boasting talks.
st.vr.kumbhakarna_tells_the_truth_then_f.s: Woken from months of sleep, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana bluntly that his pride caused this disaster and he acted in the wrong order. Then, loyal to his brother, he goes out to fight anyway, scorning boastful courtiers: the brave don't praise themselves, they act.

st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.l: Home is the people you are with; you can carry it into any wilderness.
st.vr.lakshman_chooses_to_serve.s: As the exiles leave, Lakshman's mother blesses him: treat Ram as your father, Sita as your mother, and the forest as home. She tells him to go happily.

st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.l: Anger at injustice is natural; decide what to do with it before it decides for you.
st.vr.lakshman_fury_for_ram.s: Lakshman is enraged by the injustice and wants to seize the throne by force. Ram calms him: set aside the insult, don't torment yourself, the setback may lead somewhere better. Lakshman answers that effort, not fate, decides; both views are given their due.

st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.l: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
st.vr.lakshman_holds_up_his_elder_brothe.s: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.l: Don't assume the worst of family on the strength of what you see from a distance.
st.vr.lakshman_suspects_bharata.s: From a tree at Chitrakoot, Lakshman sees Bharata's army and is sure he has come to finish them. Ram stops him: Bharata has never wronged us; why suspect him now? And no kingdom is worth winning through wrong.

st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.l: Listen hardest to the advice you least want to hear.
st.vr.maricha_tells_the_truth_then_obeys.s: Ravana asks Maricha to help him abduct Sita. Maricha, who has met Ram before, warns him again and again: flatterers are many, truth-tellers rare, and those heading for a fall reject good advice. Ravana threatens him until he agrees.

st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.l: You cannot control the news; you can control the person who walks out of the room.
st.vr.ram_accepts_exile.s: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.

st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.l: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.s: Ram lies on kusha grass by the shore for three days, asking the ocean for a way. Ignored, he tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness and takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way (Nala's bridge), and Ram releases the arrow elsewhere at its request.
st.vr.ram_asks_the_ocean_then_lifts_the_.t: Ram at the ocean: humble first, firm after

st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.l: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
st.vr.ram_blames_lakshman_in_panic.s: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.l: When someone you love is gravely ill, remember what they mean to you, and do what can be done.
st.vr.ram_cannot_fight_with_lakshman_dow.s: Ravana's spear fells Lakshman. Ram breaks down: even victory means nothing without his brother, who comforted him in every low moment. The physician Sushena sees Lakshman still breathes and sends Hanuman for the healing herbs; Hanuman brings back the mountain peak.

st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.l: Homecoming is about people, not possessions; don't let property come between siblings.
st.vr.ram_checks_if_bharata_wants_the_th.s: Victorious, Ram refuses Lanka's honours: his heart is in a hurry to see Bharata. Near Ayodhya he sends Hanuman ahead to read Bharata's face, saying if Bharata now wants the kingdom, let him keep it.

st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.l: Everything that comes together parts; let that make you gentler, not hopeless.
st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.s: Bharata begs Ram to return and rule. Ram answers with a teaching on impermanence: everything gathered runs out, everything rising falls, people meet like logs on the ocean and drift apart. Grieve, but do not let grief overturn your duty.
st.vr.ram_consoles_bharata_on_impermanen.t: Ram on why grief must not rule us

st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.l: Grief for a loyal friend, even a bird, is real grief; honour it fully.
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.s: Jatayu dies telling Ram where Ravana went. Ram says this loss weighs on him more than Sita's abduction, that the bird is as worthy of honour as his father Dasharatha, builds the pyre himself and performs the rites as for his own kin.
st.vr.ram_cremates_jatayu.t: Valmiki: Ram cremates Jatayu like his father

st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.l: Leaders who change their minds on good advice earn more trust, not less.
st.vr.ram_drops_his_plan_on_bharatas_adv.s: Ram proposes a great imperial sacrifice. Bharata gently objects that it would bring suffering to many kings and people. Ram listens and changes course, saying good advice should be taken even from the young.

st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.l: Delay is a decision too; people waiting on you are paying for it.
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.s: After four days of neglecting his work, Ram calls in everyone waiting, and tells of King Nriga: two men brought him a dispute, waited for days at his gate and were never admitted, and their anger cost him dearly.
st.vr.ram_four_days_away_from_his_people.t: King Nriga and the petitioners who waited

st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.l: Beauty can sharpen grief; a friend can remind you of your own strength.
st.vr.ram_grief_in_spring_at_pampa.s: At the beautiful lake of Pampa in spring, everything reminds Ram of Sita and his grief deepens. Lakshman tells him there is no strength greater than enthusiasm, and to rouse himself.

st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.l: In devastating loss, a steady friend can stop grief from turning into destruction.
st.vr.ram_grief_turns_to_rage.s: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.l: When you can't repay a kindness, give what you have: thanks, and your heart.
st.vr.ram_has_only_an_embrace_to_give.s: Hanuman returns with Sita's jewel and her message. Ram is overwhelmed: Hanuman has saved them all, and Ram, an exile, has nothing to give in return, so he embraces him.

st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.l: The deepest gratitude hopes the other never needs your help.
st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.s: After the coronation Ram sends his friends home, asking only to be remembered with love. Hanuman asks to live as long as Ram's story is told, so that hearing it can ease his longing. Ram rises from the throne, embraces him, grants it, and says he would give his life for each of Hanuman's services, and hopes Hanuman never falls into trouble that would let him repay it.
st.vr.ram_hopes_never_to_repay_hanuman.t: Valmiki: Hanuman's boon and Ram's debt

st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.l: A rift can close in one embrace; grief shared between siblings is lighter.
st.vr.ram_learns_his_father_died.s: Bharata finds Ram in bark clothes and falls weeping at his feet, blaming himself. Ram embraces him, tells him he sees no fault in him, and asks him not to blame his mother. Then Ram learns their father is dead and grieves that he was not there.

st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.l: Leaders protect people from their troubles; they don't pull others into their own.
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.s: Thousands of citizens follow Ram into the wilderness, determined to bring him back. At dawn he slips away while they sleep so they will go home rather than suffer for his sake.
st.vr.ram_leaves_sleeping_citizens.t: Ram slips away from the loyal crowd

st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.l: Real strength can afford to be generous; pride is what breaks a person.
st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.s: In their first fight, Ram shatters Ravana's chariot, bow and crown. Instead of killing his exhausted enemy he tells him to go home, rest and come back. Ravana goes back to Lanka humbled, his pride broken.
st.vr.ram_lets_ravana_go_home_to_rest.t: Ram lets Ravana go to rest

st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.l: Good leaders consult wisely, act promptly, and listen to people with no power.
st.vr.ram_questions_bharata_on_ruling.s: Meeting Bharata at Chitrakoot, Ram asks a long series of questions about how he is running the kingdom: whom he consults, how quickly he acts, whether he listens to the falsely accused.

st.vr.ram_remembers_one_kindness.l: Character shows in small habits: speaking first and gently, remembering kindness, forgetting slights.
