st.vr.ram_remembers_one_kindness.s: Before the crisis, Valmiki and the citizens describe the young prince: gentle in speech, unprovoked by harshness, pleased by one kindness and forgetful of a hundred wrongs, humble about his strength, attentive to ordinary people's lives.

st.vr.ram_sita_love_grows.l: Love deepens by paying attention to who the other person really is.
st.vr.ram_sita_love_grows.s: Back in Ayodhya after the wedding, Ram and Sita settle into married life. Valmiki notes that their love, though it began as an arranged match, deepened because each came to know and value the other; she could read his heart without words.

st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.l: Some seasons are for waiting; wait well, without letting grief take you.
st.vr.ram_waits_out_the_monsoon.s: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.

st.vr.shabari_waits.l: Faithful waiting, unseen by the world, is not wasted.
st.vr.shabari_waits.s: The old ascetic woman Shabari has lived for years at Pampa after her teachers died, told that Ram would one day come. She has kept gathering forest food for him. When he arrives, she welcomes him, shows him her teachers' forest, and departs in peace.

st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.l: Disagree with someone you love openly; advice is a sign of care.
st.vr.sita_questions_the_weapon.s: Sita worries that Ram, carrying weapons among peaceful hermits, will be drawn into needless violence. She tells the story of a hermit changed by keeping a sword. Ram thanks her, saying no one advises a person they don't care about, and explains his promise to protect the sages.

st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.l: Two people in trouble can carry each other.
st.vr.sugriva_consoles_ram_as_a_fellow_s.s: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.

st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.l: Comfort makes us forget our promises; a true friend reminds us in time.
st.vr.sugriva_forgets_in_comfort.s: Restored to his throne, Sugriva sinks into pleasure and forgets his promise to search for Sita. Hanuman warns him that help given late counts for little. Autumn comes; angry, Ram sends Lakshman, and Hanuman counsels the frightened Sugriva to bear harsh words and keep faith.

st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.l: A calm voice can turn a confrontation into an apology on both sides.
st.vr.sugriva_owns_the_lapse.s: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, bow twanging. Tara meets him with reason and courtesy: strong people think before anger takes over; bear the slip of someone on your side. Sugriva apologises and Lakshman asks forgiveness for his own harsh words.

st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.l: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.
st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.s: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
st.vr.sugriva_sees_threat_in_strangers.t: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words

st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.l: When you can't repay a kindness, give what you have: thanks, and your heart.
st.vr.sugriva_shakes_ram_out_of_despair.s: Hanuman returns with Sita's jewel and her message. Ram is overwhelmed: Hanuman has saved them all, and Ram, an exile, has nothing to give in return, so he embraces him.

st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.l: Even when a parent fails you, you can choose to protect their dignity.
st.vr.sumantra_drives_the_empty_chariot_.s: The charioteer returns and delivers Ram's messages: honour our father in his old age, be kind to all three mothers including Kaikeyi. He also delivers Lakshman's furious words about their father, showing two very different ways sons respond to a parent's failure.

st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.l: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.
st.vr.sumitra_sits_with_kausalya.s: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.

st.vr.tara_warns_vali.l: Anger rushes; good counsel says wait until morning, and remember who family is.
st.vr.tara_warns_vali.s: Sugriva roars a second challenge and Vali storms out to fight. His wife Tara stops him: drop this anger, fight tomorrow if you must, make peace with your brother, who is your own family. Vali will not listen.

st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.l: Many family rifts start with a misunderstanding neither side stops to check.
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.s: Vali chases a demon into a cave and tells Sugriva to wait. A year later blood flows out and no voice answers; Sugriva seals the cave in grief and is made king. Vali escapes, believes he was betrayed, and refuses every apology, driving Sugriva out.
st.vr.the_cave_two_brothers_fall_apart.t: The cave: how two brothers fell apart

st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.l: Rivalry seems huge until the end; then only the relationship matters.
st.vr.vali_asks_what_was_my_crime.s: Struck down by Ram's arrow during the duel, Vali rebukes Ram, then makes his peace. To Sugriva he says: don't hold my faults against me; we could not have both brotherhood and kingdom. He entrusts his son to his brother and tells Angada how to live.

st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.l: Rivalry seems huge until the end; then only the relationship matters.
st.vr.vali_last_words_to_his_brother_and.s: Struck down by Ram's arrow during the duel, Vali rebukes Ram, then makes his peace. To Sugriva he says: don't hold my faults against me; we could not have both brotherhood and kingdom. He entrusts his son to his brother and tells Angada how to live.

st.vr.valmiki_grief_becomes_verse.l: Grief can be turned into something that helps others; even a sage regrets words spoken in pain.
st.vr.valmiki_grief_becomes_verse.s: Valmiki sees a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating cranes and hears the survivor cry. His grief bursts out as a curse that falls into rhythm; he regrets the words but realises they are a new kind of verse. Brahma tells him to use it to tell Ram's story.

st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.l: Give a second chance to someone who comes to you sincerely, even across old lines.
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.s: Vibhishana arrives at Ram's camp. The allies suspect a spy; Hanuman reads him as sincere. Ram decides: he will not turn away anyone who comes in friendship, even with faults; whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' he will protect.
st.vr.vibhishana_distrusted_by_the_right.t: Ram takes in the enemy's brother

st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.l: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.
st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.s: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.
st.vr.vibhishana_do_not_kill_the_messeng.t: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka

st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.l: Grief for someone who wronged you is real; death ends the fight.
st.vr.vibhishana_mourns_the_brother_he_l.s: Ravana is dead. Vibhishana weeps for the brother who drove him out and hesitates to perform his rites. Ram tells him enmity ends at death and Ravana is now his to honour. Mandodari mourns: once he mastered his desires and won the world; in the end his desires mastered him.

st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.l: Speak the truth to family even when it costs you; leave if you must, without hatred.
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.s: In Ravana's war council, everyone else flatters him. Vibhishana alone says what he has seen: return Sita, avoid war. Ravana insults him as a traitor. Vibhishana says flatterers are easy to find and truth-tellers rare, wishes his brother well, and leaves.
st.vr.vibhishana_tells_his_brother_and_i.t: Vibhishana tells his brother the truth

st.vr.vishvamitra_envies_the_sage_cow.l: Envy and force cannot take what someone will not give; real power is built inside.
st.vr.vishvamitra_envies_the_sage_cow.s: King Vishvamitra is feasted by the sage Vasishtha and covets the wish-granting cow that made it possible. Vasishtha refuses every offer; the king takes her by force and is routed, then fails again with divine weapons. Humbled, he resolves to transform himself through inner discipline instead of force.
st.vr.vishvamitra_envies_the_sage_cow.t: The king who wanted the cow

vr.1.2.16.m: As he spoke, a worry rose in his heart as he looked on: 'Overcome by grief for this bird, what is this I have said?'
roles: Shows looking back at one's words while the feeling is still hot.
vr.1.2.16.sa: तस्येत्थं ब्रुवतश्चिन्ता बभूव हृदि वीक्षतः। शोकार्तेनास्य शकुनेः किमिदं व्याहृतं मया॥

vr.1.2.36.m: Sung by the sage in four equal lines and repeated again and again, his grief became a shloka, a poem.
roles: Shows the poem is born from feeling another creature's loss.
vr.1.2.36.sa: समाक्षरैश्चतुर्भिर्यः पादैर्गीतो महर्षिणा। सोऽनुव्याहरणाद् भूयः शोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः॥

scene.s: Valmiki sees a hunter shoot one of a pair of mating cranes and hears the survivor cry. His grief bursts out as a curse that falls into rhythm; he regrets the words but realises they are a new kind of verse. Brahma tells him to use it to tell Ram's story.

vr.1.21.21.m: Vishvamitra could subdue those demons himself. He has come to ask for your son for your son's own good.
roles: Shows trust in a proven teacher.
vr.1.21.21.sa: तेषां निग्रहणे शक्तः स्वयं च कुशिकात्मजः। तव पुत्रहितार्थाय त्वामुपेत्याभियाचते॥

scene.s: The sage Vishvamitra asks the king for his teenage son Ram to protect a ritual. Dasharatha, who waited years for a child, refuses and offers himself and his army instead. His guru reminds him of his word and that the sage asks for Ram's own growth, and the king lets him go.

vr.1.44.10.m: You have carried through the vow they could not keep, best of men. You have earned the highest honour in the world.
roles: Shows long effort is seen and blessed.
vr.1.44.10.sa: सा त्वया समतिक्रान्ता प्रतिज्ञा पुरुषर्षभ। प्राप्तोऽसि परमं लोके यशः परमसम्मतम्॥

vr.1.53.9.m: Not for a hundred thousand cows, not for a billion, not for heaps of silver, O king, will I give up Shabala. She stays with me.
roles: Shows what sustains his life is not for sale.
vr.1.53.9.sa: नाहं शतसहस्रेण नापि कोटिशतैर्गवाम्॥ राजन् दास्यामि शबलां राशिभी रजतस्य वा। न परित्यागमयं मत्सकाशादरिंदम ॥

vr.1.63.9.m: Ten years went by as if they were a single day and night. Lost in desire, this obstacle came and I did not see it.
roles: Shows regret at how far he drifted from his aim.
vr.1.63.9.sa: अहोरात्रापदेशेन गताः संवत्सरा दश ॥ काममोहाभिभूतस्य विघ्नोऽयं प्रत्युपस्थितः।

vr.1.64.15.m: In his anger he lost what his effort had earned, and with his senses unmastered he found no peace. Then he resolved: 'I will not give way to anger like this again, and I will not speak in it.'
vr.1.64.15.sa: कोपेन च महातेजास्तपोऽपहरणे कृते। इन्द्रियैरजितै राम न लेभे शान्तिमात्मनः॥ बभूवास्य मनश्चिन्ता तपोऽपहरणे कृते। नैवं क्रोधं गमिष्यामि न च वक्ष्ये कथंचन ॥

vr.1.65.3.m: When the thousand years were done the great sage stood still as wood; many obstacles shook him, but anger could not get inside.
vr.1.65.3.sa: पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु काष्ठभूतं महामुनिम्। विघ्नैर्बहुभिराधूतं क्रोधो नान्तरमाविशत्॥

vr.1.77.20.m: Sita was dear to Ram as the wife his father chose; yet his love kept growing because of who she was, and in her heart he lived twice over.
roles: Cultivates affection that deepens through knowing each other's qualities.
vr.1.77.20.sa: प्रिया तु सीता रामस्य दारा पितृकृता इति॥ गुणाद् रूपगुणाच्चापि प्रीतिर्भूयोऽभिवर्धते। तस्याश्च भर्ता द्विगुणं हृदये परिवर्तते॥

vr.2.1.10.m: He was always calm inside and began his words gently. Even when spoken to harshly, he did not answer in kind.
roles: Gives strength that does not need the last word.
vr.2.1.10.sa: स च नित्यं प्रशान्तात्मा मृदुपूर्वं च भाषते। उच्यमानोऽपि परुषं नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते॥

vr.2.1.11.m: A single kindness done to him, however small, was enough to please him; a hundred wrongs he did not keep in mind, being master of himself.
roles: Cultivates one kindness is allowed to be enough.
vr.2.1.11.sa: कदाचिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति । न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया॥

vr.2.100.16.m: I hope you do not take counsel all alone, nor with too many people? And that a plan you have decided on does not spread through the land before it is carried out?
roles: Shows a simple rule for how to deliberate and when to stay quiet.
vr.2.100.16.sa: कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह। कच्चित् ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति॥

vr.2.100.17.m: Having decided on a task that costs little and yields much, do you start it quickly and not delay, Bharata?
roles: Start at once what is clearly worth doing.
vr.2.100.17.sa: कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं मदोदयम्। क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्म न दीर्घयसि राघव॥

vr.2.100.20.m: Do you prefer one wise person over a thousand fools? In a crisis, a wise person can do great good.
roles: Shows choosing whose advice to keep close.
vr.2.100.20.sa: कच्चित् सहस्रैर्मूर्खाणामेकमिच्छसि पण्डितम्। पण्डितो ह्यर्थकृच्छेषु कुर्यानिःश्रेयसं महत्॥

vr.2.100.51.m: The tears that fall from the falsely accused destroy the children and herds of a ruler who governs for his own comfort.
roles: Shows the tears of the falsely accused carry weight.
vr.2.100.51.sa: यानि मिथ्याभिशस्तानां पतन्त्यश्रूणि राघव। तानि पुत्रपशून् घ्नन्ति प्रीत्यर्थमनुशासतः॥

vr.2.101.14.m: I see no fault in you, not the smallest, brother. And you should not blame your mother out of immaturity.
roles: Shows release of blame toward a parent.
vr.2.101.14.sa: न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन। न चापि जननी बाल्यात् त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि ॥

scene.s: Bharata finds Ram in bark clothes and falls weeping at his feet, blaming himself. Ram embraces him, tells him he sees no fault in him, and asks him not to blame his mother. Then Ram learns their father is dead and grieves that he was not there.

vr.2.103.10.m: When I did something well, my father used to comfort me with words that were sweet to hear. Where will I hear such words now?
roles: Shows grief landing on one small missing thing, a father's voice of approval.
vr.2.103.10.sa: पुरा प्रेक्ष्य सुवृत्तं मां पिता यान्याह सान्त्वयन्। वाक्यानि तानि श्रोष्यामि कुतः कर्णसुखान्यहम्॥

vr.2.105.13.m: Every gathering ends in running out, every rise ends in a fall, every meeting ends in parting, and every life ends in death.
roles: Shows parting as built into meeting.
vr.2.105.13.sa: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्याः। संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम्॥

vr.2.105.21.m: People rejoice when the sun rises and rejoice when the day ends, yet they do not notice their own life wearing away.
roles: Shows less clinging to the day's small gains.
vr.2.105.21.sa: नन्दन्त्युदित आदित्ये नन्दन्त्यस्तमितेऽहनि। आत्मनो नावबुध्यन्ते मनुष्या जीवितक्षयम्॥

vr.2.105.23.m: As two pieces of wood meet on the wide ocean and, after some time, drift apart again, so wives, children, relatives and wealth come together and then move away. Their parting is certain.
roles: Holding people closely while knowing the time is lent.
vr.2.105.23.sa: यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे। समेत्य तु व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कंचन॥ एवं भार्याश्च पुत्राश्च ज्ञातयश्च वसूनि च। समेत्य व्यवधावन्ति ध्रुवो ह्येषां विनाभवः॥

vr.2.109.4.m: Whether a person is noble or not, brave or merely boastful, clean or unclean, it is conduct alone that shows it.
roles: Self-respect rests on one's own conduct.
vr.2.109.4.sa: कुलीनमकुलीनं वा वीरं पुरुषमानिनम्। चारित्रमेव व्याख्याति शुचिं वा यदि वाशुचिम्॥

vr.2.109.8.m: If I live by desire, the whole world will follow me, because as the rulers behave, so do the people.
roles: One's conduct is copied by those who look up to one.
vr.2.109.8.sa: कामवृत्तोऽन्वयं लोकः कृत्स्नः समुपवर्तते। यद्वृत्ताः सन्ति राजानस्तद्वृत्ताः सन्ति हि प्रजाः॥

vr.2.112.19.m: Whether from desire or greed, your mother did this for your sake. Do not hold it in your mind; treat her as a son treats his mother.
roles: Keeps the relationship without excusing the act.
vr.2.112.19.sa: कामाद् वा तात लोभाद् वा मात्रा तुभ्यमिदं कृतम्। न तन्मनसि कर्तव्यं वर्तितव्यं च मातृवत्॥

scene.s: Bharata threatens to fast at Ram's door until he returns. Ram persuades him to rise, and they reach a compromise: Bharata takes Ram's sandals to rule in his name. At parting Ram asks him to drop his resentment of their mother.
scene.t: The sandals: a compromise between brothers

vr.2.115.17.m: My brother has entrusted this to me out of love. I will look after it until Ram comes back.
roles: Shows a fourteen-year commitment stated simply.
vr.2.115.17.sa: भ्रात्रा तु मयि संन्यासो निक्षिप्तः सौहृदादयम्। तमिमं पालयिष्यामि राघवागमनं प्रति॥

vr.2.19.32.m: As he set out for the forest and gave up the earth, no change could be seen in his mind, as if he stood beyond the world.
roles: A picture of a mind that loss does not rearrange.
vr.2.19.32.sa: न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुंधराम्। सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया॥

scene.s: On the morning of his coronation, Ram is summoned and told by Kaikeyi that he must go into the forest for fourteen years. He agrees without anger, and is hurt only that his father could not tell him himself. He walks out showing no change of mind, already thinking of those he must comfort.

vr.2.19.6.m: Only one sorrow burns my heart: that the king did not tell me himself about Bharata's coronation.
roles: Shows him accepting the loss while the hurt of being bypassed by his own father burns.
vr.2.19.6.sa: अलीकं मानसं त्वेकं हृदयं दहते मम। स्वयं यन्नाह मां राजा भरतस्याभिषेचनम्॥

vr.2.21.46.m: Hold your sorrow gently in your heart, mother; do not grieve. Once I have kept my father's word, I will come back here from the forest.
roles: A child promises return and asks the parent to bear the interval.
vr.2.21.46.sa: शोकः संधार्यतां मातर्हृदये साधु मा शुचः। वनवासादिहैष्यामि पुनः कृत्वा पितुर्वचः॥

scene.s: Ram tells his mother he must leave for fourteen years in the forest.

vr.2.22.2.m: Hold back your anger and grief, lean on steadiness alone, set this insult aside and take up real cheerfulness. Quickly undo the preparations made for my coronation and get on with what needs doing, without fuss.
roles: Shows leaning on steadiness alone when insulted.
vr.2.22.2.sa: निगृह्य रोष शोकं च धैर्यमाश्रित्य केवलम्। अवमानं निरस्यैनं गृहीत्वा हर्षमुत्तमम्॥ उपक्लुप्तं यदैतन्मे अभिषेकार्थमुत्तमम्। सर्वं निवर्तय क्षिप्रं कुरु कार्य निरव्ययम्॥

scene.s: Lakshman is enraged by the injustice and wants to seize the throne by force. Ram calms him: set aside the insult, don't torment yourself, the setback may lead somewhere better. Lakshman answers that effort, not fate, decides; both views are given their due.

vr.2.22.24.m: Lakshman, do not torment yourself over this reversal of fortune. Between the kingdom and life in the forest, the forest may be the greater blessing.
roles: Shows the kingdom and forest held on one scale.
vr.2.22.24.sa: मा च लक्ष्मण संतापं कार्षीर्लक्ष्या विपर्यये। राज्यं वा वनवासो वा वनवासो महोदयः॥

scene.s: Lakshman is enraged by the injustice and wants to seize the throne by force. Ram calms him: set aside the insult, don't torment yourself, the setback may lead somewhere better. Lakshman answers that effort, not fate, decides; both views are given their due.

vr.2.23.9.m: The person who can push back fate with effort does not lose heart when fate damages his interests.
roles: Shows refusing to be told that nothing can be done.
vr.2.23.9.sa: दैवं पुरुषकारेण यः समर्थः प्रबाधितुम्। न दैवेन विपत्रार्थः पुरुषः सोऽवसीदति॥

scene.s: Lakshman is enraged by the injustice and wants to seize the throne by force. Ram calms him: set aside the insult, don't torment yourself, the setback may lead somewhere better. Lakshman answers that effort, not fate, decides; both views are given their due.

vr.2.24.20.m: Take care that when I am gone the king does not wear himself out with grief for his son, that this terrible sorrow does not destroy him. Look after the old king's welfare always.
roles: Shows seeing the father's sorrow even while leaving.
vr.2.24.20.sa: यथा मयि तु निष्क्रान्ते पुत्रशोकेन पार्थिवः॥ श्रमं नावाप्नुयात् किंचिदप्रमत्ता तथा कुरु। दारुणश्चाप्ययं शोको यथैनं न विनाशयेत्॥ राज्ञो वृद्धस्य सततं हितं चर समाहिता।

scene.s: Ram's mother faints at the news and begs to come with him. Ram gently refuses, asks her to look after his grieving father, and wins her blessing for the journey.

vr.2.25.2.m: May the goodness you have kept so gladly and so faithfully protect you, tiger of the Raghus.
roles: A mother's blessing to carry into hardship.
vr.2.25.2.sa: यं पालयसि धर्म त्वं प्रीत्या च नियमेन च। स वै राघवशार्दूल धर्मस्त्वामभिरक्षतु॥

vr.2.34.28.m: Stay tonight, see your mother and me. Rest, have everything you want, and set out early tomorrow.
roles: A father who cannot stop the leaving asks for one more night.
vr.2.34.28.sa: मातरं मां च सम्पश्यन् वसेमामद्य शर्वरीम्। तर्पितः सर्वकामैस्त्वं श्वः काल्ये साधयिष्यसि ॥

vr.2.40.8.m: Saying 'Go, go' again and again, Sumitra told him: Think of Ram as your father Dasharatha, of Sita as me, and of the forest as Ayodhya. Go happily, my son.
vr.2.40.8.sa: लक्ष्मणं त्वेवमुक्त्वासौ संसिद्धं प्रियराघवम्। सुमित्रा गच्छ गच्छेति पुनः पुनरुवाच तम्॥ राम दशरथं विद्धि मां विद्धि जनकात्मजाम्। अयोध्यामटवीं विद्धि गच्छ तात यथासुखम्॥

vr.2.44.17.m: You will see him again, back from the forest. Let go of grief and confusion, my queen. I tell you the truth.
roles: Shows trust in a child's ability to come through.
vr.2.44.17.sa: निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्। जहि शोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥

scene.s: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.

vr.2.44.9.m: When the blameless one lies down at night, the cool moon, which takes away the day's heat, will touch him and embrace him like a father, and gladden his heart.
roles: Shows a mother's worry given a tender picture of where her child sleeps.
vr.2.44.9.sa: शयानमनघं रात्रौ पितेवाभिपरिष्वजन्। धर्मघ्नः संस्पृशञ्छीतश्चन्द्रमा ह्लादयिष्यति॥

vr.2.46.22.m: Leaders should free people from the troubles they bring on themselves, never pull them into troubles of their own making.
roles: Shows noticing what one's trouble costs those who follow.
vr.2.46.22.sa: पौरा ह्यात्मकृताद् दुःखाद् विप्रमोच्या नृपात्मजैः। न तु खल्वात्मना योज्या दुःखेन पुरवासिनः॥

vr.2.58.18.m: The king has grown old; do not push him aside. Live as prince by carrying out his wishes.
roles: Shows seeing what old age takes from him.
vr.2.58.18.sa: अतिक्रान्तवया राजा मा स्मैनं व्यपरोरुधः। कुमारराज्ये जीवस्व तस्यैवाज्ञाप्रवर्तनात्॥

vr.2.62.13.m: I know what is right, righteous one, and I know you are truthful. It was in my anguish over my son that I said what I said.
roles: Shows she owns the harsh words she spoke.
vr.2.62.13.sa: जानामि धर्मे धर्मज्ञ त्वां जाने सत्यवादिनम्। पुत्रशोकार्तया तत्तु मया किमपि भाषितम्॥

vr.2.62.14.m: Grief destroys steadiness, grief destroys learning, grief destroys everything. There is no enemy like grief.
roles: Names a mother who has just seen what her grief made her say.
vr.2.62.14.sa: शोको नाशयते धैर्यं शोको नाशयते श्रुतम्। शोको नाशयते सर्वं नास्ति शोकसमो रिपुः॥

scene.s: In her grief Kausalya lashes out at her husband for exiling their son. When he folds his hands and asks her forgiveness, she is horrified, apologises, and explains that grief made her speak.

vr.2.63.11.m: This sorrow has come to me, my queen, by my own doing, like a child who swallows poison out of ignorance.
roles: Shows him tracing his present pain to his own old act.
vr.2.63.11.sa: तदिदं मेऽनुसम्प्राप्तं देवि दुःखं स्वयंकृतम्। सम्मोहादिह बालेन यथा स्याद् भक्षितं विषम्॥

vr.2.63.7.m: Whoever, at the start of an undertaking, does not weigh how serious or slight it is, what it will lead to, and what could go wrong, is called a child.
roles: Shows a dying man tracing his sorrow to one rash act of his youth.
vr.2.63.7.sa: गुरुलाघवमर्थानामारम्भे कर्मणां फलम्। दोषं वा यो न जानाति स बाल इति होच्यते।७।।

scene.s: Dying of grief, Dasharatha confesses to Kausalya that as a young prince he shot at a sound in the dark and killed a boy filling water for his blind, aged parents. He took the water to them and told them the truth himself. The father cursed him to lose a son as they had, and now, longing for Ram, the king dies at midnight.
scene.t: The boy at the river: Dasharatha's old guilt

vr.2.64.19.m: Had you not told us this terrible deed yourself, your head would have shattered into a hundred thousand pieces.
roles: Shows owning a wrong oneself before being found out.
vr.2.64.19.sa: यद्येतदशुभं कर्म न स्म मे कथयेः स्वयम्। फलेन्मूर्धा स्म राजन् सद्यः शतसहस्रधा॥

scene.s: Dying of grief, Dasharatha confesses to Kausalya that as a young prince he shot at a sound in the dark and killed a boy filling water for his blind, aged parents. He took the water to them and told them the truth himself. The father cursed him to lose a son as they had, and now, longing for Ram, the king dies at midnight.
scene.t: The boy at the river: Dasharatha's old guilt

vr.2.64.9.m: You are the refuge of us who have no other; you are the eyes of us who cannot see. Our lives hang on you. Why don't you speak?
roles: Shows old parents calling to the child their lives depend on with no answer.
vr.2.64.9.sa: त्वं गतिस्त्वगतीनां च चक्षुस्त्वं हीनचक्षुषाम्। समासक्तास्त्वयि प्राणाः कथं त्वं नाभिभाषसे॥

scene.s: Dying of grief, Dasharatha confesses to Kausalya that as a young prince he shot at a sound in the dark and killed a boy filling water for his blind, aged parents. He took the water to them and told them the truth himself. The father cursed him to lose a son as they had, and now, longing for Ram, the king dies at midnight.
scene.t: The boy at the river: Dasharatha's old guilt

vr.2.7.27.m: I see no difference between Ram and Bharata. So I am glad the king will crown Ram.
vr.2.7.27.sa: रामे वा भरते वाहं विशेषं नोपलक्षये। तस्मात्तुष्टास्मि यद्राजा रामं राज्येऽभिषेक्ष्यति॥

scene.s: The maid Manthara works on Queen Kaikeyi's insecurity until she is consumed by fear for her son's future. Kaikeyi makes the doting old king promise before she names her wish, then demands Ram's exile and Bharata's coronation. Bound by his word, Dasharatha pleads, rages and collapses.
scene.t: Kaikeyi's boons and the king's blind promise

vr.2.72.25.m: Mother, of what illness did the king die while I was away? Blessed are Ram and the others who performed my father's last rites themselves.
roles: Shows the ache of not having been there.
vr.2.72.25.sa: अम्ब केनात्यगाद् राजा व्याधिना मय्यनागते। धन्या रामादयः सर्वे यैः पिता संस्कृतः स्वयम्॥

vr.2.72.27.m: Where is my father's gentle hand now, the hand that used to brush the dust off me again and again?
roles: Depicts grief remembered through a father's touch.
vr.2.72.27.sa: क्व स पाणिः सुखस्पर्शस्तातस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः। यो हि मां रजसा ध्वस्तमभीक्ष्णं परिमार्जति॥

vr.2.75.15.m: Noble lady, why do you blame me, who knew nothing and did nothing wrong? You know how deep my love for Ram is.
roles: Shows falsely accused by someone he loves, for something done in his name.
vr.2.75.15.sa: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीति स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥

vr.2.77.21.m: Three pairs come to every creature without exception: hunger and thirst, grief and confusion, old age and death. Since none can be avoided, you should not give way like this.
roles: Shows standing up again in the face of what cannot be avoided.
vr.2.77.21.sa: त्रीणि द्वन्द्वानि भूतेषु प्रवृत्तान्यविशेषतः। तेषु चापरिहार्येषु नैवं भवितुमर्हसि॥

vr.2.8.8.m: Lucky Kausalya, they say: tomorrow, under the Pushya star, the best of the twice-born will crown her son heir to the great kingdom.
vr.2.8.8.sa: सुभगा किल कौसल्या यस्याः पुत्रोऽभिषेक्ष्यते। यौवराज्येन महता श्वः पुष्येण द्विजोत्तमैः॥

scene.s: The maid Manthara works on Queen Kaikeyi's insecurity until she is consumed by fear for her son's future. Kaikeyi makes the doting old king promise before she names her wish, then demands Ram's exile and Bharata's coronation. Bound by his word, Dasharatha pleads, rages and collapses.
scene.t: Kaikeyi's boons and the king's blind promise

vr.2.82.11.m: How could a son of Dasharatha steal a kingdom? The kingdom and I both belong to Ram. Speak what is right here.
roles: Shows saying no before the whole assembly.
vr.2.82.11.sa: कथं दशरथाज्जातो भवेद् राज्यापहारकः। राज्यं चाहं च रामस्य धर्म वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥

vr.2.84.9.m: But if Bharata comes in good faith towards Ram, this army may cross the Ganga safely today.
roles: Shows prepare, then test the facts before judging.
vr.2.84.9.sa: यदि तुष्टस्तु भरतो रामस्येह भविष्यति। इयं स्वस्तिमती सेना गङ्गामद्य तरिष्यति॥

scene.s: Ram's friend Guha sees Bharata's army and assumes he has come to kill Ram. He prepares to block the river but goes to meet him first. Learning Bharata's intent, he becomes his guide and shows him the grass bed where Ram slept, where Bharata vows to live as an ascetic until Ram returns.

vr.2.97.12.m: When has Bharata ever done you wrong? What has happened that you now fear and suspect him like this?
roles: Shows trust built on how someone has always behaved.
vr.2.97.12.sa: विप्रियं कृतपूर्वं ते भरतेन कदा नु किम्। ईदृशं वा भयं तेऽद्य भरतं यद् विशङ्कसे॥

scene.s: From a tree at Chitrakoot, Lakshman sees Bharata's army and is sure he has come to finish them. Ram stops him: Bharata has never wronged us; why suspect him now? And no kingdom is worth winning through wrong.

vr.2.97.4.m: Any wealth that would come to me through the ruin of my relatives or friends I would never accept, any more than food laced with poison.
roles: Shows kin and friends weighing more than the prize.
vr.2.97.4.sa: यद् द्रव्यं बान्धवानां वा मित्राणां वा क्षये भवेत्। नाहं तत् प्रतिगृह्णीयां भक्ष्यान् विषकृतानिव॥

vr.2.97.7.m: This sea-girt earth is not hard for me to win, gentle brother. But I would not want even Indra's throne through wrong.
roles: Shows strength that chooses not to take.
vr.2.97.7.sa: नेयं मम मही सौम्य दुर्लभा सागराम्बरा। नहीच्छेयमधर्मेण शक्रत्वमपि लक्ष्मण॥

vr.3.10.17.m: You said this out of love and friendship for me. I am pleased with you, Sita; no one gives advice to someone they do not care about.
roles: Shows thanking the person who questions you.
vr.3.10.17.sa: मम स्नेहाच्च सौहार्दादिदमुक्तं त्वा वचः॥ परितुष्टोऽस्म्यहं सीते न ह्यनिष्टोऽनुशास्यते।

vr.3.41.20.m: Though I try to stop you out of concern for your good, you will not accept my words. People whose time is running out do not take the good advice their friends give.
roles: Names an adviser who knows he will not be heard.
vr.3.41.20.sa: निवार्यमाणस्तु मया हितैषिणा न मृष्यसे वाक्यमिदं निशाचर। परेतकल्पा हि गतायुषो नरा हितं न गृह्णन्ति सुहृद्भिरीरितम्॥

scene.s: Ravana asks Maricha to help him abduct Sita. Maricha, who has met Ram before, warns him again and again: flatterers are many, truth-tellers rare, and those heading for a fall reject good advice. Ravana threatens him until he agrees.

vr.3.43.6.m: This deer's form is the trick of a master of illusion, bright as a city in the clouds. No such jewelled deer exists anywhere on earth, Raghava. It is an illusion, no doubt.
roles: Shows testing an attraction against what actually exists.
vr.3.43.6.sa: अस्य मायाविदो माया मृगरूपमिदं कृतम्। भानुमत् पुरुषव्याघ्र गन्धर्वपुरसंनिभम्॥ मृगो ह्येवंविधो रत्नविचित्रो नास्ति राघव। जगत्यां जगतीनाथ मायैषा हि न संशयः॥

scene.s: A dazzling deer with a golden, jewelled hide appears near the hut. Lakshman warns that no such deer exists; it must be a trick. Sita longs for it and Ram, captivated too, gives chase, leaving the hut exposed.

vr.3.50.15.m: Carry only the load that does not crush you, friend; eat only the food you can digest without falling ill.
roles: Names measuring a load before lifting it.
vr.3.50.15.sa: स भारः सौम्य भर्तव्यो यो नरं नावसादयेत्। तदन्नमपि भोक्तव्यं जीर्यते यदनामयम्॥

scene.s: The aged vulture Jatayu wakes to see Ravana carrying Sita off. He warns him, then fights him alone and is mortally wounded. Later Ram finds him dying, hears his news, and cremates him with the honour due a father.

vr.3.50.18.m: I am old; you are young, with bow, chariot, armour and arrows. Even so, you will not take Vaidehi from me unharmed.
roles: Shows age and weakness do not decide the duty.
vr.3.50.18.sa: वृद्धोऽहं त्वं युवा धन्वी सरथः कवची शरी। न चाप्यादाय कुशली वैदेहीं मे गमिष्यसि ॥

scene.s: The aged vulture Jatayu wakes to see Ravana carrying Sita off. He warns him, then fights him alone and is mortally wounded. Later Ram finds him dying, hears his news, and cremates him with the honour due a father.

vr.3.65.4.m: You should not destroy the worlds for the wrong done by one. Surely we can find out whose broken war chariot this is.
roles: Shows the innocent kept in view.
vr.3.65.4.sa: एकस्य नापराधेन लोकान् हन्तुं त्वमर्हसि। ननु जानामि कस्यायं भग्नः सांग्रामिको रथः॥

scene.s: Ram returns to an empty hut. He searches, questions trees and animals, breaks down and finally rages that he will destroy the world. Lakshman calms him: don't punish the whole world for one person's crime; trouble comes to everyone and passes.

vr.3.66.17.m: Your understanding, wise one, is beyond even the gods' reckoning. Grief has only put your wisdom to sleep, and I am here to wake it.
vr.3.66.17.sa: बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया। शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं सम्बोधयाम्यहम्॥

vr.3.66.5.m: Take heart, best of men. Which living being does trouble not touch? Troubles strike like fire, king, and pass in a moment.
roles: Holds on because trouble moves through.
vr.3.66.5.sa: आश्वसिही नरश्रेष्ठ प्राणिनः कस्य नापदः। संस्पृशन्त्यग्निवद् राजन् क्षणेन व्यपयान्ति च॥

vr.3.66.9.m: Even the mighty Sun and Moon, the two eyes of the world, on whom everything rests, go through eclipses.
vr.3.66.9.sa: यौ धर्मों जगतो नेत्रौ यत्र सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम्। आदित्यचन्द्रौ ग्रहणमभ्युपेतौ महाबलौ॥

vr.3.72.7.m: You must make him your friend, best of friends. Thinking it over, I see no success for you without it.
roles: Names seeking out someone who has known the same loss.
vr.3.72.7.sa: तदवश्यं त्वया कार्यः स सुहृत् सुहृदां वर। अकृत्वा नहि ते सिद्धिमहं पश्यामि चिन्तयन् ॥

scene.s: Freed from a curse, the creature Kabandha tells the grieving brothers to seek out Sugriva, an exile who has also lost his wife and home. Only a friend in the same trouble, he says, can help them now.
scene.t: Kabandha: find a friend who understands

vr.3.74.12.m: So the great ones told me, best of men, and for you I have gathered every kind of forest food from the banks of the Pampa.
roles: Shows the waiting was spent preparing an offering.
vr.3.74.12.sa: एवमुक्ता महाभागैस्तदाहं पुरुषर्षभ। मया तु संचितं वन्यं विविधं पुरुषर्षभ॥ तवार्थे पुरुषव्याघ्र पम्पायास्तीरसम्भवम्।

vr.3.74.22.m: The flowers and blue lilies they offered here in their worship have still not withered.
roles: Shows a student still tending her teachers' place.
vr.3.74.22.sa: देवकार्याणि कुर्वद्भिर्यानीमानि कृतानि वै। पुष्पैः कुवलयैः सार्धं म्लानत्वं न तु यान्ति वै॥

vr.3.9.19.m: This is the old story of what carrying a weapon does: keeping a weapon close is said to change a person, as contact with fire changes wood.
roles: Shows what you keep at hand slowly shaping what you do.
vr.3.9.19.sa: एवमेतत् पुरावृत्तं शस्त्रसंयोगकारणम्। अग्निसंयोगवद्धेतुः शस्त्रसंयोग उच्यते॥

scene.s: Sita worries that Ram, carrying weapons among peaceful hermits, will be drawn into needless violence. She tells the story of a hermit changed by keeping a sword. Ram thanks her, saying no one advises a person they don't care about, and explains his promise to protect the sages.

vr.3.9.26.m: The skilful reach what is right by disciplining themselves with effort through many restraints. Happiness is not reached through comfort.
vr.3.9.26.sa: आत्मानं नियमैस्तैस्तैः कर्षयित्वा प्रयत्नतः। प्राप्यते निपुणैर्धर्मो न सुखाल्लभते सुखम्॥

vr.4.1.101.m: Noble brother, enthusiasm is powerful; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. For the person who has it, nothing in the world is out of reach.
roles: Names energy of effort as strength itself.
vr.4.1.101.sa: उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥

vr.4.10.6.m: Seeing me in despair, the citizens and ministers made me king; it was not my wish. Please forgive me for it.
roles: Pleading to be believed by someone who has already decided.
vr.4.10.6.sa: विषादात्विह मां दृष्ट्वा पौरैर्मन्त्रिभिरेव च॥ अभिषिक्तो न कामेन तन्मे क्षन्तुं त्वमर्हसि।

scene.s: Vali chases a demon into a cave and tells Sugriva to wait. A year later blood flows out and no voice answers; Sugriva seals the cave in grief and is made king. Vali escapes, believes he was betrayed, and refuses every apology, driving Sugriva out.
scene.t: The cave: how two brothers fell apart

vr.4.15.22.m: Your younger brother deserves your care. Near you or far away, he is your own family. I see no relative on earth to equal him.
roles: Shows seeing the rival as kin again.
vr.4.15.22.sa: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयानेष वानरः॥ तत्र वा सन्निहस्थो वा सर्वथा बन्धुरेव ते। नहि तेन समं बन्धुं भुवि पश्यामि कंचन ॥

scene.s: Sugriva roars a second challenge and Vali storms out to fight. His wife Tara stops him: drop this anger, fight tomorrow if you must, make peace with your brother, who is your own family. Vali will not listen.

vr.4.15.7.m: Let go of this anger that has come on like a river in flood, as you throw off last night's garland when you get up in the morning.
roles: Lets the surge pass before acting.
vr.4.15.7.sa: साधु क्रोधमिमं वीर नदीवेगमिवागतम्। शयनादुत्थितः काल्यं त्यज मुक्तामिव स्रजम्॥

vr.4.2.16.m: Clearly your restless monkey nature is showing, friend: because your mind is so flighty, you cannot settle yourself on a clear thought.
roles: Shows fear running ahead of the facts.
vr.4.2.16.sa: अहो शाखामृगत्वं ते व्यक्तमेव प्लवङ्गम। लघुचित्ततयात्मानं न स्थापयसि यो मतौ।। ।॥

scene.s: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
scene.t: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words

vr.4.22.23.m: Do not be too familiar, and do not be distant either; both are serious mistakes. So keep a sense of the middle.
roles: Shows reading how close to stand with those who hold power.
vr.4.22.23.sa: न चातिप्रणयः कार्यः कर्तव्योऽप्रणयश्च ते। उभयं हि महादोषं तस्मादन्तरदृग्भव॥

vr.4.22.3.m: Sugriva, do not hold my faults against me. I was dragged by a confusion of mind I could not resist.
vr.4.22.3.sa: सुग्रीव दोषेण न मां गन्तुमर्हसि किल्वषात्। कृष्यमाणं भविष्येण बुद्धिमोहेन मां बलात्॥

scene.s: Struck down by Ram's arrow during the duel, Vali rebukes Ram, then makes his peace. To Sugriva he says: don't hold my faults against me; we could not have both brotherhood and kingdom. He entrusts his son to his brother and tells Angada how to live.

vr.4.22.4.m: Brother, it seems we were not meant to have both happiness at once: brotherly love and the kingdom. It turned out otherwise.
roles: Shows regret that it went wrong between them.
vr.4.22.4.sa: युगपद् विहितं तात न मन्ये सुखमावयोः। सौहार्दै भ्रातृयुक्तं हि तदिदं जातमन्यथा॥

vr.4.24.9.m: How could a brother, however greedy, take pleasure in killing a brother of such great worth, once he weighs the joy of a kingdom against this grief?
roles: Depicts him getting what he wanted at a cost he cannot bear.
vr.4.24.9.sa: भ्राता कथं नाम महागुणस्य भ्रातुर्वधं राम विरोचयेत। राज्यस्य दुःखस्य च वीर सारं विचिन्तयन्कामपुरस्कृतोऽपि॥

scene.s: Sugriva has won, but seeing Tara's grief he is crushed by remorse: how could anyone enjoy a kingdom bought with a brother's life? He remembers Vali only ever said 'don't do it again.'

vr.4.27.24.m: Enough, brother. Do not sink into this pain. You know that those who keep grieving lose every purpose they had.
roles: Shows holding purpose through a season of waiting.
vr.4.27.24.sa: अलं वीर व्यथां गत्वा न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि। शोचते ह्यवसीदन्ति सर्वार्था विदितं हिते॥

scene.s: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.

vr.4.27.29.m: The rainy season has come; wait for autumn. Then you will defeat Ravana with his kingdom and his allies.
roles: Shows waiting as part of the campaign, not a retreat from it.
vr.4.27.29.sa: शरत्कालं प्रतीक्षस्व प्रावृटकालोऽयमागतः। ततः सराष्ट्र सगणं रावणं तं वधिष्यसि॥

scene.s: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.

vr.4.28.62.m: Once he has rested, Sugriva will see for himself that the time has come and remember the help he received. I have no doubt.
roles: Shows giving a friend time before judging him.
vr.4.28.62.sa: स्वयमेव हि विश्रम्य ज्ञात्वा कालमुपागतम्। उपकारं च सुग्रीवो वेत्स्यते नात्र संशयः॥

scene.s: The rains come and Ram must wait four months on a mountain before any search can begin. He cannot sleep for grief. Lakshman reminds him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this is a season for waiting. Ram resolves to wait and to give Sugriva time.

vr.4.29.7.m: Whoever acts on a friend's business after its time has passed does not truly serve that friend, even if he does something big.
vr.4.29.7.sa: यो हि कालव्यतीतेषु मित्रकार्येषु वर्तते। स कृत्वा महतोऽप्यान्न मित्रार्थेन युज्यते॥

vr.4.3.19.m: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
roles: Gives a concrete picture of clear, unhurried speech.
vr.4.3.19.sa: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उर:स्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥

vr.4.32.15.m: You must patiently bear the harsh words of great-hearted Ram, who is in pain and has lost his wife, even when they come to you through another man.
roles: Shows remembering what he has lost.
vr.4.32.15.sa: आर्तस्य हृतदारस्य परुषं पुरुषान्तरात्। वचनं मर्षणीयं ते राघवस्य महात्मनः॥

scene.s: Restored to his throne, Sugriva sinks into pleasure and forgets his promise to search for Sita. Hanuman warns him that help given late counts for little. Autumn comes; angry, Ram sends Lakshman, and Hanuman counsels the frightened Sugriva to bear harsh words and keep faith.

vr.4.32.7.m: Making a friend is easy in every way; keeping the friendship is hard. Because minds are changeable, affection can break over very little.
roles: Names a man who worries aloud that a small lapse has cost him a friend.
vr.4.32.7.sa: सर्वथा सुकरं मित्रं दुष्करं प्रतिपालनम्। अनित्यत्वात् तु चित्तानां प्रीतिरल्पेऽपि भिद्यते॥

vr.4.33.39.m: Prince, this is no time for anger, and anger should not be turned on your own people. Hero, you should bear even the lapse of someone who wants your good.
roles: Making room for the failure of someone on your side.
vr.4.33.39.sa: न कोपकालः क्षितिपालपुत्र न चापि कोपः स्वजने विधेयः। त्वदर्थकामस्य जनस्य तस्य प्रमादमप्यर्हसि वीर सोढुम्॥

scene.s: Lakshman storms into Kishkindha, bow twanging. Tara meets him with reason and courtesy: strong people think before anger takes over; bear the slip of someone on your side. Sugriva apologises and Lakshman asks forgiveness for his own harsh words.

vr.4.35.9.m: Best of men, people of real character, like you, do not suddenly fall under the control of anger without first thinking things over.
vr.4.35.9.sa: सत्त्वयुक्ता हि पुरुषास्त्वद्विधाः पुरुषर्षभ। अविमृश्य न रोषश्य सहसा यान्ति वश्यताम् ॥

vr.4.36.20.m: And forgive me, friend, the harsh words I said to you after hearing the grieving Ram.
roles: Shows friendship put back before the work resumes.
vr.4.36.20.sa: यच्च शोकाभिभूतस्य श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम्। मया त्वं परुषाण्युक्तस्तत् क्षमस्व सखे मम॥

vr.4.49.6.m: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
roles: Shows not closing one's eyes when tired.
vr.4.49.6.sa: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥

vr.4.62.13.m: I could give you back your wings this very day. But by staying here as you are, you will do something for the good of the world.
roles: Living on through a long wait.
vr.4.62.13.sa: उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्। इहस्थस्त्वं हि लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि॥

scene.s: The despairing monkeys meet Sampati, Jatayu's old brother, whose wings burnt long ago. A sage once told him to live on, because one day his knowledge would be needed. Now he tells them Sita is in Lanka, and his wings grow back.
scene.t: Sampati, the bird who could not fly

vr.4.66.28.m: Now I am old and my strength has faded. This is your time; you have every quality it needs.
roles: Names his qualities by someone who knows.
vr.4.66.28.sa: स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः। साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान् सर्वगुणान्वितः॥

vr.4.66.7.m: Your strength, intelligence, energy and courage stand out among all beings, best of monkeys. Why do you not step up?
vr.4.66.7.sa: बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव। विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे।७।।

scene.s: At the ocean's edge, each monkey says how far he can leap; none can cross. Old Jambavan turns to Hanuman, who has sat silent, and reminds him of his birth and power: why are you holding back? This is your time. Hanuman grows and prepares to leap.
scene.t: Jambavan reminds Hanuman who he is

vr.4.7.10.m: But the foolish person who keeps giving in to despair sinks helplessly in grief, like an overloaded boat in water.
roles: Shows warns what happens when steadiness is given up.
vr.4.7.10.sa: बालिशस्तु नरो नित्यं वैक्लव्यं योऽनुवर्तते। स मज्जत्यवशः शोके भाराक्रान्तेव नौ ले॥

scene.s: Ram and Sugriva swear friendship before a fire. Sugriva shows Ram the jewels Sita dropped; Ram breaks down, and Sugriva comforts him: in trouble the steady person thinks it through, and a friend is the greatest refuge.

vr.4.7.14.m: I say this for your good, as a friend; I am not lecturing you. Honour our friendship and do not grieve.
roles: Shows how to stand by a grieving friend.
vr.4.7.14.sa: हितं वयस्यभावेन ब्रूमि नोपदिशामि ते। वयस्यतां पूजयन्मे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि ॥

vr.4.7.9.m: In disaster, in money trouble, in fear, even when life itself is at stake, the steady person who thinks things through with their own mind does not sink.
roles: Names the quality that does not go under.
vr.4.7.9.sa: व्यसने वार्थकृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे। विमृशंश्च स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान् नावसीदति॥

vr.4.8.8.m: Rich or poor, happy or unhappy, faultless or flawed, a friend is one's greatest refuge.
roles: Names valuing the friends one has.
vr.4.8.8.sa: आढ्यो वापि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा। निर्दोषश्च सदोषश्च वयस्यः परमा गतिः॥

vr.5.1.146.m: Whoever has these four, as you do, chief of monkeys, never sinks in his work: steadiness, clear sight, judgement and skill.
vr.5.1.146.sa: यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव। धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्य स कर्मसु न सीदति ॥

vr.5.1.91.m: Now that this task has come, great one, it is your turn to let the ocean and me show our gratitude. Please accept it gladly.
roles: Shows an old kindness remembered and returned.
vr.5.1.91.sa: अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च। प्रीतिं प्रीतिमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महामते॥

vr.5.1.94.m: The time for my work presses on me, and the day is passing. I have given my word: I will not stop on the way.
roles: Shows keeping to the task while the day lasts.
vr.5.1.94.sa: त्वरते कार्यकाले मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते। प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्तरा॥

vr.5.12.10.m: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
roles: Shows a concrete plan for places not yet searched.
vr.5.12.10.sa: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥

vr.5.13.43.m: Giving up brings many harms; one who lives on finds good things. So I will hold on to life; for the living, meeting again is certain.
roles: Shows holding on to life itself.
vr.5.13.43.sa: विनाशे बहवो दोषा जीवन् प्राप्नोति भद्रकम्। तस्मात् प्राणान् धरिष्यामि ध्रुवो जीवति संगमः॥

vr.5.21.14.m: You cannot tempt me with power or wealth. I belong to Raghava as light belongs to the sun.
roles: States her loyalty as part of what she is.
vr.5.21.14.sa: शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा। अनन्या राघवेणाहं भास्करेण यथा प्रभा॥

scene.s: Ravana comes to the grove offering Sita wealth and power, and threatens her with death if she refuses. Trembling, she places a blade of grass between them and refuses: she cannot be bought, and he should return her before he destroys himself.

vr.5.26.39.m: Love lasts while someone is in sight; out of sight, affection fades. But that is the way of the ungrateful. Ram will not let it fade.
roles: Names trust in the other's constancy.
vr.5.26.39.sa: दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः। नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति॥

vr.5.30.18.m: I must speak to her in ordinary human words that carry meaning. There is no other way to comfort this blameless woman.
roles: Shows him planning his words around her fear.
vr.5.30.18.sa: अवश्यमेव वक्तव्यं मानुषं वाक्यमर्थवत्। मया सान्त्वयितुं शक्या नान्यथेयमनिन्दिता ॥

vr.5.30.34.m: Battles are uncertain, and I don't like a gamble. What wise person would turn a sure task into an unsure one?
roles: Shows choosing the sure route over a show of strength.
vr.5.30.34.sa: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते। कश्च निःसंशयं कार्यं कुर्यात् प्राज्ञः ससंशयम्॥

vr.5.30.40.m: I will recite good and true words about Ram, best of the Ikshvakus, speaking gently, and arrange it all so that Sita can trust what she hears.
roles: Shows a frightened listener in the opening.
vr.5.30.40.sa: इक्ष्वाकूणां वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः। शुभानि धर्मयुक्तानि वचनानि समर्पयन्॥ श्रावयिष्यामि सर्वाणि मधुरां प्रब्रुवन् गिरम्। श्रद्धास्यति यथा सीता तथा सर्वं समादधे॥

vr.5.34.5.m: How true this lovely old saying seems to me: joy comes to a person who stays alive, even if it takes a hundred years.
roles: Staying alive is the one thing asked.
vr.5.34.5.sa: कल्याणी वत गाथेयं लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मा। एति जीवन्तमानन्दो नरं वर्षशतादपि॥

vr.5.36.44.m: Hearing Ram spoken of, Sita's sorrow lifted; hearing of his sorrow, she grieved as much as he did. She was like an autumn night, the moon rising through the last of the rain clouds.
roles: Shows relief and sorrow held in the same moment.
vr.5.36.44.sa: सा रामसंकीर्तनवीतशोका रामस्य शोकेन समानशोका। शरन्मुखेनाम्बुदशेषचन्द्रा निशेव वैदेहसुता बभूव ॥

vr.5.38.32.m: Show me your great-hearted kindness, best of men. I have you, my protector, and yet I look like someone who has no one.
roles: Shows she has to ask to be remembered.
vr.5.38.32.sa: स कुरुष्व महोत्साहां कृपां मयि नरर्षभ। त्वया नाथवती नाथ अनाथा इव दृश्यते॥

vr.5.39.20.m: And for me, so unlucky, your being near, friend, would free me from this great sorrow, even if only for a moment.
roles: Shows a moment's relief is all she hopes for.
vr.5.39.20.sa: मम चैवाल्पभाग्यायाः सांनिध्यात् तव वानर । अस्य शोकस्य महतो मुहूर्त मोक्षणं भवेत्॥

vr.5.39.40.m: So take heart, bless you. Wait for the time to come. Before long you will see Ram, blazing like fire.
roles: Shows holding on for a named reason.
vr.5.39.40.sa: तदाश्वसिहि भद्रं ते भव त्वं कालकाक्षिणी। नचिराद् द्रक्ष्यसे रामं प्रज्वलन्तमिवानलम्॥

scene.s: Hanuman's parting words to Sita before he leaps back across the sea to bring Ram.

vr.5.41.6.m: No single means achieves even a small task. The one who knows many ways to the goal is the one able to reach it.
roles: Shows resourcefulness in place of one fixed plan.
vr.5.41.6.sa: नह्येकः साधको हेतुः स्वल्पस्यापीह कर्मणः। यो ह्यर्थं बहुधा वेद स समर्थोऽर्थसाधने॥

vr.5.55.10.m: Burning Lanka was a small thing, no doubt, but overcome by anger I have destroyed the root of my mission. Surely Sita has perished, for no part of Lanka is left unburnt; the whole city is ash.
roles: Shows terror that he has harmed the one he came to save.
vr.5.55.10.sa: ईषत्कार्यमिदं कार्यं कृतमासीन्न संशयः। तस्य क्रोधाभिभूतेन मया मूलक्षयः कृतः॥ विनष्टा जानकी व्यक्तं न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते। लङ्कायाः कश्चिदुद्देशः सर्वा भस्मीकृता पुरी॥

vr.5.55.3.m: Blessed indeed are the great-hearted who, with good sense, check anger the moment it rises, as water puts out a blazing fire.
roles: Buddhi set against anger at the moment it rises.
vr.5.55.3.sa: धन्याः खलु महात्मानो ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम्। निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा॥

scene.s: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.
scene.t: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka

vr.5.55.5.m: An angry person never knows what should and should not be said. For the angry, nothing is off limits to do or to say.
roles: Knowing in advance what anger will switch off.
vr.5.55.5.sa: वाच्यावाच्यं प्रकुपितो न विजानाति कर्हिचित्। नाकार्यमस्ति क्रुद्धस्य नावाच्यं विद्यते क्वचित्॥

vr.6.1.12.m: What weighs on my mind is this: I, so poor here, cannot do anything equal in return for the one who brought me such good news.
roles: Names gratitude that wants to repay and cannot.
vr.6.1.12.sa: इदं तु मम दीनस्य मनो भूयः प्रकर्षति। यदिहास्य प्रियाख्यातुर्न कुर्मि सदृशं प्रियम् ॥

vr.6.10.17.m: All the ministers have held back from telling you this, but I must tell you what I have seen and heard. Weigh it properly, then act.
roles: Says the needed thing to someone powerful.
vr.6.10.17.sa: प्रापणे चास्य मन्त्रस्य निवृत्ताः सर्वमन्त्रिणः। अवश्यं च मया वाच्यं यदृष्टमथवा श्रुतम्।। संविधाय यथान्यायं तद्भवान्कर्तुमर्हति॥

vr.6.101.18.m: In the mountains and forests, when I was grief-stricken, careless and despairing, you were the one who comforted me, mighty brother.
roles: Names what someone has been while they can still be told.
vr.6.101.18.sa: शोकार्तस्य प्रमत्तस्य पर्वतेषु वनेषु च॥ विषण्णस्य महाबाहो समाश्वासयिता मम।

vr.6.109.15.m: No one has ever known only victory in war: a fighter either falls to others or brings others down.
roles: Shows winning and falling as two sides of entering the field.
vr.6.109.15.sa: नैकान्तविजयो युद्धे भूतपूर्वः कदाचन। परैर्वा हन्यते वीरः परान्वा हन्ति संयुगे॥

scene.s: Ravana is dead. Vibhishana weeps for the brother who drove him out and hesitates to perform his rites. Ram tells him enmity ends at death and Ravana is now his to honour. Mandodari mourns: once he mastered his desires and won the world; in the end his desires mastered him.

vr.6.109.23.m: Enmity ends with death. Our purpose is achieved. Let his last rites be performed; he is now as much mine as yours.
roles: Shows being claimed as one's own at the end.
vr.6.109.23.sa: मरणान्तानि वैराणि निवृतं नः प्रयोजनम्। क्रियतामस्य संस्कारो ममाप्येष यथा तव ॥

scene.s: Ravana is dead. Vibhishana weeps for the brother who drove him out and hesitates to perform his rites. Ram tells him enmity ends at death and Ravana is now his to honour. Mandodari mourns: once he mastered his desires and won the world; in the end his desires mastered him.

vr.6.111.11.m: Long ago you conquered your senses and so conquered the three worlds. Now, as if remembering that grudge, those same senses have conquered you.
roles: Shows how the master of the world fell by what he stopped guarding.
vr.6.111.11.sa: इन्द्रियाणि पुरा जित्वा जितं त्रिभुवनं त्वया॥ स्मरद्भिरिव तद्वैरमिन्द्रियैरेव निर्जितः।

scene.s: Ravana is dead. Vibhishana weeps for the brother who drove him out and hesitates to perform his rites. Ram tells him enmity ends at death and Ravana is now his to honour. Mandodari mourns: once he mastered his desires and won the world; in the end his desires mastered him.

vr.6.113.29.m: A good person does not repay wrongdoers in kind; the standard must be kept, for good people are adorned by their conduct. Whether people are wicked or good, or even deserve death, a noble person should be compassionate, for no one is without fault. Even toward the cruel who harm others, one should not act basely.
roles: Shows compassion offered even where punishment is deserved.
vr.6.113.29.sa: न परः पापमादत्ते परेषां पापकर्मणाम्। समयो रक्षितव्यस्तु सन्तश्चारित्रभूषणाः।॥ पापानां वा शुभानां वा वधार्हाणामथापि वा। कार्य कारुण्यमार्येण न कश्चिन्त्रापराध्यति॥ लोकहिंसाविहाराणां क्रूराणां पापकर्मणाम्। कुर्वतामपि पापानि नैव कार्यमशोभनम् ॥

scene.s: Hanuman brings Sita the news of victory and offers to punish the guards who tormented her. She refuses: they were following orders, and no one is without fault; show compassion even to those who wronged you.

vr.6.121.16.m: It is not that I refuse you, lord of the rakshasas. But my heart hurries me to see my brother Bharata, who came to Chitrakoot to bring me back, and whose plea I did not grant.
roles: Depicts the heart running ahead to one person at home after years away.
vr.6.121.16.sa: न खल्वेतन्न कुर्यां ते वचनं राक्षसेश्वर। तं तु मे भ्रातरं द्रष्टुं भरतं त्वरते मनः॥ मां निवर्तयितुं योऽसौ चित्रकूटमुपागतः। . शिरसा याचतो यस्य वचनं न कृतं मया॥

vr.6.125.12.m: If, having held the kingdom so long, the fortunate Bharata now wants it for himself, let him rule the whole earth.
roles: The brother's wish is placed before the claim.
vr.6.125.12.sa: संगत्या भरतः श्रीमानराज्येनार्थी स्वयं भवेत्। प्रशास्तु वसुधां सर्वामखिलां रघुनन्दनः॥

scene.s: Victorious, Ram refuses Lanka's honours: his heart is in a hurry to see Bharata. Near Ayodhya he sends Hanuman ahead to read Bharata's face, saying if Bharata now wants the kingdom, let him keep it.

vr.6.127.38.m: This whole kingdom, which you left in my care, I hand back to you. Today my life has meaning and my wish is fulfilled, now that I see you back in Ayodhya as king.
roles: Shows fulfilment in the other's return, not in keeping.
vr.6.127.38.sa: एतत्ते सकलं राज्यं न्यासं निर्यातितं मया॥ अद्य जन्म कृतार्थं मे संवृत्तश्च मनोरथः। यत्त्वां पश्यामि राजानमयोध्यां पुनरागतम्॥

vr.6.16.20.m: O king, people who always say pleasant things are easy to find. Someone who says what is unwelcome but good for you is rare, and so is someone who will listen to it.
roles: Names the worth of saying the hard, helpful thing.
vr.6.16.20.sa: सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः। अप्रियस्य च पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः॥

vr.6.16.24.m: Forgive what I said; I said it for your good, out of respect for you as my elder. Protect yourself and this city. I wish you well. I am leaving. Be happy without me.
roles: Gives no curse, only a blessing at the door.
vr.6.16.24.sa: तन्मर्षयतु यच्चोक्तं गुरुत्वाद्धितमिच्छता। आत्मानं सर्वथा रक्ष पुरीं चेमां सराक्षसाम्। स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सुखी भव मया विना॥

scene.s: In Ravana's war council, everyone else flatters him. Vibhishana alone says what he has seen: return Sita, avoid war. Ravana insults him as a traitor. Vibhishana says flatterers are easy to find and truth-tellers rare, wishes his brother well, and leaves.
scene.t: Vibhishana tells his brother the truth

vr.6.17.50.m: I will speak, king, not to argue, not to compete, not to show I know more, and not from my own wishes, but plainly, as the matter deserves, out of respect for you.
roles: Shows checking why one is about to speak.
vr.6.17.50.sa: न वादान्नापि संघर्षानाधिक्यान च कामतः। वक्ष्यामि वचनं राजन्यथार्थं राम गौरवात्॥

vr.6.18.23.m: That dove received even the one who had carried off its mate when he came to it. If a dove could do that, best of monkeys, how much more a person like me?
roles: Shows hospitality to one who has done harm.
vr.6.18.23.sa: स हि तं प्रतिजग्राह भार्याहर्तारमागतम्। कपोतो वानरश्रेष्ठ किंपुनर्मद्विधो जनः॥

scene.s: Vibhishana arrives in the sky over Ram's camp. Sugriva argues he should be killed as a spy; Hanuman and Ram disagree. Ram tells the story of a dove that sheltered the hunter who had caught its mate, cites the sage Kandu on protecting whoever asks for shelter, and makes his vow: whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' gets safety from all beings, even if it were Ravana himself.
scene.t: Valmiki: Ram's vow of refuge and the dove

vr.6.18.26.m: Whether in distress or in pride, an enemy who has come to you for shelter must be protected by a person of steady mind, even at the cost of his own life.
roles: Shows being a refuge for the frightened.
vr.6.18.26.sa: आतॊ वा यदि वा दृप्तः परेषां शरणं गतः। अरिः प्राणान्परित्यज्य रक्षितव्यः कृतात्मना॥

scene.s: Vibhishana arrives in the sky over Ram's camp. Sugriva argues he should be killed as a spy; Hanuman and Ram disagree. Ram tells the story of a dove that sheltered the hunter who had caught its mate, cites the sage Kandu on protecting whoever asks for shelter, and makes his vow: whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' gets safety from all beings, even if it were Ravana himself.
scene.t: Valmiki: Ram's vow of refuge and the dove

vr.6.18.3.m: I will never turn away someone who has come in friendship, even if he has faults. Good people see nothing wrong in this.
vr.6.18.3.sa: मित्रभावेन संप्राप्तं न त्यजेयं कथंचन। दोषो यद्यपि तस्य स्यात्सतामेतदगर्हितम्॥

scene.s: Vibhishana arrives at Ram's camp. The allies suspect a spy; Hanuman reads him as sincere. Ram decides: he will not turn away anyone who comes in friendship, even with faults; whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' he will protect.
scene.t: Ram takes in the enemy's brother

vr.6.18.31.m: Whoever comes to me even once and says 'I am yours', asking for shelter, I give freedom from fear, from every being. This is my vow.
vr.6.18.31.sa: सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते। अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद्ब्रतं मम॥

vr.6.19.4.m: Hearing his words, Ram spoke to him, comforting him with words and seeming to drink him in with his eyes.
roles: Shows comfort in both word and gaze.
vr.6.19.4.sa: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामो वचनमब्रवीत्॥ वचसा सान्त्वयित्वैनं लोचनाभ्यां पिबनिव।

scene.s: Vibhishana arrives in the sky over Ram's camp. Sugriva argues he should be killed as a spy; Hanuman and Ram disagree. Ram tells the story of a dove that sheltered the hunter who had caught its mate, cites the sage Kandu on protecting whoever asks for shelter, and makes his vow: whoever comes once and says 'I am yours' gets safety from all beings, even if it were Ravana himself.
scene.t: Valmiki: Ram's vow of refuge and the dove

vr.6.22.42.m: I too am able to build a bridge across the ocean. So let the best of the monkeys start building it this very day.
roles: Cultivates owning a skill he had kept quiet about.
vr.6.22.42.sa: समर्थश्चाप्यहं सेतुं कर्तुं वै वरुणालये। तस्मादद्यैव बध्नन्तु सेतुं वानरपुङ्गवाः॥

vr.6.34.11.m: If there is any talk about him, or anything decided at all, tell me everything. That would be the greatest kindness to me.
roles: Shows a captive asking only to know what is being decided about her fate.
vr.6.34.11.sa: यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्। निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तद्वरो मे स्यादनुग्रहः॥

scene.s: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.
scene.t: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house

vr.6.59.131.m: Go. I know you are worn out from fighting. Go back into Lanka, king of the night-walkers. Rest, then come out again with chariot and bow, and you will see my strength.
roles: Even an enemy is allowed to recover.
vr.6.59.131.sa: प्रयाहि जानामि रणार्दितस्त्वं प्रविश्य रात्रिंचरराज लङ्काम्। आश्वस्य निर्याहि रथी सधन्वी तदा बलं प्रेक्ष्यसि मे रथस्थः॥

scene.s: In their first fight, Ram shatters Ravana's chariot, bow and crown. Instead of killing his exhausted enemy he tells him to go home, rest and come back. Ravana goes back to Lanka humbled, his pride broken.
scene.t: Ram lets Ravana go to rest

vr.6.63.4.m: From the start, great king, you never thought this through. Proud of your strength alone, you never weighed where it would lead.
roles: Shows pride in strength blinding him to consequences.
vr.6.63.4.sa: प्रथमं वै महाराज कृत्यमेतदचिन्तितम्। केवलं वीर्यदर्पण नानुबन्धो विचारितः॥

scene.s: Woken from months of sleep, Kumbhakarna tells Ravana bluntly that his pride caused this disaster and he acted in the wrong order. Then, loyal to his brother, he goes out to fight anyway, scorning boastful courtiers: the brave don't praise themselves, they act.

vr.6.63.5.m: A man in power who does last what should come first, and first what should come last, does not know good policy from bad.
roles: Shows sequence as part of judgement.
vr.6.63.5.sa: यः पश्चात्पूर्वकार्याणि कुर्यादैश्वर्यमास्थितः। पूर्वं चोत्तरकार्याणि न स वेद नयानयौ॥

vr.6.65.4.m: The truly brave do not put up with praising themselves. Without showing off, they do what is hard.
roles: Shows courage in the deed and not in the telling.
vr.6.65.4.sa: न मर्षयन्ति चात्मानं संभावयितुमात्मना। अदर्शयित्वा शूरास्तु कर्म कुर्वन्ति दुष्करम्॥

vr.7.40.10.m: Hearing the nectar of your deeds, hero, Lord, I will clear away my longing for you, as the wind scatters a bank of clouds.
roles: Arranges a life around hearing of Rama.
vr.7.40.10.sa: तच्छ्रुत्वाहं ततो वीर तव चर्यामृतं प्रभो। उत्कण्ठां तां हरिष्यामि मेघलेखामिवानलिः॥

vr.7.40.12.m: So it shall be, best of monkeys, without doubt. As long as my story is current in the world, your fame and your life will last. For each single service you have done me I would give my life, and for the rest we remain in your debt. May what you have done for me be digested within me; a person needs repaying only in times of trouble.
roles: Names a debt gladly left unpaid because paying it would need the friend's misfortune.
vr.7.40.12.sa: एवमेतत्कपिश्रेष्ठ भविता नात्र संशयः। चरिष्यति कथा यावदेषा लोके च मामिका॥ तावचे भविता कीर्तिः शरीरेऽप्यसवस्तथा। लोका हि यावत्स्थास्यन्ति तावत्स्थास्यन्ति मे कथाः।। एकैकस्योपकारस्य प्राणान्दास्यामि ते कये। शेषस्येहोपकाराणां भवाम ऋणिनो वयम्॥ मदङ्गे जीर्णतां यातु यत्त्वयोपकृतं कपे। नरः प्रत्युपकाराणामापत्स्वायाति पात्रताम्।।२४

vr.7.40.6.m: And my only request, king, is that you always remember me, and Sugriva, with great love. Go now, free from distress.
roles: Shows a parting that asks only to be remembered with love.
vr.7.40.6.sa: अहं च नित्यशो राजन्सुग्रीवसहितस्त्वया। स्मर्तव्यः परया प्रीत्या गच्छ त्वं विगतज्वरः॥

vr.7.49.10.m: Accept this welcome, trust me and let your fever of worry pass. Think of this as coming to your own home, and do not despair.
vr.7.49.10.sa: इदमऱ्या प्रतीच्छ त्वं विस्रब्धा विगतज्वरा। यथा स्वगृहमभ्येत्य विषादं चैव मा कृथाः॥ श्रुत्वा तु भाषितं सीता मुनेः परममद्भुतम्। शिरसा वन्द्य चरणौ तथेत्याह कृताञ्जलिः॥

vr.7.53.4.m: Four days now I have not attended to the people's business, gentle Lakshman, and it cuts me to the core.
roles: Depicts duty left undone while sunk in his own pain.
vr.7.53.4.sa: चत्वारो दिवसाः सौम्य कार्य पौरजनस्य च । अकुर्वाणस्य सौमित्रे तन्मे मर्माणि कृन्तति॥

vr.7.72.10.m: Be kind to me, Ram of boundless strength. I cannot go on living far away like a calf without its mother.
roles: Shows years of duty far from home, and he asks not to be sent away again.
vr.7.72.10.sa: स मे प्रसादं काकुत्स्थ कुरुष्वामितविक्रम। मातृहीनो यथा वत्सो न चिरं प्रवसाम्यहम्॥

vr.7.72.14.m: You are dearer to me than life itself, without doubt. But a kingdom must be looked after. So stay with me seven nights, and then go back to Madhura with your people.
roles: Duty is kept without denying the bond.
vr.7.72.14.sa: ममापि त्वं सुदयितः प्राणैरपि न संशयः। अवश्यं करणीयं च राज्यस्य परिपालनम्॥ तस्मात्त्वं वस काकुत्स्थ सप्तरात्रं मया सह। ऊवं गन्तासि मधुरां सभृत्यबलवाहनः॥

vr.7.83.15.m: The wise should not do anything that brings suffering to people. Good advice should be taken even from the young, elder brother of Lakshman; so I accept what you have said as right and fitting.
roles: Gives advice weighed by its merit, not the speaker's age.
vr.7.83.15.sa: लोकपीडाकरं कर्म न कर्तव्यं विचक्षणैः। बालानां तु शुभं वाक्यं ग्राह्यं लक्ष्मणपूर्वज। तस्माच्छृणोमि ते वाक्यं साधु युक्तं महाबल।।२०
